operations.specification: This operation allows guest users to register for a new member account on the discussion board. Registration is the first step for unauthenticated guests to become authenticated members with full content creation and interaction privileges. The operation collects essential registration information (username, email, password) and creates a new member account in pending_email_verification status. Upon successful registration, the system sends a verification email and returns JWT tokens for immediate authenticated access.
operations.name: join
operations.summary: Register a new member account from guest status
operations.description:
This endpoint enables guest users to create a new member account on the discussion board platform. Guests provide a unique username, valid email address, and secure password to register. The system validates the registration data, creates a new member account with pending_email_verification status, and sends a verification email to the provided address.

Upon successful registration, the operation immediately issues JWT access and refresh tokens, allowing the user to authenticate as a member. However, certain member privileges (such as posting articles and comments) may require email verification completion.

The registration process enforces username uniqueness (case-insensitive), email uniqueness (case-insensitive), and password strength requirements (minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character). Username must be 3-30 characters containing only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens.

This operation is public and requires no authentication. Any guest can attempt to register, subject to validation rules and rate limiting to prevent abuse.

After successful registration, the user receives an email with a verification link. Clicking this link transitions the account from pending_email_verification to active status, enabling full member capabilities.

responseBody.description: JWT authentication tokens (access and refresh) for the newly registered member account

operations.specification: This operation allows guest users to refresh their JWT access tokens using a valid refresh token. When an access token expires after 30 minutes, guests who have a valid refresh token can obtain a new access token without re-entering credentials. This enables seamless session continuation for browsing activities. The operation validates the provided refresh token and issues a new access token with updated expiration.
operations.name: refresh
operations.summary: Refresh JWT access token using a valid refresh token
operations.description:
This endpoint enables token refresh for guest sessions or registered users with valid refresh tokens. The refresh mechanism allows users to obtain a new access token when the current access token expires (30-minute lifespan) without requiring full re-authentication.

The operation accepts a valid refresh token (14-day lifespan) and validates its authenticity and expiration status. Upon successful validation, the system issues a new access token with a fresh 30-minute expiration period. The refresh token itself may optionally be rotated for enhanced security.

This operation is essential for maintaining seamless user experience during extended browsing sessions. Users don't need to repeatedly enter credentials as long as their refresh token remains valid.

The refresh token is typically stored securely (httpOnly cookie or secure storage) and transmitted with refresh requests. If the refresh token is expired, invalid, or revoked, the operation returns an authentication error, requiring the user to log in again with full credentials.

This endpoint is public but requires a valid refresh token in the request. Rate limiting prevents abuse and brute-force attacks on the refresh mechanism.

requestBody.description: Refresh token information for obtaining a new access token

responseBody.description: New JWT authentication tokens (access and optionally rotated refresh token)

operations.specification: This operation handles user registration (join) for new members. It creates a new member account with username, email, and password, sets the account to pending_email_verification status, generates an email verification token, and sends a verification email. This is the first step in the member authentication flow.
operations.name: join
operations.summary: Register a new member account and initiate email verification
operations.description:
This operation creates a new member account in the discussion board system. It accepts registration credentials including username, email, and password, validates them according to system requirements, and creates a new member record in the discussion_board_members table.

The registration process enforces username uniqueness (3-30 characters, alphanumeric with underscores and hyphens), email uniqueness and format validation, and password strength requirements (minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character). Upon successful account creation, the system sets the account status to pending_email_verification and email_verified to false.

A unique email verification token is generated and sent to the provided email address. The user must verify their email before they can log in and access member features. The verification token expires after 24 hours, after which the user can request a new verification email.

This operation implements the join authentication type, issuing initial JWT tokens (access and refresh) upon successful registration. The response includes the authenticated member information and tokens, allowing immediate session establishment after email verification.

Security considerations include protection against username enumeration attacks by providing generic error messages, rate limiting to prevent abuse, and secure password hashing (bcrypt or equivalent) before storage. The system never stores passwords in plain text.

responseBody.description: Authorized member session with JWT tokens for authentication

operations.specification: This operation handles member login authentication. It validates username/email and password credentials, verifies that the email has been verified, checks account status is active, and issues JWT access and refresh tokens for authenticated sessions.
operations.name: login
operations.summary: Authenticate member credentials and issue session tokens
operations.description:
This operation authenticates existing members using their credentials (username or email plus password) and establishes an authenticated session by issuing JWT tokens.

The login process validates that the provided username or email exists in the discussion_board_members table and that the password matches the stored password_hash using secure comparison. The system implements security measures including rate limiting after 5 failed attempts within 15 minutes, generic error messages to prevent username enumeration, and session tracking in discussion_board_member_sessions.

Before issuing tokens, the system verifies that email_verified is true and status is 'active'. If the email is unverified, the login is rejected with a message prompting email verification. If the account is suspended or deleted, appropriate error messages are returned.

Upon successful authentication, the system generates a new access token (30-minute expiration) and refresh token (14-day expiration), updates the last_login_at timestamp, creates a new record in discussion_board_member_sessions tracking the login IP, href, and referrer, and returns the authenticated member information along with the tokens.

The JWT access token payload includes user ID, role (member), username, email verification status, token issuance timestamp, and token expiration timestamp. The refresh token payload includes user ID, token family ID for rotation security, issuance timestamp, and expiration timestamp.

Security features include protection against brute force attacks through rate limiting, secure password comparison to prevent timing attacks, and comprehensive session logging for security auditing.

requestBody.description: Member login credentials with username or email and password

responseBody.description: Authorized member session with JWT tokens for authentication

operations.name: refresh
operations.summary: Refresh access token using valid refresh token
operations.description:
This operation enables members to obtain new access tokens when their current access token expires, without requiring full re-authentication with username and password. It implements secure token refresh using refresh tokens.

The refresh process validates that the provided refresh token is properly signed, not expired (14-day lifetime), and associated with an active member session in discussion_board_member_sessions. The system checks that the member account still exists, is not deleted (deleted_at is null), email remains verified (email_verified is true), and status is 'active'.

Upon successful validation, the system generates a new access token with 30-minute expiration and optionally rotates the refresh token by invalidating the old refresh token and issuing a new one. This rotation mechanism enhances security by limiting the window of vulnerability if a refresh token is compromised.

If the refresh token is expired, the system rejects the request and requires the user to log in again with credentials. If the member account has been suspended or deleted since the refresh token was issued, the token is invalidated and access is denied.

The response includes the new access token and optionally a new refresh token if rotation is implemented. The member information is included in the response for client state synchronization.

Security considerations include validating token signature integrity, checking token expiration before processing, verifying account status hasn't changed since token issuance, and implementing token rotation to limit exposure from compromised tokens.

responseBody.description: Authorized member session with new JWT tokens

operations.specification: This operation handles moderator account registration. New moderators create their accounts by providing username, email, and password. The system validates the input, creates a moderator account with pending_email_verification status, generates a verification token, and sends a verification email. Upon successful registration, the moderator receives JWT tokens (access and refresh) in the response. This is a public endpoint that does not require authentication.
operations.description:
This operation creates a new moderator account in the discussion board system.

The registration process begins when a user submits their desired username, email address, and password. The system validates that the username is unique, between 3-30 characters, and contains only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens. The email address must be valid format and unique across all moderator accounts. The password must meet security requirements: minimum 8 characters with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character.

Upon successful validation, the system creates a new moderator record in the discussion_board_moderators table with status set to pending_email_verification and email_verified set to false. The password is securely hashed using bcrypt or equivalent before storage. The system generates a unique email verification token valid for 24 hours and sends a verification email to the provided address.

The response includes JWT tokens (access token with 30-minute expiration and refresh token with 30-day expiration) allowing immediate authenticated access, though full moderator privileges require email verification. The system records the account creation timestamp and initializes default values for profile_visibility (public) and activity_visibility (public).

This endpoint is publicly accessible and does not require authentication, as it enables new moderators to create accounts. Rate limiting is applied to prevent abuse, restricting registration attempts from the same IP address.

Upon successful authentication, the system validates the credentials, checks email verification status, verifies the account is active, and issues JWT tokens for session management. operations.description:
This operation authenticates a moderator and establishes an authenticated session.

The login process accepts either username or email address along with the password. The system performs case-insensitive lookup for the username or email in the discussion_board_moderators table. If no matching account is found, the system returns a generic error message "Invalid username/email or password" without revealing which credential was incorrect, preventing username enumeration attacks.

When an account is found, the system verifies the provided password against the stored password_hash using secure comparison. If the password is incorrect, the same generic error message is returned. The system tracks failed login attempts and implements rate limiting: after 5 failed attempts within 15 minutes from the same IP address, login is temporarily blocked for 30 minutes.

Before issuing tokens, the system checks the email_verified field. If false, the login is rejected with message "Please verify your email address before logging in" and offers to resend the verification email. The system also validates that the account status is "active" - suspended or deleted accounts are denied access with appropriate error messages.

Upon successful authentication, the system generates a new access token (30-minute expiration) and refresh token (30-day expiration). The last_login_at timestamp is updated to the current time. A new session record is created in discussion_board_moderator_sessions capturing the IP address, user agent, and connection details for security auditing.

This is a public endpoint that does not require prior authentication. The response includes the complete moderator profile along with authentication tokens.

operations.description:
This operation enables token refresh for maintaining authenticated moderator sessions.

The refresh process is initiated when a client's access token expires but they have a valid refresh token. The system validates the provided refresh token by verifying its signature, checking expiration (30 days from issuance), and confirming it hasn't been invalidated or revoked. The refresh token contains the moderator's user ID which is used to retrieve the current account state.

The system performs several security checks before issuing new tokens. First, it verifies the moderator account still exists in the discussion_board_moderators table. Second, it checks the account status is "active" - suspended or deleted accounts cannot refresh tokens. Third, it validates the email_verified field is true, as unverified accounts should re-authenticate.

If any validation fails, the refresh is denied and the client must perform a full login. When validation succeeds, the system generates a new access token with 30-minute expiration and optionally rotates the refresh token for enhanced security (implementing refresh token rotation prevents token reuse if compromised).

The response includes the new access token and refresh token along with the moderator's current profile information, ensuring the client has up-to-date account data. The last_login_at timestamp is NOT updated during refresh operations as this is not a full login event.

This endpoint requires a valid refresh token but does not require an active access token (as the access token has expired). Session records in discussion_board_moderator_sessions are maintained across refresh operations.

It operates on the discussion_board_categories table, which provides the primary taxonomy structure for organizing economic and political discussion topics. The operation targets a specific category identified by its unique slug parameter. This is a hard delete operation that completely removes the category record from the database, as the schema does NOT include soft delete columns like deleted_at for categories. When a category is deleted, all associated article-category relationships in the discussion_board_article_categories junction table are automatically removed through cascade deletion, ensuring referential integrity. This operation should only be performed by moderators with appropriate permissions, and should be used carefully as it affects content organization across the entire platform.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a category from the discussion board system
operations.description:
This operation permanently removes a category from the discussion board's taxonomy structure, completely deleting the category record from the discussion_board_categories table. Categories serve as the primary organizational framework for economic and political discussion topics, providing structured browsing and content discovery for users.

When a category is deleted, the system performs a hard delete operation that completely removes the category record. The schema does NOT support soft deletion for categories as there is no deleted_at timestamp column. This means deletion is immediate and permanent. All associated relationships in the discussion_board_article_categories junction table are automatically removed through database cascade deletion constraints, ensuring that no orphaned references remain. Articles previously categorized under the deleted category will lose that categorization, though the articles themselves remain intact.

This operation is restricted to moderators only, as category management is a system-wide administrative function that affects content organization for all users. Moderators must exercise caution when deleting categories, as the action is irreversible. Before deletion, moderators should consider whether articles need to be recategorized, whether the category has historical significance, and whether deletion might disrupt ongoing discussions organized under that category. The operation should be logged as a moderation action for audit purposes, and moderators may want to notify the community when significant categories are removed from the taxonomy.

The category is identified by its unique slug parameter, which is matched against discussion_board_categories. This is a complex search operation supporting multiple filters including publication status, date ranges, view counts, comment counts, and keyword search across article titles and body content. operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated articles within a specific category
operations.description:
This operation provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for discovering articles within a specific discussion board category. Categories are the primary taxonomy for organizing economic and political discourse topics, and this endpoint enables users to explore all content within a particular subject area with advanced filtering, sorting, and pagination.

The operation performs a complex query joining the discussion_board_articles table with the discussion_board_article_categories junction table to identify articles belonging to the specified category (matched by slug from discussion_board_categories). The request body supports extensive filtering options including publication status (published, draft, archived), date range filters for article creation, author filtering, keyword search across both article titles and body content using PostgreSQL full-text search with trigram indexing, view count ranges, and comment count ranges. Results automatically exclude soft-deleted articles by filtering WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, ensuring only active content appears in search results.

The response returns paginated results using the IPageIDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary type, which contains both pagination metadata (total count, page number, page size, total pages) and an array of article summaries. The summary format provides essential information for list display including article ID, title, excerpt (first 200 characters of body or explicit summary field), author information (username, display name), category and tag information, view and comment counts, and publication timestamp. This optimized response format enables fast rendering of article lists without transferring full article bodies.

Sorting options allow users to organize results by creation date (newest or oldest first), view count (most viewed first), comment count (most discussed first), or last update timestamp (recently active first). The operation supports all user actor types with appropriate permission handling: guests can search published articles, members can search published articles plus their own drafts, and moderators can search all articles including those from suspended users for moderation purposes. Performance is optimized through database indexing on created_at, status, and trigram indexes on title and body columns, ensuring search results return within 2 seconds even with large article datasets.

Permanently removes a tag from the discussion board tag system using its URL-friendly slug identifier. This operation performs a hard delete, completely removing the tag record from the discussion_board_tags table and all associated article-tag relationships from the discussion_board_article_tags junction table.

This operation is designed for moderators who need to maintain the tag taxonomy by removing tags that are unused, inappropriate, misspelled, redundant, or violate community guidelines. When a tag is deleted, articles that were tagged with it remain fully functional and retain all other tags and categories, ensuring content integrity is preserved.

The deletion cascades automatically to all article-tag associations, meaning if a tag was applied to 100 articles, all 100 relationships are removed atomically with the tag deletion. This maintains referential integrity and prevents orphaned junction table records. Since the discussion_board_tags schema does not include a deleted_at column, this is a permanent deletion that cannot be recovered through the system - deleted tags must be manually recreated if needed again.

Security and authorization considerations are critical for this operation. Only users with moderator privileges can delete tags, as tag removal affects content organization across the entire platform and all users. The operation requires the moderator to be authenticated with a valid JWT token containing moderator role claims. Tag deletion should be logged in moderation action audit trails to maintain accountability for tag management decisions.

This operation works in coordination with the tag-based content discovery system specified in the Search and Discovery requirements. When a tag is deleted, any active user browsing or searching by that tag should receive appropriate feedback that the tag no longer exists, with suggestions to browse other related tags or categories.

operations.specification: This operation handles member registration by creating a new user account in the discussion_board_members table. It validates all registration input (username, email, password), creates the account with pending_email_verification status, generates an email verification token, and sends a verification email to the provided email address. The operation implements comprehensive validation rules including username uniqueness (validated against @@unique([username]) constraint), email uniqueness (validated against @@unique([email]) constraint), and password strength requirements as defined in the User Actors and Authentication requirements document. operations.summary: Register a new member account with email verification
operations.description:
This operation creates a new member account in the discussion board system, implementing the complete user registration workflow as defined in the User Actors and Authentication requirements. The operation accepts registration credentials including username, email, and password, performs comprehensive validation against business rules, and initializes the user account with pending email verification status.

The registration process enforces strict validation rules to ensure data integrity and security. Usernames must be unique across the system (enforced by @@unique([username]) constraint), between 3-30 characters, and contain only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens. Email addresses must be unique across the system (enforced by @@unique([email]) constraint) and follow standard email format validation. Passwords must meet complexity requirements including minimum 8 characters with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character. The system validates username and email uniqueness by checking existing records in discussion_board_members table before account creation.

Upon successful validation, the system creates a new account with status set to pending_email_verification, generates a unique email verification token with 24-hour expiration, and sends a verification email to the provided address. The account remains in pending status until email verification is completed through the verification link. The operation implements rate limiting and security measures including prevention of username enumeration, email address validation, and protection against common registration attacks. The response returns a summary of the created account excluding sensitive authentication data including password_hash and email verification token.

This operation serves as the entry point for new users joining the discussion board community, establishing their identity and credentials for future authentication. After successful registration, users must verify their email address before gaining full member privileges to create articles and post comments. The response type IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary MUST exclude password_hash, password-related fields, and other authentication-sensitive data to prevent security vulnerabilities.

The operation enables administrative and discovery features including member directory browsing, user search, and account management workflows. It implements mandatory three-tier privacy filtering based on requester authentication: guests see only members with profile_visibility = 'public', authenticated members see 'public' and 'members_only' profiles, and moderators see all profiles including 'private' ones. The response summary type MUST exclude password_hash and email addresses to protect privacy and security.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of discussion board members
operations.description:
This operation provides comprehensive search and retrieval capabilities for member accounts in the discussion board system. It enables users to discover other community members, search by username or display name, filter by account characteristics, and browse the member directory with pagination support. The operation implements flexible filtering and sorting to support various use cases from administrative user management to public member discovery.

The search functionality supports keyword matching against usernames, display_names, and bio content using trigram-based similarity search (leveraging GIN indexes on these fields) for fuzzy matching capabilities. Users can filter members by account status (active, suspended, pending_email_verification), profile visibility settings (public, members_only, private), date ranges for account creation, and activity metrics including article count and comment count thresholds. Advanced filtering options enable finding members who joined in specific time periods, have specific levels of contribution activity, or match certain profile characteristics. The operation leverages database indexes on status, created_at, email_verified, display_name, and bio fields for efficient query performance.

Security and privacy controls are integral to this operation and MANDATORY for implementation. The system enforces three-tier privacy filtering based on requester authentication status: (1) Guest users see ONLY members with profile_visibility = 'public', (2) Authenticated members see members with profile_visibility IN ('public', 'members_only'), and (3) Moderators see ALL members regardless of profile_visibility setting. The operation NEVER exposes sensitive information in responses - the IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary type MUST exclude password_hash, email addresses, password-related fields, and authentication tokens. Email addresses are visible ONLY to the account owner viewing their own profile or to moderators for legitimate moderation purposes, never in public or member-level search results.

Pagination is implemented with configurable page size (default 20 members per page, options for 10, 50, 100) and efficient offset-based or cursor-based navigation to handle large member bases. Sorting options include newest members first (by created_at DESC), alphabetical by username or display_name, most active by article or comment counts, and most recently logged in (by last_login_at DESC). The operation returns member summary information optimized for list displays including id, username, display_name, bio, profile_picture_url, location, website_url, profile_visibility, created_at, and derived counts for articles and comments. All returned data respects privacy settings and excludes authentication credentials and personally identifiable information not intended for public disclosure.

It operates on the discussion_board_members table and performs a complete account deletion including all associated data. The operation is accessible through the member's unique username parameter. This operation requires authentication and authorization - only the account owner can delete their own account (self-service deletion). The deletion process follows the account deletion workflow defined in the requirements, which includes confirmation requirements and data handling rules. When executed, this operation removes the member's personal data, handles their published content according to the content anonymization policy, deletes associated attachments, and cleans up all related records. This is a destructive operation that cannot be undone after the grace period expires.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a member account and associated personal data

Permanently deletes a member account from the discussion board system, removing all personal data in compliance with GDPR and privacy requirements. This operation implements the complete account deletion workflow as defined in the User Profiles and Settings requirements document, ensuring that all personally identifiable information is securely erased while handling published content according to the platform's content preservation policy.

The deletion process performs several critical actions: removes the member's email address, password hash, profile information (display name, bio, location, website), profile picture, privacy settings, notification preferences, login history, and activity history from the system. Published articles and comments are either anonymized (changing authorship to 'Deleted User') or completely removed based on the content policy configuration. All file attachments associated with deleted content are removed from storage. Active sessions are immediately terminated and all JWT refresh tokens are invalidated to prevent further access.

This operation requires the authenticated member to be deleting their own account - members cannot delete other members' accounts. The operation includes security measures such as requiring password confirmation in the request and may implement a grace period before permanent deletion as defined in the requirements. The deletion is atomic and transactional to ensure data consistency - if any part of the deletion fails, all changes are rolled back. Moderation logs that reference the deleted account are preserved for audit purposes but with personal data removed. This operation is irreversible after completion and represents a complete termination of the member's relationship with the discussion board platform.

It operates on the discussion_board_members table, specifically updating the password_hash field after validating the current password and applying password strength requirements. The operation is accessed through the member's unique username parameter and requires the authenticated member to be updating their own password (self-service password management). Password changes trigger security actions including invalidation of all existing JWT refresh tokens to force re-authentication across all devices and sessions. The operation follows the password management requirements defined in the User Actors and Authentication document and User Profiles and Settings document, enforcing password complexity rules and security best practices.
operations.summary: Update member account password with security verification
operations.description:
Updates the password for an authenticated member account, implementing comprehensive security measures to protect account integrity and user data. This operation follows the password change workflow defined in the User Profiles and Settings requirements, requiring verification of the current password before allowing the new password to be set, thus preventing unauthorized password changes even if an attacker gains temporary session access.

The password update process enforces strict password strength requirements: minimum 8 characters in length, must contain at least one uppercase letter (A-Z), at least one lowercase letter (a-z), at least one numeric digit (0-9), and at least one special character from the set (!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>?). The new password must differ from the current password to prevent users from rotating back to the same password. The operation validates the new password against common password breach databases to prevent use of compromised passwords. Password strength is calculated and users are encouraged to choose strong passwords, though medium-strength passwords meeting the minimum requirements are accepted.

When a password change completes successfully, the system performs critical security actions: updates the password_hash field in the discussion_board_members table using secure hashing (bcrypt or equivalent), invalidates all existing JWT refresh tokens across all devices and sessions to force re-authentication, issues a new refresh token for the current session to maintain the user's login state, and sends a confirmation email to the registered email address notifying the member of the password change with instructions for reporting unauthorized changes. The operation maintains comprehensive security event logging, recording the password change timestamp, IP address, and session information for security auditing. This operation is essential for account security, enabling members to maintain control of their accounts and respond to potential security threats.

It operates on the discussion_board_moderators table from the Prisma schema, allowing modification of profile fields including display_name, bio, location, website_url, profile_picture_url, email, and moderation_permissions. The operation validates input against the same rules as moderator account creation and requires the moderator to be authenticated and either updating their own profile or having appropriate administrative privileges.
operations.summary: Update moderator profile and account information in discussion_board_moderators table
operations.description:
Updates an existing moderator's profile information and account settings within the discussion board system. This operation enables moderators to maintain their profile data including display name, biography, location, website URL, and profile picture. Additionally, it supports updating email addresses (with verification requirements) and moderation permission settings for administrative purposes.

The operation validates all input fields according to the business rules defined in the requirements. Display names are limited to 50 characters, biographies to 500 characters, and locations to 100 characters. Website URLs must be properly formatted HTTP/HTTPS addresses. Email changes trigger a verification workflow to confirm ownership of the new address. Profile pictures must reference valid image URLs.

This operation requires authentication and proper authorization. Moderators can update their own profiles at any time. Administrative users with elevated privileges can update other moderators' profiles and permission settings. The system validates that the moderator account exists and is not deleted before applying updates. All changes are recorded with updated_at timestamps for audit purposes.

requestBody.description: Updated moderator profile information including optional display name, bio, location, website, profile picture, email, and moderation permissions

operations.specification: This operation performs soft deletion of a moderator account by setting the deleted_at timestamp in the discussion_board_moderators table. The operation marks the moderator account as deleted while preserving the record for audit purposes and referential integrity with related entities such as moderation actions, warnings, and suspensions. After soft deletion, the moderator cannot log in or perform moderation actions, but their historical contributions and moderation records remain accessible for system accountability.
operations.summary: Soft delete moderator account in discussion_board_moderators table
operations.description:
Performs a soft deletion of a moderator account by setting the deleted_at timestamp, effectively deactivating the account while preserving all historical data and audit trails. This operation is critical for maintaining system accountability as it ensures that all moderation actions, user warnings, suspensions, and content modifications performed by this moderator remain traceable in the system logs.

When a moderator account is soft deleted, the system immediately invalidates all active sessions for that moderator, preventing any further access. The moderator's profile becomes inaccessible for login, but their username and profile information remain in the database to support foreign key relationships with articles, comments, moderation actions, and other entities they have interacted with.

This operation requires careful consideration of system integrity. If the moderator being deleted is the only active moderator in the system, the operation should be prevented to ensure continuous moderation capabilities. Additionally, all related entities such as moderation_actions, user_warnings, and user_suspensions maintain their references to the deleted moderator for complete audit trail preservation. The soft deletion approach aligns with GDPR compliance by allowing personal data removal while maintaining necessary audit records for legal and accountability purposes.

parameters.name: moderatorUsername
parameters.description: Unique business identifier username of the target moderator to be deleted (global scope)

responseBody.description: Soft-deleted moderator account information with deleted_at timestamp set, confirming successful deactivation

operations.specification: This operation allows a moderator to change their own account password. It operates on the discussion_board_moderators table and requires the moderator to authenticate their current password before setting a new one. The operation validates password strength requirements (minimum 8 characters, at least one letter and one number) and updates the password_hash field. Upon successful password update, all existing sessions in discussion_board_moderator_sessions are marked as expired by setting expired_at to the current timestamp, requiring re-authentication on all devices.
operations.summary: Update moderator account password with current password verification
operations.description:
This operation enables authenticated moderators to change their account password by providing their current password for verification and submitting a new password that meets security requirements. The password change process is a critical security operation that ensures only the legitimate account owner can modify authentication credentials.

The operation validates that the current password matches the stored password_hash in the discussion_board_moderators table before accepting the new password. The new password must meet complexity requirements including minimum 8 characters length, at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character. Password strength is validated server-side to prevent weak passwords that could compromise account security.

Upon successful password update, the system marks all existing moderator sessions as expired by setting the expired_at timestamp to the current time in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table. This ensures the moderator must re-authenticate on all devices with the new password, providing security in case the password change was prompted by suspected account compromise. The system updates the password_hash field and the updated_at timestamp in the discussion_board_moderators table.

Security measures implemented include requiring current password verification to prevent unauthorized changes, enforcing strong password complexity requirements to resist brute force attacks, expiring all active sessions to invalidate potentially compromised access, and logging the password change event for security audit trails. Note that JWT refresh token management (if implemented) is handled at the application layer outside the database schema.

responseBody.description: Updated moderator profile information (excluding password_hash)

operations.specification: This operation handles new user registration for the discussion board system. It creates a new member account in the discussion_board_members table with status 'pending_email_verification' and email_verified set to false. Validation rules: Username must be 3-30 characters, alphanumeric plus underscores and hyphens only, must be unique (case-insensitive check). Email must be valid format per RFC 5322, must be unique (case-insensitive check). Password must be minimum 8 characters, must contain at least one uppercase letter (A-Z), one lowercase letter (a-z), one digit (0-9), and one special character. The operation sets default values: role 'member', profile_visibility 'public', activity_visibility 'public', email_verified false, status 'pending_email_verification'. Email verification workflow (token generation and validation) is handled by the application layer using signed JWT tokens containing user ID and expiration, with verification processed through a separate endpoint.
operations.summary: Register a new member account with email verification workflow
operations.description:
This operation enables new users to create member accounts on the discussion board platform, allowing them to participate in economic and political discussions by creating articles and posting comments. Registration is the entry point for converting guest visitors into active community members.

The registration process collects essential account information including a unique username (3-30 characters, alphanumeric with underscores and hyphens), a valid email address, and a secure password meeting complexity requirements (minimum 8 characters with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character). The system validates username and email uniqueness against existing accounts in the discussion_board_members table using case-insensitive comparison, rejecting duplicates with clear error messages.

Upon successful validation and account creation, the system creates a new record in discussion_board_members with email_verified set to false and status set to 'pending_email_verification'. The account is assigned default values including role 'member', profile_visibility 'public', and activity_visibility 'public'. The password is securely hashed before storage in the password_hash field, never stored in plain text. Account creation timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are set automatically.

Email verification is handled at the application layer using cryptographically signed JWT tokens that contain the user ID and expiration timestamp. The verification token is sent via email with a link that, when clicked, is validated by a separate verification endpoint. This email verification step prevents fraudulent registrations and ensures users have access to their registered email for future account recovery and notifications. The verification process updates email_verified to true and status to 'active' when successfully completed.

Security measures implemented include username and email uniqueness validation to prevent account conflicts, secure password hashing using industry-standard algorithms, email verification to confirm account ownership, input sanitization to prevent injection attacks, and validation against reserved usernames (admin, moderator, system, anonymous). Rate limiting should be applied to prevent automated registration abuse.

requestBody.description: Registration information including username, email, and password

responseBody.description: Registration confirmation with newly created member account information (excluding password_hash) and verification instructions

operations.name: register

operations.specification: This operation authenticates a user (either member or moderator) by validating their credentials and issuing JWT access and refresh tokens for session management. It operates on the discussion_board_members and discussion_board_moderators tables, validating the provided username/email and password against stored password hashes. Upon successful authentication, the system creates a new session record in the corresponding session table (discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions) and returns JWT tokens with appropriate claims including user ID, role, username, and email verification status. The operation supports authentication for both member and moderator user actors, determining the appropriate user type based on the credentials provided.
operations.summary: Authenticate user credentials and issue JWT access and refresh tokens
operations.description:
Authenticate a user (member or moderator) by validating their username or email address along with their password against the stored credentials in the discussion_board_members or discussion_board_moderators tables. This operation serves as the primary entry point for users to access authenticated features of the discussion board system.

The authentication process validates that the provided credentials match an existing account with a verified email address and active status. The system checks the password against the securely stored password_hash using industry-standard hashing algorithms. If authentication succeeds, the system generates two JWT tokens: a short-lived access token (30-minute expiration) for API requests and a longer-lived refresh token (30-day expiration) for obtaining new access tokens without re-entering credentials.

Security measures include rate limiting after 5 failed login attempts within 15 minutes from the same IP address, prevention of login for accounts with unverified email addresses (email_verified must be true), and denial of access for suspended or deleted accounts (status must be 'active'). The operation creates a session record in either discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions tracking the login event with IP address, connection URL, and referrer information for comprehensive security auditing.

The JWT access token payload includes user ID, user role (member or moderator), username, email verification status, and token issuance/expiration timestamps for comprehensive session management and role-based access control throughout the system. This operation enables all authenticated functionality including article creation, comment posting, profile management, and moderation actions.

requestBody.description: User credentials including username or email and password for authentication validation

responseBody.description: Authentication result containing JWT access token, refresh token, user identity information, and role designation

operations.name: login

operations.specification: This operation terminates the current member user session by invalidating the refresh token and ending authenticated access. It operates on the discussion_board_member_sessions table, setting the expired_at timestamp for the current session record to mark it as ended. The operation identifies the session to terminate based on the authenticated member's JWT access token, which contains the member ID. Upon successful logout, the system prevents the refresh token from being used to obtain new access tokens, effectively requiring fresh authentication for future access to member-protected features.
operations.summary: Terminate current member session and invalidate authentication tokens
operations.description:
Terminate the currently authenticated member session by invalidating the refresh token and recording the session end time in the discussion_board_member_sessions table. This operation enables members to securely end their authenticated session, preventing further use of the current refresh token to obtain new access tokens.

The logout process marks the current session as expired by setting the expired_at timestamp to the current time, creating a complete audit trail of session duration and member activity. The operation extracts the member's identity and current session information from the JWT access token, eliminating the need for request body parameters. After successful logout, the client must discard both the access token and refresh token from local storage to complete the logout process.

This operation is particularly important for security when members access the system from shared or public devices, as it ensures that sessions are properly terminated rather than remaining active until the 30-day refresh token expiration. The logout action only affects the current device's session - members can remain logged in on other devices if they have multiple active sessions across different browsers or devices. When a member changes their password, all sessions across all devices are invalidated automatically through a separate mechanism, but manual logout only terminates the specific session from which it was initiated.

The operation requires a valid member access token to identify the session to be terminated. No request body is needed as all session information is derived from the authentication token. The response confirms successful logout, after which the member must authenticate again using the login operation to regain access to protected member features such as article creation and comment posting.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful member session termination

operations.name: logout

operations.specification: This operation terminates the current moderator user session by invalidating the refresh token and ending authenticated access. It operates on the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table, setting the expired_at timestamp for the current session record to mark it as ended. The operation identifies the session to terminate based on the authenticated moderator's JWT access token, which contains the moderator ID. Upon successful logout, the system prevents the refresh token from being used to obtain new access tokens, effectively requiring fresh authentication for future access to moderator-protected features.
operations.summary: Terminate current moderator session and invalidate authentication tokens

Terminate the currently authenticated moderator session by invalidating the refresh token and recording the session end time in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table. This operation enables moderators to securely end their authenticated session, preventing further use of the current refresh token to obtain new access tokens.

The logout process marks the current session as expired by setting the expired_at timestamp to the current time, creating a complete audit trail of session duration and moderator activity. The operation extracts the moderator's identity and current session information from the JWT access token, eliminating the need for request body parameters. After successful logout, the client must discard both the access token and refresh token from local storage to complete the logout process.

This operation is particularly important for security when moderators access the system from shared or public devices, as it ensures that sessions are properly terminated rather than remaining active until the 30-day refresh token expiration. The logout action only affects the current device's session - moderators can remain logged in on other devices if they have multiple active sessions across different browsers or devices. When a moderator changes their password, all sessions across all devices are invalidated automatically through a separate mechanism, but manual logout only terminates the specific session from which it was initiated.

The operation requires a valid moderator access token to identify the session to be terminated. No request body is needed as all session information is derived from the authentication token. The response confirms successful logout, after which the moderator must authenticate again using the login operation to regain access to protected moderator features such as content moderation and user management.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful moderator session termination

operations.name: logout

prerequisites.description: Moderator must be logged in with an active session before they can log out. The logout operation requires a valid JWT access token containing session information to identify which session to terminate.

operations.specification: This operation refreshes the user's authentication tokens by validating the current session and issuing new access tokens. It operates on the session tables (discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions) in the Prisma schema, checking session validity through the session ID, created_at, and expired_at fields. The operation allows authenticated users to obtain new JWT access tokens without re-entering credentials, supporting seamless session continuation. The operation validates the provided session identifier, checks the session has not expired, verifies the associated user account is active, and generates a fresh access token with appropriate expiration time (30 minutes for access token).
operations.summary: Refresh authentication tokens for active user sessions
operations.description:
Refresh the user's authentication tokens to maintain an active session without requiring re-authentication. This operation is essential for providing a seamless user experience by allowing users to continue their session when the access token expires.

The operation validates the current session by checking the session record in the database (discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions tables). Upon successful validation, the system generates a new access token valid for 30 minutes. The operation checks that the session has not expired by comparing the current time against the session's expired_at field, and verifies the user account is in an active state (not suspended, banned, or deleted).

Security considerations include validating that the user account status is active (checking the status field in discussion_board_members or discussion_board_moderators table), ensuring the session has not been explicitly expired, and verifying the session belongs to the requesting user. The operation maintains the security integrity of the authentication system by checking session validity through the expired_at timestamp field and user account status field.

This operation is critical for maintaining user sessions across device usage patterns and supports the JWT-based authentication architecture defined in the user actors and authentication requirements. It works with both member and moderator sessions, respecting the different session tracking tables for each actor type.

requestBody.description: Session identifier to validate and exchange for new access token

responseBody.description: New access token for continued authenticated access

operations.name: refresh

prerequisites.description: User must have previously logged in to obtain a refresh token. The refresh operation validates and exchanges an existing refresh token from a login session for a new access token.

operations.specification: This operation verifies a user's email address by validating a verification token provided through application logic and updating the email_verified field and status in the Prisma schema. It operates on the discussion_board_members or discussion_board_moderators tables, changing the email_verified field from false to true and transitioning the account status from pending_email_verification to active. The operation enables account activation by confirming email ownership, which is a mandatory step before users can create articles, post comments, or fully participate in the discussion board. Token validation occurs through application logic using a secure token service or cache layer, with the database update only modifying the email_verified and status fields upon successful token verification.
operations.summary: Verify user email address using verification token from registration email
operations.description:
Verify a user's email address to activate their account and enable full platform access. This operation is a critical step in the user registration workflow, confirming that the provided email address is valid and accessible by the user.

The operation validates an email verification token sent to the user's email address during registration. Token validation is handled through application logic with a secure token service or cache layer (such as Redis), as the Prisma schema tables do not store verification tokens directly. Tokens are unique, cryptographically secure, and time-limited to 24 hours for security. Upon receiving a valid token, the system updates the database by setting the email_verified field to true and transitions the account status from pending_email_verification to active in the discussion_board_members or discussion_board_moderators table.

Security considerations include validating token authenticity through the application's token service, checking token expiration (24-hour validity window), ensuring the token has not been used previously, and verifying the associated account exists and is in pending_email_verification status by querying the status field. If the token is expired, the system provides appropriate error messaging and allows users to request a new verification email.

This operation works with both member and moderator accounts, as both user types require email verification before gaining full platform access. Successful email verification is a prerequisite for logging in and performing any authenticated actions such as creating articles, posting comments, or accessing moderation tools. The operation follows the authentication requirements specified in the user actors and authentication documentation, ensuring only verified users can fully participate in the discussion board by updating the email_verified and status fields in the Prisma schema.

requestBody.description: Email verification token received in the verification email during registration

responseBody.description: Verification result with account activation status and authentication tokens for immediate login

operations.name: verify

prerequisites.description: Member account must be created with pending_email_verification status before email can be verified

operations.specification: This operation initiates the password recovery process for users who have forgotten their password. It operates on the discussion_board_members table by looking up the user account associated with the provided email address and generating a secure password reset token with a 2-hour expiration. The operation creates a password reset request record and sends an email containing a unique reset link to the user's registered email address. This is the first step in the two-step password reset flow, followed by the password reset confirmation operation. The operation implements security measures including rate limiting to prevent abuse and email enumeration protection by returning the same success message regardless of whether the email exists in the system.
operations.summary: Request password reset for forgotten password recovery
operations.description:
Initiates the password recovery process for users who have forgotten their password and need to reset it. This operation allows users to request a password reset by providing their registered email address, triggering the system to send a password reset email with a secure reset link.

When a user submits a password reset request, the system validates the email format and checks if an account exists with that email address. For security reasons, the system returns the same success message regardless of whether the email exists in the database, preventing email enumeration attacks where malicious actors could determine which email addresses are registered in the system.

If an account exists with the provided email, the system generates a unique password reset token with a 2-hour expiration and sends an email to the user containing a password reset link. The reset email includes the token, expiration notice, security notice that if the user didn't request this they can ignore the email, and instructions if the link doesn't work. The reset token is single-use and cryptographically secure, ensuring that only the legitimate account owner can reset the password.

This operation implements rate limiting to prevent abuse, limiting password reset requests to once every 5 minutes per email address. If a user attempts to request multiple resets within the rate limit window, the system returns an error indicating they must wait before requesting another reset.

The operation is accessible to all users including guests, members, and moderators, as password recovery is a pre-authentication function. This operation must be followed by the password reset confirmation operation (POST /auth/password-reset/confirm) to complete the password reset process. The relationship between these two operations is critical: this operation generates the reset token and sends it via email, while the confirmation operation validates the token and actually updates the password.

requestBody.description: Password reset request containing the email address of the account to recover

responseBody.description: Generic success message indicating reset instructions were sent if account exists

operations.name: request

prerequisites.description: Member account must exist with a registered email address before password reset can be requested

operations.specification: This operation completes the password reset process by validating the reset token and updating the user's password. It operates on the discussion_board_members table by locating the user account associated with the provided reset token, validating the token is not expired and has not been used, verifying the new password meets security requirements, updating the password_hash field with the new securely hashed password, and invalidating all existing user sessions to force re-authentication. The operation marks the reset token as used to prevent reuse and sends a confirmation email to notify the user of the password change. This is the second step in the two-step password reset flow, following the password reset request operation that generates and sends the reset token.
operations.summary: Complete password reset with token validation and new password
operations.description:
Completes the password reset process by validating the reset token received via email and setting a new password for the user account. This operation is the second step in the password recovery flow, following the password reset request operation that generated and sent the reset token.

When a user clicks the password reset link in their email and submits a new password, this operation validates several critical security requirements. First, it verifies that the reset token is valid, has not expired (tokens expire after 2 hours), and has not been previously used. If the token is expired, invalid, or already used, the system rejects the request and displays an error message prompting the user to request a new password reset.

The operation validates that the new password meets all complexity requirements including minimum 8 characters length, at least one uppercase letter, at least one lowercase letter, at least one number, and at least one special character. The system also checks that the new password is not identical to common compromised passwords from known breach databases. If the new password fails any validation requirement, the system provides specific feedback indicating which requirements are not met.

When all validation passes, the system securely hashes the new password using bcrypt or Argon2 and updates the password_hash field in the discussion_board_members table. Immediately after the password is updated, the system invalidates all existing refresh tokens and active sessions for that user account, forcing the user to log in again from all devices with the new password. This security measure ensures that if an unauthorized party had gained access to the account, they are immediately logged out when the legitimate owner resets the password.

Upon successful password reset, the system sends a confirmation email to the user's registered email address notifying them that their password was changed, including the timestamp of the change and instructions for what to do if the change was unauthorized. The reset token is permanently invalidated to prevent reuse, and the user is redirected to the login page with a success message prompting them to log in with their new password.

This operation is accessible to all users including guests since it is part of the pre-authentication password recovery flow. The operation provides critical account security functionality, enabling users to regain access to their accounts when they forget their password while maintaining strong security controls to prevent unauthorized password changes.

requestBody.description: Password reset confirmation containing the reset token and new password

responseBody.description: Confirmation message indicating password was successfully reset

operations.name: confirm

prerequisites.description: Password reset token must be generated and sent via email before it can be used to confirm password reset

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated list of published articles from the discussion_board_articles table with advanced filtering, searching, and sorting capabilities. It supports complex queries to find articles based on various criteria including title keywords, body content search, author filtering, category filtering, tag filtering, publication date ranges, and view/comment count thresholds. This operation operates on the discussion_board_articles Prisma table and provides comprehensive search functionality for content discovery in the economic and political discussion board.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of discussion board articles
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of articles from the discussion board system. This operation provides advanced search capabilities for discovering economic and political discussion content based on multiple criteria including keyword search across titles and body content, author filtering, category and tag-based filtering, publication date ranges, and engagement metrics.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and multiple sorting options. Users can sort articles by publication date (newest or oldest first), view count (most viewed), comment count (most discussed), or last update time (recently active discussions). This enables users to discover content in ways that match their interests and browsing patterns.

Security and performance considerations include rate limiting for search operations to prevent abuse, optimized database queries with proper indexing on search fields, and appropriate filtering of soft-deleted articles (where deleted_at is not null) to exclude them from results. The operation respects article visibility rules, returning only published articles (status = 'published') to regular users while potentially allowing moderators to search across all statuses.

This operation integrates with the discussion_board_articles table as defined in the Prisma schema, incorporating fields such as title, body, discussion_board_member_id (author), status, view_count, comment_count, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. The response includes article summary information optimized for list displays, with options to include author details, category names, tag lists, and engagement metrics based on the request parameters.

Related operations that work together with this search include the article detail retrieval endpoint (GET /articles/{articleId}) for viewing full article content after finding relevant articles through search, and the article creation endpoint (POST /articles) for members who want to contribute new content after browsing existing discussions.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filtering parameters, sorting options, and pagination configuration for article discovery

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of article summaries matching the search criteria with metadata

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation creates a new article in the discussion_board_articles table for authenticated members to publish economic and political discussion content. The article creation includes validation of required fields (title, body, category), optional metadata (summary, tags), and support for attaching multiple image and document files. The operation enforces business rules including title length (5-200 characters), body length (20-50000 characters), category requirement, tag limits (maximum 5 tags), and attachment limits (maximum 10 images and 5 documents). Upon successful creation, the article is published with status 'published', view_count and comment_count initialized to 0, and the authenticated member set as the author in the discussion_board_member_id field.
operations.summary: Create and publish a new discussion board article as a member
operations.description:
Create a new article in the discussion board system for sharing economic and political analysis, commentary, and discussions. This operation allows authenticated members to publish content with rich text formatting, categorization, tagging, and multimedia attachments including images and documents.

The article creation process validates all required fields according to business rules defined in the requirements. The title must be between 5 and 200 characters, providing enough space for descriptive headlines while preventing excessive length. The body content must be between 20 and 50,000 characters, ensuring substantive content while preventing abuse. The system requires selection of at least one category from predefined economic and political topic categories (stored in discussion_board_categories), and supports up to 5 optional tags (from discussion_board_tags) for enhanced discoverability.

Attachment support enables evidence-based discussions by allowing members to upload supporting materials. Articles can include up to 10 image attachments (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP formats, maximum 5MB each) for charts, graphs, infographics, and visual evidence, as well as up to 5 document attachments (PDF, DOCX, DOC, TXT, RTF, ODT formats, maximum 10MB each) for research papers, policy documents, and supplementary materials. The total attachment size across all files is limited to 50MB per article to balance functionality with storage and performance considerations.

Upon successful creation, the system sets the article status to 'published', initializes view_count and comment_count to 0, assigns the authenticated member as the author in the discussion_board_member_id field, and records the creation timestamp. The operation returns the complete article entity including the system-generated article ID, allowing the client to navigate to the newly published article.

Security and data integrity measures include authentication verification to ensure only logged-in members can create articles, input sanitization to prevent XSS attacks while preserving formatting, validation of category and tag references against the discussion_board_categories and discussion_board_tags tables, file upload validation including type checking, size limits, and malware scanning, and rate limiting to prevent spam or automated article creation abuse.

This operation integrates with multiple system components including the user authentication system to verify member identity, the file storage system to handle image and document uploads (discussion_board_article_images and discussion_board_article_documents tables), the category and tag systems for content organization (discussion_board_article_categories and discussion_board_article_tags junction tables), and the snapshot system which creates an initial version record in discussion_board_article_snapshots for audit trail purposes.

Related operations include the article search endpoint (PATCH /articles) for discovering existing content before posting to avoid duplicates, the article detail endpoint (GET /articles/{articleId}) for viewing the newly published article, and the article update endpoint (PUT /articles/{articleId}) for editing the article after publication if corrections are needed.

requestBody.description: Article creation data including title, body content, category, optional tags, optional summary, and attachment references

responseBody.description: Complete article entity with generated ID, timestamps, initial counts, and all submitted content

This operation integrates with multiple system components including the user authentication system to verify moderator identity, the file storage system to handle image and document uploads (discussion_board_article_images and discussion_board_article_documents tables), the category and tag systems for content organization (discussion_board_article_categories and discussion_board_article_tags junction tables), the snapshot system which creates an initial version record in discussion_board_article_snapshots for audit trail purposes, and the moderation system which may log this action in discussion_board_moderation_actions for oversight.

operations.summary: Update an existing article with new content and metadata
operations.description:
Update the content and metadata of an existing article in the discussion board system. This operation allows article authors to modify their published articles by updating the title, body content, summary, publication status, associated categories, tags, and managing image and document attachments. The operation enforces strict ownership validation ensuring that only the original author (identified by discussion_board_member_id) can update their own articles, unless the requesting user is a moderator who possesses elevated permissions to edit any article regardless of authorship.

The update process validates all input fields according to the business rules defined in the requirements. Article titles must be between 5 and 200 characters, body content must be between 20 and 50,000 characters, summaries are optional with a maximum of 500 characters, and up to 5 tags can be applied with each tag being 2-30 characters. The system validates that selected categories exist in the discussion_board_categories table and that tags conform to the normalized lowercase format defined in the discussion_board_tags table.

When a member successfully updates their article, the system creates a new record in the discussion_board_article_snapshots table to preserve the previous version for version control and audit purposes. This snapshot includes the complete article state before the update including title, body, summary, and status fields along with a timestamp marking when this version existed. The created_by_member_id in the snapshot references the member who made the update.

Attachment management during article updates supports adding new images and documents up to the defined limits (10 images maximum, 5 documents maximum, with individual file size limits of 5MB for images and 10MB for documents). When attachments are removed during an edit, the system marks the corresponding records in discussion_board_article_images or discussion_board_article_documents with a deleted_at timestamp following the soft deletion pattern. The system enforces total attachment limits including both existing and newly added files.

The operation automatically updates the updated_at timestamp to the current time, preserving the original created_at timestamp as an immutable historical record. If a moderator performs the update, the last_modified_by_moderator_id field is set to the moderator's ID to track moderator intervention in the content. The view_count and comment_count fields are not modified by this operation as they are system-managed metrics updated through separate processes.

This endpoint respects the soft deletion mechanism in the schema. If the article has a non-null deleted_at timestamp, the article is considered deleted and the update operation returns a 404 Not Found error. Only active articles (deleted_at is null) can be updated through this endpoint.
