operations.specification: This operation performs a soft delete on a specific article in the discussion board system by setting the deleted_at timestamp in the discussion_board_articles table. The article record is preserved in the database for audit trail and potential recovery purposes, but is hidden from public view. When an article is soft deleted, the system should also handle associated data appropriately: comments may be soft deleted by setting their deleted_at timestamps, article snapshots are retained as historical records, article-category and article-tag junction table entries may be removed or retained based on implementation strategy, and image and document attachments may be soft deleted by setting their deleted_at fields. This operation is identified by the article's unique UUID identifier passed as a path parameter. The soft deletion can be performed either by the article's original author (discussion_board_member_id) or by any moderator, with appropriate permission checks enforced at the business logic level.
operations.summary: Mark an article as deleted while preserving it for audit and potential recovery
operations.description:
This operation marks an article as deleted in the discussion board system by setting the deleted_at timestamp, while preserving all article data and relationships in the database for audit trail purposes and potential recovery. This follows the soft delete pattern defined in the Prisma schema for the discussion_board_articles table.

When an article is soft deleted, the system sets the deleted_at field to the current timestamp. This timestamp acts as a marker that the article has been deleted, causing it to be filtered out from public article listings, search results, and normal browsing interfaces. However, the complete article record remains in the database with all its content, metadata, and relationships intact. This preservation is essential for maintaining discussion context, enabling content recovery if deletion was accidental or incorrect, supporting moderation audit trails, and complying with data retention requirements.

The soft deletion process affects related data in a coordinated manner. Comments posted on the article (discussion_board_comments) are typically also soft deleted by setting their deleted_at timestamps, hiding the entire discussion thread from public view while preserving it for audit purposes. Historical article snapshots (discussion_board_article_snapshots) are retained unchanged since they represent historical versions and serve as permanent audit records. Category associations (discussion_board_article_categories) and tag associations (discussion_board_article_tags) may be removed or retained based on implementation strategy. Image attachments (discussion_board_article_images) and document attachments (discussion_board_article_documents) are typically soft deleted by setting their deleted_at fields, hiding them from public access while preserving file metadata and enabling potential restoration.

From a security and permissions perspective, this operation can be performed by two types of users. The original article author (identified by discussion_board_member_id in the article record) has the right to delete their own articles at any time after publication. Additionally, any moderator has the authority to delete any article regardless of authorship as part of content moderation responsibilities. The system enforces these permissions by verifying either ownership match or moderator role before allowing the deletion to proceed. When a moderator deletes another user's article, the action should be logged in the discussion_board_moderation_actions table with action_type set to delete_content, creating a complete audit trail of the moderation intervention.

This operation supports content recovery and audit capabilities. Because soft deleted articles remain in the database with all their data intact, moderators or the original author can potentially restore the article by clearing or nullifying the deleted_at timestamp. The article and all its associated content can be brought back to public visibility if the deletion was performed in error or if review determines the content does not violate guidelines. This recovery capability is a key advantage of soft deletion over hard deletion. Users should still be prompted for confirmation before deletion is executed to prevent accidental deletions, even though soft deletion is reversible.

operations.specification: This operation allows authenticated members to upload and attach image files to an existing article in the discussion board system. It operates on the discussion_board_article_images table, creating new image attachment records associated with the specified article. The operation accepts a request body containing image upload information including the image file data (represented as a URI string), original filename, MIME type, dimensions, and file size. The system validates that the uploaded image meets all requirements defined in the file storage specifications: supported formats (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP), maximum individual file size (5MB), valid dimensions (minimum 50x50 pixels, maximum 8000x8000 pixels), and adherence to the total attachment limit (maximum 10 images per article). The operation is identified by the article's UUID passed as a path parameter. Upon successful upload, the system stores the image file, generates a unique stored filename to prevent conflicts, records metadata in the discussion_board_article_images table, and associates the image with the parent article. The uploaded_by_member_id is automatically captured from the authenticated user context.
operations.summary: Upload and attach image files to an existing article
operations.description:
This operation enables authenticated members to enhance their articles by uploading image attachments such as charts, graphs, infographics, or photographs that support their economic or political analysis. Images serve as visual evidence and help readers better understand complex concepts discussed in the article text.

The image upload process begins when a member submits image data along with metadata. The system performs comprehensive validation before accepting the upload. File type validation ensures the image is in one of the supported formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP. The system validates the MIME type matches the file content, not just the file extension, preventing users from bypassing restrictions by renaming files. File size validation confirms the image does not exceed the 5MB limit for individual images. Dimension validation checks that the image is at least 50x50 pixels (minimum readable size) and does not exceed 8000x8000 pixels (maximum practical size). The system also verifies that adding this image will not cause the article to exceed the maximum of 10 total image attachments.

When all validations pass, the system proceeds with the upload process. The image file is stored in the file storage system with a unique generated filename (stored_name) to prevent filename conflicts while preserving the original user-provided filename (original_name) for display purposes. The system records comprehensive metadata in the discussion_board_article_images table including the parent article reference (discussion_board_article_id), the uploader's member ID (uploaded_by_member_id) captured from the authenticated session, original and stored filenames, MIME type, file size in bytes, image dimensions (width and height), and the upload timestamp (created_at). The uploaded_by_member_id field is particularly important for tracking who added each attachment and enforcing permission rules for attachment management.

From a security and permissions perspective, this operation is restricted to authenticated members and moderators. The article author can add images to their own article, and moderators can add images to any article as part of content management duties. The system should verify the article exists and is accessible before accepting image uploads. Additionally, the system must scan uploaded images for malware and reject any files that fail security validation, protecting the community from malicious uploads. When an image is successfully uploaded, it becomes immediately visible on the article page in the order it was uploaded, with the original filename displayed to help readers identify the content. Note that uploaded images have soft delete support through the deleted_at field, allowing recovery if images are removed in error or if the parent article deletion is reversed.

It operates on the discussion_board_article_documents table, creating new document attachment records linked to the parent article. The operation accepts document files in supported formats (PDF, DOCX, DOC, TXT, RTF, ODT) up to 10MB per file, validates file type and size, scans for security threats, stores the files securely, and creates database records tracking the attachments. This endpoint enables members and moderators to add supporting documentation, research papers, policy documents, and other reference materials to their articles after initial publication.
operations.summary: Upload and attach document files to an article
operations.description:
Creates new document attachments for an existing article by uploading and validating document files, then linking them to the parent article. This operation enables article authors to enhance their economic and political discussions with supporting materials such as PDF research papers, Word documents with detailed analysis, or text files with supplementary data.

The operation performs comprehensive validation on uploaded documents. Each file is checked for format compatibility (must be PDF, DOCX, DOC, TXT, RTF, or ODT), size constraints (maximum 10MB per document), and security threats through malware scanning. Files are validated both by MIME type and actual file content to prevent format spoofing. The system enforces article-level limits, rejecting uploads that would exceed the maximum of 5 document attachments per article or the total attachment size limit of 100MB across all files and images.

When validation passes, the system generates a unique storage filename to prevent conflicts, stores the file securely, and creates a record in the discussion_board_article_documents table. The record captures the original filename for user display, the secure stored filename, file metadata (size, MIME type), the uploader's member ID, and the creation timestamp. The uploaded_by_member_id field tracks who added the document for accountability and moderation purposes.

Permissions are validated to ensure only the article author or moderators can add documents to an article. Members can only attach documents to their own articles, while moderators can attach documents to any article as part of their content management capabilities. The operation returns the complete document attachment information upon success, including the generated document ID, stored metadata, and access URLs for downloading the document.

operations.summary: Create a new comment on a discussion board article
operations.description:
This operation enables authenticated members and moderators to post new comments on articles within the discussion board system. Comments are the primary mechanism for user engagement and discussion on economic and political topics, allowing the community to respond to article content, ask questions, and engage in substantive dialogue.

The operation validates that the target article exists and is accessible, verifies the user is authenticated as a member or moderator, and validates the comment content meets length requirements (minimum 1 character, maximum 5000 characters as specified in requirements). The comment is associated with the article identified by the articleId path parameter and attributed to the authenticated user through the author_type discriminator field and corresponding discussion_board_member_id or discussion_board_moderator_id foreign key.

Upon successful creation, the comment appears immediately in the article's comment thread without requiring moderation approval. The system automatically records the creation timestamp, sets the comment status to active, and increments the parent article's comment_count metadata. Comments support single-level threading through the discussion_board_parent_comment_id field, allowing replies to top-level comments while maintaining simplicity by preventing deeply nested conversation threads.

Security considerations include authentication verification to prevent unauthenticated posting, input sanitization to prevent XSS attacks, rate limiting to prevent spam (members limited to reasonable posting frequency), and content validation to ensure meaningful contributions. The operation respects the article's publication status, allowing comments only on published articles, not drafts or deleted content.

Related operations include GET /articles/{articleId}/comments for retrieving comment threads, PUT /comments/{commentId} for editing own comments, and DELETE /comments/{commentId} for removing comments. This operation is fundamental to the discussion board's core value proposition of enabling evidence-based discourse on economic and political topics.

The system validates the updated content against the same rules as comment creation: minimum 1 character, maximum 5000 characters, with sanitization to prevent XSS attacks.

The operation updates the comment content in the discussion_board_comments table, sets the updated_at timestamp to the current time, and creates a new snapshot in discussion_board_comment_snapshots to preserve the edit history. Comment edits do not affect the comment's position in the thread or its relationship to parent articles or parent comments. The operation validates that the authenticated user has permission to delete the comment (either they are the original author or they are a moderator), confirms the deletion intent, and marks the comment as deleted. When a top-level comment with replies is deleted, all child replies are also hidden from public view following the cascade hiding rule defined in the requirements.
operations.summary: Soft-delete a comment from a discussion board article
operations.description:
This operation allows members and moderators to remove comments from discussion board articles by performing a soft deletion. The comment system maintains data integrity and audit trails by marking comments as deleted rather than permanently removing them from the database.

When a user deletes a comment, the system validates appropriate permissions - either the user is the original comment author, or they are a moderator with elevated privileges to manage any content. Members can only delete their own comments, while moderators can delete any comment to enforce community guidelines and maintain discussion quality.

The deletion process sets the deleted_at timestamp in the discussion_board_comments table to the current time, effectively hiding the comment from public view while preserving the record for moderation review and audit purposes. The soft-deleted comment remains in the database for historical tracking, compliance requirements, and potential recovery scenarios. The comment content is retained but marked as deleted, and it no longer appears in comment listings or search results for regular users.

The system maintains referential integrity throughout the deletion process, ensuring that the parent article's comment_count is decremented to reflect the hidden comment. The operation respects the business rule that comments appear immediately without requiring approval, as specified in the comment system requirements.

Security considerations include validating user authentication, enforcing content validation rules to prevent XSS attacks through sanitization, rate limiting to prevent spam, and ensuring the authenticated member has permission to post replies. The operation maintains data integrity by validating referential integrity between the reply, parent comment, and parent article.

operations.specification: This operation provides advanced search functionality across all published articles in the discussion board system. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table with complex filtering, sorting, and pagination capabilities. The search supports keyword matching across article titles and body content using trigram indexes, filtering by categories and tags through junction tables, filtering by author, date ranges, and attachment presence. Results are returned in paginated format with configurable page sizes and multiple sorting options including relevance, date, view count, and comment count.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve filtered, paginated list of discussion board articles
operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive, filtered, and paginated list of discussion board articles based on advanced search criteria. This operation enables users to discover relevant economic and political discussions through keyword search, category filtering, tag filtering, author filtering, and date range constraints.

The search functionality performs full-text search across article titles and body content using PostgreSQL trigram indexes for efficient partial matching. Users can search for keywords like "monetary policy" or "trade agreements" and receive ranked results based on relevance. The system prioritizes title matches over body content matches to surface the most relevant articles.

This operation supports comprehensive filtering options including multiple category selection (articles matching any selected category), multiple tag selection (articles matching all selected tags), author filtering by member username, date range filtering for publication dates, and attachment presence filtering (articles with images, documents, or any attachments). Filters can be combined to create highly specific queries.

Sorting capabilities include multiple options: relevance-based ranking for keyword searches (default when search keywords are provided), newest first by creation date (default when no keywords), oldest first, most viewed by view_count, most commented by comment_count, and recently updated by updated_at timestamp. The system maintains consistent performance even with complex filter and sort combinations through appropriate database indexing.

Pagination follows standard patterns with configurable page size (10, 20, 50, or 100 articles per page, default 20) and page number navigation. Results include total article count, total page count, current page number, and the array of matching articles in summary format optimized for list display.

Security considerations include rate limiting on search operations to prevent abuse, filtering out soft-deleted articles (where deleted_at is not null), respecting article status (only published articles visible to guests, draft articles visible only to authors), and appropriate access control based on the requesting user's authentication status. The operation is accessible to all users including guests, members, and moderators, with identical search capabilities for all user types.

This operation integrates with the discussion_board_articles table as the primary data source, joins with discussion_board_article_categories and discussion_board_categories for category filtering, joins with discussion_board_article_tags and discussion_board_tags for tag filtering, joins with discussion_board_members for author information, and references discussion_board_article_images and discussion_board_article_documents for attachment filtering. The response returns summary information optimized for search result display, including article metadata, excerpt from body content, author information, category and tag lists, and attachment indicators without loading full attachment details.

responseBody.description: Paginated search results containing article summaries matching the specified criteria with relevance ranking

It operates on the discussion_board_reports table with filtering and sorting capabilities specific to moderation workflows. The operation supports filtering by report status (pending, under_review, resolved, dismissed), report reason categories, target content type (article or comment), date ranges, and reviewing moderator. Results are returned in paginated format with sorting options optimized for moderation queue management. This operation is restricted to moderators only as it exposes the moderation review queue.
operations.summary: Retrieve filtered, paginated list of content reports for moderator review
operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive, filtered, and paginated list of content reports submitted by members flagging potentially inappropriate articles or comments. This operation provides moderators with access to the moderation review queue, enabling efficient content moderation and community guideline enforcement.

The report listing system supports filtering by multiple criteria to help moderators prioritize and manage their workload effectively. Moderators can filter by report status to focus on pending reports requiring review, reports currently under review by other moderators, resolved reports for reference, or dismissed reports where no action was taken. Status filtering enables efficient queue management and workload distribution among multiple moderators.

Additional filtering capabilities include report reason category filtering (spam, harassment, hate speech, misinformation, off-topic, profanity, personal information disclosure, other), target content type filtering to show only article reports or only comment reports, date range filtering for reports submitted within specific timeframes, reporter filtering by member username for investigating report patterns, and reviewing moderator filtering to see which reports are assigned to specific moderators. These filters can be combined to create focused moderation views.

Sorting options are optimized for moderation workflows including priority sorting showing most-reported content first (multiple reports on same content), oldest first to handle reports in submission order and prevent neglect, newest first to address recent reports quickly, and status-then-date sorting to group by status and sort chronologically within each status group. The default sort order is priority-based to surface urgent reports requiring immediate attention.

Each report in the results includes comprehensive information for moderator decision-making: report metadata (ID, submission timestamp, current status), reporter information (username, report history), reported content preview (article title and excerpt or comment content), report details (selected reason category, optional detailed explanation from reporter), count of reports on the same content (for priority assessment), reviewing moderator information if assigned, and resolution notes if the report has been resolved. This rich information enables moderators to make informed decisions quickly.

Pagination follows standard patterns with configurable page size (25, 50, or 100 reports per page, default 50 for moderator efficiency) and page number navigation. The response includes total report count, total page count, current page number, and the array of report summaries optimized for the moderation dashboard display.

Security and access control are critical for this operation. It is restricted exclusively to users with the moderator role, verified through JWT token authentication. The operation validates moderator status before executing queries and logs all moderation queue access for audit purposes. Regular members and guests receive a 403 Forbidden error if they attempt to access this endpoint, protecting the confidentiality of the moderation process and reporter identities.

This operation integrates with multiple tables in the moderation system: discussion_board_reports as the primary data source, joins with discussion_board_members for reporter information, joins with discussion_board_moderators for reviewing moderator information, joins with discussion_board_articles for reported article content, joins with discussion_board_comments for reported comment content, and references discussion_board_moderation_actions for resolution tracking. The polymorphic relationship between reports and their targets (articles or comments) is handled through the reported_article_id and reported_comment_id fields with appropriate null handling.

The report is immediately added to the moderation queue with pending status, and all active moderators are notified of the new report for review.

If the reason is other, additional details are required to provide context for moderators.

The reporting system supports the progressive moderation workflow where members identify potential violations, moderators review the reports in their queue, and appropriate enforcement actions are taken. Multiple members can report the same content, with the system consolidating reports and increasing priority for content with five or more reports. This operation integrates with the moderation dashboard where moderators review pending reports and take action to maintain community standards.

operations.summary: Update content report status and resolution by report identifier
operations.description:
Updates an existing content report with review status, resolution notes, and moderator assignment. This operation is central to the moderation workflow, enabling moderators to process reports submitted by community members who flag articles or comments that potentially violate community guidelines.

When a moderator reviews a report, they can update the report status to reflect the current review state: under_review when they begin examining the content, resolved when they take action on the reported content, or dismissed when the report is found to be invalid. The operation also allows moderators to assign themselves as the reviewing moderator and document their decision through resolution notes. Status transitions typically follow the pattern: pending → under_review → resolved/dismissed.

The operation validates that the specified report exists in the discussion_board_reports table and that the authenticated moderator has permission to update reports. It ensures referential integrity by verifying that any assigned reviewing_moderator_id corresponds to a valid moderator account. The system automatically updates the updated_at timestamp to track when the report was last modified, maintaining a complete audit trail of moderation activity. Resolution notes are recommended when setting status to resolved or dismissed to document the moderator's decision rationale.

This operation is typically used in conjunction with related moderation actions. After updating a report status, moderators often create corresponding moderation_actions records to document specific enforcement actions taken (content deletion, user warnings, etc.). The operation supports the progressive discipline system by enabling moderators to track violation patterns across multiple reports for the same user or content.

operations.summary: Dismiss a content report without taking action on the reported content
operations.description:
Dismisses a content report after moderator review determines that no violation occurred or no action is warranted. This operation is a specialized moderation workflow action that allows moderators to close reports without taking enforcement actions against the reported content or its author. Dismissal explicitly indicates that no community guideline violation was found, distinguishing it from resolution which implies action was taken.

When a moderator dismisses a report, the system updates the report status to dismissed in the discussion_board_reports table, assigns the moderator as the reviewing_moderator_id, and records dismissal reasoning in the resolution_notes field. This creates a complete record of why the report was dismissed, which is valuable for moderator accountability, training, and handling potential appeals. The reported content remains unchanged and visible, and no enforcement actions are taken against the content author.

The operation validates that the specified report exists and is in a state that can be dismissed (typically pending or under_review status). It ensures the authenticated moderator has appropriate permissions to dismiss reports. The system automatically updates the updated_at timestamp to track when the dismissal occurred.

This operation supports the moderation system's transparency by documenting false reports or reports that don't meet community guideline violation thresholds. It helps moderators track report accuracy patterns and identify users who may be abusing the reporting system. Dismissed reports remain in the audit trail permanently, contributing to the overall moderation accountability and quality assurance processes.

These filters can be combined to perform sophisticated queries such as finding all content deletions by a specific moderator in the past month or identifying all user suspensions triggered by community reports.

Security and access control are critical for this operation. Only authenticated moderators have access to the moderation action logs, ensuring that audit information remains confidential within the moderation team. The operation includes comprehensive pagination support with configurable page sizes and multiple sorting options (newest first, oldest first, by moderator, by action type) to facilitate efficient review of potentially large audit datasets.

Each moderation action record in the results includes the complete context: the moderator who performed the action, the type and reason for the action, the targeted entity (article, comment, or user), timestamps, detailed notes, and relationships to triggering reports. This comprehensive information enables moderators to understand the full context of past decisions, maintain consistency in enforcement, and identify patterns that may require policy adjustments or additional moderator training.

The moderation action record captures multiple dimensions of the intervention: the specific moderator who performed the action with their unique identifier, the precise type of action taken (edit_content, delete_content, restore_content, warn_user, suspend_user, ban_user, lift_suspension, dismiss_report), the target entity affected by the action (identified by target_type and target_id), the reason or justification for the action, and optional detailed notes explaining the decision-making process and context.

This operation integrates deeply with the broader moderation system defined in the requirements. When a moderator takes action in response to a community report, the operation links the action to the triggering report through the related_report_id field, enabling traceability from user reports through moderator review to final resolution. When moderators take proactive actions without a triggering report, the related_report_id remains null, indicating moderator-initiated enforcement.

The audit trail created by this operation serves multiple critical business purposes. It enables oversight and accountability by providing complete visibility into all moderator decisions. It supports consistent enforcement by allowing moderators to review how similar cases were handled previously. It facilitates appeal processes by documenting the rationale for actions that users may contest. It identifies patterns in moderation activity that may indicate policy gaps, training needs, or emerging community issues.

All moderation action records are permanent and cannot be deleted, though they may be supplemented with additional notes or corrections. This immutability ensures the integrity of the audit trail for legal compliance, community trust, and operational transparency.

This ensures complete traceability of when warnings were issued versus when they were modified. The warned member may receive notification of significant changes to warnings affecting their account standing.

Soft deletion of warnings is crucial for maintaining moderation accountability and audit trails. Even when warnings are retracted, the system preserves records of what actions were taken, by whom, and when they were reversed. This supports appeals processes where members can challenge warnings, and reviewing moderators can overturn incorrect decisions without erasing the historical record.

The operation updates the warning's deleted_at timestamp to the current time and sets the updated_at timestamp accordingly. The warning will no longer appear in the user's active warnings list or count toward progressive discipline escalation. However, moderators can still view the deleted warning in audit logs and moderation history interfaces for full transparency.

Security and permission validation ensures only moderators can delete warnings, and the operation confirms the warning exists and is not already deleted before proceeding. Deleting a warning does not automatically reverse any subsequent enforcement actions that may have been based on the warning (such as suspensions), though it may be grounds for reviewing those actions separately.

operations.summary: Retrieve comprehensive moderation dashboard overview with pending reports and recent activity
operations.description:
This operation provides moderators with a comprehensive overview of the moderation dashboard, consolidating critical information from multiple data sources to enable efficient moderation workflows. The dashboard overview serves as the primary entry point for moderators to assess current moderation needs and prioritize their work.

The overview includes several key components that give moderators complete situational awareness. First, it displays all pending reports that require review, including both article and comment reports that members have flagged for potential guideline violations. Each pending report shows essential metadata such as report reason, submission time, and number of reports on the same content to help moderators prioritize urgent issues. Second, the overview presents recent moderation actions taken by all moderators, creating transparency and enabling team coordination. This includes content edits, deletions, user warnings, and suspensions with timestamps and brief descriptions. Third, it shows currently active user suspensions that are in effect, helping moderators track enforcement actions and upcoming expiration dates.

The dashboard aggregates statistics across the moderation system to provide quantitative insights into moderation workload and trends. Key metrics include total pending reports awaiting review, reports currently under review by other moderators, reports resolved in the past 24 hours, total active suspensions in effect, and warnings issued in the past week. These statistics help moderators understand system health and identify patterns that may require policy adjustments or additional moderator resources.

Security considerations include strict authorization enforcement ensuring only authenticated moderators can access this endpoint. The operation respects moderator permissions as defined in the discussion_board_moderators table, where the moderation_permissions field may specify different access levels for different moderator roles. The dashboard data is sensitive and contains information about reported content and user enforcement actions that must not be exposed to regular members or guests.

This operation integrates data from the discussion_board_reports table to show pending and recent reports, the discussion_board_moderation_actions table to display recent moderator interventions, the discussion_board_user_warnings table to count recent warnings, and the discussion_board_user_suspensions table to show active suspensions. The response provides a unified view of this distributed data, optimized for quick assessment and decision-making by moderators who need to efficiently manage community content quality.

The statistics help moderators and administrators understand moderation workload patterns, enforcement effectiveness, and community health trends over time.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed moderation statistics and analytics for system health monitoring
operations.description:
This operation provides moderators with detailed statistical analysis of moderation activity and system health metrics. The statistics endpoint goes beyond the basic overview to deliver comprehensive analytics that help moderators understand trends, measure effectiveness, and identify areas requiring attention. This data-driven approach to moderation enables informed decision-making about policy enforcement and resource allocation.

The statistics response includes several analytical dimensions that provide deep insight into moderation patterns. Time-series data shows how report volumes, moderation actions, and enforcement decisions have changed over various time periods including the past 24 hours, past week, and past month. This temporal analysis helps identify emerging issues, seasonal patterns, or trending topics that may require increased moderation attention. Breakdown by violation type categorizes reports and actions by the type of guideline violation such as spam, harassment, misinformation, and offensive content, enabling moderators to understand which policy areas see the most activity and may need clearer guidelines or additional enforcement focus.

Moderator workload distribution shows how moderation work is distributed across the moderator team, including reports reviewed per moderator, average review time per report, and actions taken per moderator. This helps identify workload balance issues and recognize particularly active or effective moderators. Resolution outcome statistics track how reports are resolved including percentage dismissed as false reports, percentage resulting in content edits, percentage resulting in content deletion, and percentage resulting in user warnings or suspensions. These metrics measure the accuracy of community reporting and the appropriateness of moderation responses.

User behavior metrics analyze patterns in user violations and enforcement effectiveness. Statistics include repeat violation rates showing what percentage of warned or suspended users commit subsequent violations, time between violations for users with multiple infractions, and effectiveness of progressive discipline in reducing problematic behavior. Content health metrics measure overall community quality including ratio of reported content to total content, average time to resolve reports, and percentage of content requiring moderation intervention.

The operation calculates aggregations and percentages from raw data in the underlying tables, including GROUP BY operations on time periods and violation categories, COUNT and SUM aggregations for various metrics, and AVERAGE calculations for response times and resolution rates. The statistics do not map to a single Prisma table but instead represent computed analytical views derived from multiple tables through complex SQL queries and business logic.

Security and authorization requirements ensure only authenticated moderators can access these statistics. The data contains sensitive information about enforcement actions and community health that must be restricted to users with moderation privileges. The response does not include personally identifiable information about specific users but provides aggregate anonymous statistics suitable for system monitoring and policy evaluation.

responseBody.description: Comprehensive statistical analysis of moderation activity including time-series trends, violation breakdowns, moderator workload, and effectiveness metrics

operations.name: statistics

prerequisites.description: Reports must exist to calculate report metrics including total reports, resolution times, and violation type distributions
Moderation actions must exist to calculate action metrics including action counts, type distributions, and temporal trends
User warnings must exist to calculate user behavior metrics and progressive discipline effectiveness
User suspensions must exist to calculate suspension counts, user behavior patterns, and enforcement escalation metrics

authorizations.name: guest
authorizations.description: Unauthenticated visitors who can browse and read public articles and comments but cannot post, comment, or interact with content. Guests can register for an account or log in if they already have one.

authorizations.name: member

authorizations.name: moderator
authorizations.description: Trusted users with elevated permissions who can manage all content across the discussion board. Moderators can edit or delete any article or comment (not just their own), manage user accounts, enforce community guidelines, handle reported content, and maintain the overall quality of discussions.

access.description:

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

username.description:
Unique username for member identification and login.

Must be 3-30 characters long and contain only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens. The username serves as a permanent identifier for the user account and is used for login authentication along with the email address.

Usernames are case-insensitive for uniqueness validation, meaning 'JohnDoe' and 'johndoe' are considered the same username. The system enforces username uniqueness across all member accounts to prevent conflicts.

Reserved usernames (such as 'admin', 'moderator', 'system') are prohibited to prevent impersonation of system roles.

email.description:
Email address for authentication, notifications, and account recovery.

Must be a valid email address following standard email format specifications. The email serves as the primary contact method and an alternative login identifier (users can log in with either username or email).

Email addresses are unique across all member accounts using case-insensitive comparison. The system validates email format and sends a verification email to confirm email ownership before activating full member privileges.

This email address will receive important notifications including account verification, password reset instructions, and security alerts. Members can change their email address later through a separate verification process.

password.description:
Plain text password for account authentication.

Must be at least 8 characters long and contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character (!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>?) to ensure password strength and account security.

The password is transmitted to the server in plain text over HTTPS and immediately hashed using a secure one-way hashing algorithm (bcrypt or Argon2) before storage. The system never stores passwords in plain text format.

Users are encouraged to create strong, unique passwords. The system validates password strength in real-time during registration and provides feedback on password quality. Commonly compromised passwords (from known breach databases) are rejected to enhance security.

This password will be used for future login operations and can be changed later through the account settings with proper verification.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.
IP address not provided by client (server will extract from request).

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.

This field is OPTIONAL and can be provided by the client for server-side rendering (SSR) scenarios where the actual client IP needs to be forwarded. When not provided (null or undefined), the backend server automatically extracts the IP address from the HTTP request headers.

The IP address is used for security monitoring, rate limiting, and session management. It helps detect suspicious activities such as multiple failed login attempts from the same IP or concurrent sessions from vastly different geographic locations.

For direct browser-to-server connections, clients typically omit this field and let the server detect the IP. For SSR scenarios, the application server should provide the actual client IP to ensure accurate session tracking.

href.description:
Connection URL where the registration session was initiated.

This is the MANDATORY current page URL from which the user is registering. It represents the complete URL of the registration page or component, including protocol, domain, path, and any query parameters.

The href value is used for session tracking, analytics, and security purposes. It helps identify the context in which the user registered and enables detection of unusual registration patterns or potential security issues.

For single-page applications (SPAs), this should be the current browser URL. For multi-page applications, this is the registration page URL. For mobile applications using WebView, this should reflect the appropriate application context.

Example values:
- 'https://discussion.example.com/register'
- 'https://discussion.example.com/signup?source=homepage'
- 'https://discussion.example.com/auth/join'

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the registration page.

This is the MANDATORY previous page URL from which the user navigated to the registration page. It represents the page the user was viewing before deciding to register, providing context about their journey to registration.

The referrer value is used for analytics, understanding user acquisition sources, and tracking registration conversion funnels. It helps identify which pages or external sources drive user registrations.

For direct navigation (user types URL directly or uses bookmark), this should be an empty string. For navigation from another page, this should be the complete URL of that previous page.

Example values:
- 'https://discussion.example.com/articles/economic-policy' (registered after reading an article)
- 'https://search.google.com/search?q=economic+discussion+board' (came from search)
- '' (empty string for direct navigation)
- 'https://news.example.com/article-with-link' (external referrer)

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IRegistration.description:
Registration request data for creating a new member account from guest status.

This DTO contains all information necessary for a guest user to register as a member of the discussion board. Registration is the first step in the user lifecycle, transitioning an unauthenticated guest into an authenticated member with content creation privileges.

The registration process creates a new member account in pending_email_verification status. Upon successful account creation, the system sends a verification email to the provided address and immediately issues JWT tokens for authenticated access. However, certain member privileges (posting articles and comments) require email verification completion.

This is a self-registration operation where the guest themselves are creating their own account, so session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are included to establish the initial session immediately upon registration. The href and referrer fields are mandatory as they capture the registration context, while ip is optional since the server can extract it from the HTTP request.

The system enforces strict validation rules including username uniqueness (case-insensitive), email uniqueness (case-insensitive), username format restrictions, and password strength requirements. Any validation failures result in specific error messages guiding the user to correct their input.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated guest session.

This UUID corresponds to the guest record in the discussion_board_guests table. It uniquely identifies this particular guest browsing session across all requests and enables session tracking for analytics and rate limiting purposes.

session_token.description:
Unique session identifier for tracking guest activity across requests.

This token uniquely identifies the guest browsing session and is used to track activity patterns, implement rate limiting, and maintain session continuity across multiple API requests. The session token is generated during initial guest access and remains constant throughout the guest's browsing session.

Session tokens are enforced as unique in the discussion_board_guests table through a database constraint. They serve as a stable identifier for unauthenticated users who do not have permanent user accounts, enabling basic analytics and security measures like preventing abuse through excessive requests from the same session.

The session token is distinct from JWT tokens - it is a simple session identifier stored in the database rather than a cryptographically signed authentication credential. It provides session continuity for guests who are browsing public content without requiring full authentication.

ip_address.description:
IP address of the guest user for security monitoring and rate limiting.

Captures the network address from which the guest is accessing the discussion board. This information is critical for implementing security measures including rate limiting to prevent abuse (limiting requests per IP address), detecting suspicious activity patterns or potential bot traffic, identifying geographic access patterns for analytics, and enforcing IP-based access controls if needed.

The IP address is automatically extracted from HTTP request headers by the backend server or can be explicitly provided in server-side rendering scenarios. It is stored in the discussion_board_guests table and indexed for efficient querying when implementing rate limiting or security investigations.

IP addresses are logged for all guest sessions to maintain security audit trails and enable detection of coordinated abuse attempts from multiple sessions originating from the same network location.

user_agent.description:
Browser user agent string for analytics and compatibility tracking.

Captures the User-Agent HTTP header sent by the guest's browser or client application. This string identifies the browser type, version, operating system, and device used to access the discussion board. The information supports several use cases including tracking browser compatibility and identifying rendering issues, analyzing device distribution (desktop vs mobile vs tablet), detecting bot traffic through user agent patterns, and understanding platform usage across different client environments.

The user agent is automatically extracted from HTTP request headers by the backend. It is optional (nullable) because some clients or privacy-focused browsers may not send User-Agent headers, or the header may be blocked by proxies.

Stored in the discussion_board_guests table for analytics purposes, this data helps inform technical decisions about browser support, responsive design priorities, and compatibility testing strategies. It is not used for access control but rather for understanding and optimizing the user experience across different platforms.

last_activity_at.description:
Timestamp of the guest's most recent activity for session management.

Records the date and time of the guest's last interaction with the discussion board, such as page views, article reads, or API requests. This timestamp is automatically updated by the system on each authenticated request from the guest session.

The last activity timestamp serves multiple purposes in session management including identifying inactive sessions for cleanup (sessions with no activity for extended periods may be expired), tracking engagement patterns to understand typical guest browsing duration, implementing session timeout policies, and providing data for analytics about guest user behavior.

Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information (timestamptz in database). The field is indexed in the discussion_board_guests table to enable efficient queries for session cleanup processes that remove stale guest sessions.

Unlike permanent member accounts, guest sessions are temporary and may be purged after extended inactivity. The last_activity_at timestamp is the key field for determining when sessions should be considered abandoned and eligible for deletion.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest session was created.

Records the exact date and time when this guest session was first established and the corresponding record was inserted into the discussion_board_guests table. This timestamp is immutable after session creation and provides the start point for session duration calculations.

The creation timestamp is used for session lifecycle management including calculating session age for analytics (how long guests browse before leaving or registering), implementing session expiration policies based on absolute session age, tracking guest user acquisition patterns over time, and providing audit trails for security investigations.

Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information (timestamptz in database). Combined with last_activity_at, this enables differentiation between total session lifetime and active browsing time, helping understand guest engagement patterns and typical conversion timelines from guest to registered member.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized.description:
Response payload containing authenticated guest session information and JWT tokens.

This schema represents the successful result of guest authentication operations, specifically token refresh. It provides the guest session identifier and complete JWT token set necessary for subsequent authenticated API requests.

The response includes comprehensive guest session information from the discussion_board_guests table, including the unique session identifier (id and session_token), connection metadata (ip_address and user_agent), and temporal tracking (last_activity_at and created_at). This complete session context enables robust session management, security monitoring, and analytics tracking for unauthenticated users browsing the discussion board.

The token object contains both access and refresh tokens following the standardized authentication token structure, enabling guests to maintain authenticated sessions for browsing public content. While guests have read-only access and cannot create content, the JWT tokens authenticate their session for rate limiting, personalization, and potential transition to member registration.

This enhanced response provides clients with complete visibility into the guest session state, supporting features like session duration display, activity tracking, and informed decision-making about session management and user experience optimization.

refresh_token.description:
Valid refresh token issued during previous authentication.

This token is used to obtain a new access token when the current access token expires. The refresh token has a 14-day lifespan and must be valid and not expired for the operation to succeed.

The refresh token is typically stored securely in httpOnly cookies or secure client storage and transmitted with refresh requests to maintain session continuity without requiring users to re-enter credentials.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IRefresh.description:
Request payload for refreshing JWT access token using a valid refresh token.

This schema represents the data required to refresh an expired access token without requiring full re-authentication. The refresh mechanism enables seamless session continuation for guest users browsing the discussion board.

When an access token expires after its 30-minute lifespan, users can use their refresh token (valid for 14 days) to obtain a new access token. This prevents interruption of browsing activities and maintains user session state without requiring repeated credential entry.

The refresh operation validates the provided refresh token's authenticity, expiration status, and association with a valid session before issuing new tokens. Rate limiting is applied to prevent abuse and brute-force attacks on the refresh mechanism.

username.description:
Unique username for member identification and login.

Must be between 3 and 30 characters long and contain only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens. The username is used for login, public display, and profile URLs.

Username is checked for uniqueness (case-insensitive) and validated against reserved system keywords (admin, moderator, system, anonymous, deleted, user). Special characters and spaces are not allowed to ensure URL safety.

email.description:
Email address for authentication and notifications.

Must be a valid email format and unique across all member accounts. This email will receive a verification link that must be confirmed before the account can be used.

The email is used for login, password recovery, and system notifications. The system validates email format according to standard specifications and checks for uniqueness using case-insensitive comparison.

password.description:
Password for account authentication.

Must be at least 8 characters long and contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character (!@#$%^&*). The password is securely hashed (bcrypt or equivalent) before storage and never stored in plain text.

Password strength is validated to ensure account security. Common passwords and passwords matching the username or email are rejected.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking.

Optional field that can be provided by the client for server-side rendering scenarios. If not provided, the server will extract the IP address from the request headers.

Used to populate the ip field in the discussion_board_member_sessions table for security auditing and rate limiting purposes.

href.description:
Connection URL where the registration occurred.

Required field indicating the current page URL where the user initiated registration. Used to populate the href field in the discussion_board_member_sessions table.

This information is valuable for analytics and understanding user registration flows. Must be a valid URI format.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the registration page.

Required field indicating the previous page URL before the user reached the registration page. Used to populate the referrer field in the discussion_board_member_sessions table.

This can be an empty string for direct access (user navigated directly to registration without a referrer). Must be a valid URI format when provided.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IJoin.description:
Member registration request for creating new accounts.

This DTO is used when a new user registers for a member account on the discussion board. It contains all required information for account creation including credentials (username, email, password) and session context (ip, href, referrer).

The registration process enforces strict validation rules on all fields to ensure data quality and security. Usernames must be unique and follow naming conventions. Email addresses must be unique and valid. Passwords must meet complexity requirements.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are included because this is a self-signup operation where the user themselves is creating their account and establishing their first session. The backend uses this information to create the initial session record in discussion_board_member_sessions.

Upon successful registration, the account is created with status pending_email_verification and email_verified set to false. A verification email is sent, and the user must verify their email before they can log in and access member features.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated member.

This is the member's primary key from the discussion_board_members table, used for all subsequent API requests requiring member identification.

username.description:
Username of the newly registered and authenticated member.

Provides immediate context about the authenticated account. This is the permanent username that will be used for attribution in articles and comments.

email.description:
Email address of the registered member.

Confirms the email address associated with the account. Included in registration response for user verification and record-keeping.

display_name.description:
Optional alternative display name for public-facing member identification.

When provided, this display name (1-50 characters) is shown instead of the username in public contexts such as article authorship, comment attribution, and user profiles. If null or not provided, the system falls back to displaying the username.

Display names allow members to present themselves with a preferred name or pseudonym while keeping their username as a stable login identifier.

bio.description:
Optional member biography or self-description.

This free-form text field (maximum 500 characters) allows members to describe themselves, their interests, expertise, or perspective on economic and political topics. The bio is displayed on the member's public profile if profile_visibility allows.

Basic text formatting such as line breaks is preserved, but HTML tags are stripped to prevent XSS attacks. This helps other community members understand the author's background when reading their contributions.

location.description:
Optional geographic location of the member.

This is a free-text field (maximum 100 characters) where members can specify their city, country, region, or any geographic identifier they wish to share. No geocoding or validation is performed - it is purely informational and displayed on the member's public profile.

Location information provides context for members' perspectives on regional economic policies or political developments.

website_url.description:
Optional personal or professional website URL.

Members can provide a link to their personal blog, professional profile, research page, or other web presence. The URL must be properly formatted with http:// or https:// protocol and is displayed as a clickable link on the member's public profile.

This field enables members to share their credentials, additional writings, or institutional affiliations with the community.

profile_picture_url.description:
URL of the member's profile picture or avatar.

This URL points to the member's uploaded profile picture, which is displayed throughout the platform in article bylines, comment attribution, and the member's profile page. If null, the system displays a default avatar image.

Profile pictures are uploaded through a separate file upload endpoint and stored in the file storage system. This field contains only the URL reference to the stored image.

email_verified.description:
Indicates whether the member's email address has been verified.

Email verification is required before a member can create articles or post comments. The verification process involves sending a verification email with a unique token link that the member must click to confirm email ownership.

This field is set to false upon account creation and updated to true when the email verification link is successfully validated. Members with unverified emails can log in but have restricted content creation capabilities until verification is completed.

status.description:
Current status of the member account.

This field controls account lifecycle and access permissions. Valid status values include pending_email_verification for newly created accounts awaiting email confirmation, active for verified accounts in good standing with full member access, suspended for temporarily disabled accounts due to moderation action, and deleted for accounts that have been soft-deleted and are pending permanent removal.

Status transitions are tracked and logged for audit purposes. Status changes affect authentication eligibility and content creation permissions throughout the system.

profile_visibility.description:
Controls who can view this member's profile information.

Valid values include public for profiles visible to all users including guests, members_only for profiles visible only to authenticated members and moderators, and private for profiles visible only to moderators (for moderation purposes).

This privacy setting determines access to the member's profile page, bio, location, website, and other personal information. It does not affect the visibility of the member's articles or comments, which remain publicly accessible.

activity_visibility.description:
Controls who can view this member's activity history.

Valid values include public for activity visible to all users including guests, members_only for activity visible only to authenticated members and moderators, and hidden for activity not displayed on the profile but still accessible through article and comment listings.

Activity visibility affects the display of the member's articles and comments list on their profile page. Individual articles and comments remain accessible through normal browsing and search regardless of this setting.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the member's most recent successful login.

This field is automatically updated each time the member successfully authenticates. It is used for account security monitoring, inactive account detection, and activity analytics.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information (stored as timestamptz in database). A null value indicates the member has never logged in since account creation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the member account was originally created.

This is an immutable field set automatically during account registration. It is used for calculating account age, displaying member since information, sorting members by join date, and audit trail purposes.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, representing the exact moment the member record was inserted into the discussion_board_members table.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the member profile was last modified.

This field is automatically updated whenever any member account information changes, including profile edits, password changes, privacy setting updates, or status changes. It helps track account maintenance activity and identify recently updated profiles.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, representing the most recent modification to any field in the member record.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the member account.

When a member deletes their account, this field is set to the deletion timestamp rather than immediately removing the record. This enables account recovery during a grace period (typically 14-30 days), maintains referential integrity for authored articles and comments, and preserves audit trail for moderation records.

A null value indicates the account is active. A non-null value indicates the account is soft-deleted, should be excluded from active member lists, and prevented from authenticating. After the grace period expires, the account may be permanently deleted or anonymized according to content retention policies.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IAuthorized.description:
Successful registration response with authentication tokens.

Returned after successful account creation and automatic authentication. This type contains the newly created member's essential information along with JWT authentication tokens that enable immediate platform access.

The registration operation automatically logs in the user after email verification, creating an initial session in discussion_board_member_sessions and issuing authentication tokens. This provides a seamless onboarding experience where users can immediately begin participating after verifying their email.

The response includes the member's unique identifier (id), authentication tokens (access and refresh tokens packaged in the token object), and basic account information (username, email). This allows the client application to store authentication credentials and immediately identify the logged-in user.

Security note: This response includes the member's email address, which is normally protected and not exposed in public API responses. It is included here only because the user just registered with this email and should receive confirmation of the account details they provided.

username_or_email.description:
Username or email address for login identification.

Members can log in using either their unique username or their registered email address. The system will look up the account using either identifier.

This flexible login approach improves user experience by allowing members to use whichever identifier they remember. The system performs case-insensitive lookup for both username and email.

password.description:
Password for authentication.

Plain text password provided by the user for verification against the stored password hash. The password is validated using secure comparison to prevent timing attacks.

After 5 failed login attempts within 15 minutes, the account is temporarily locked for 30 minutes to prevent brute force attacks. Error messages do not reveal whether the username/email or password was incorrect.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking.

Optional field that can be provided by the client for server-side rendering scenarios. If not provided, the server will extract the IP address from the request headers.

Used to populate the ip field in the discussion_board_member_sessions table for security auditing, concurrent session tracking, and rate limiting purposes.

href.description:
Connection URL where the login occurred.

Required field indicating the current page URL where the user initiated login. Used to populate the href field in the discussion_board_member_sessions table.

This information helps track where users are logging in from and can be useful for identifying suspicious login patterns or understanding user flows.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the login page.

Required field indicating the previous page URL before the user reached the login page. Used to populate the referrer field in the discussion_board_member_sessions table.

Can be an empty string for direct access. This information helps understand how users navigate to the login page and can be valuable for analytics and user experience optimization.

IDiscussionBoardMember.ILogin.description:
Member login credentials for authentication.

This DTO is used when existing members authenticate to access the discussion board. It accepts either username or email along with the password, providing flexible login options for users.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are included because this is a self-login operation where the user themselves is establishing their own session. The backend uses this information to create a new session record in discussion_board_member_sessions, tracking where and when the login occurred for security monitoring and analytics.

The login process validates credentials against the discussion_board_members table, checking that the password matches the stored hash and that the account is active and email-verified. Failed login attempts are tracked and rate-limited to prevent brute force attacks.

Upon successful authentication, the system creates a new session record, updates the last_login_at timestamp, and issues JWT tokens (access and refresh) for maintaining the authenticated session.

refreshToken.description:
Valid refresh token issued during login or previous refresh operation.

This JWT token must be properly signed, not expired (14-day lifetime from issuance), and associated with an active member session in discussion_board_member_sessions. The system validates token signature integrity, expiration timestamp, and session validity before processing the refresh request.

If the refresh token is expired, compromised, or associated with a suspended/deleted account, the refresh operation will fail and require full re-authentication with username and password.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRefresh.description:
Request parameters for refreshing an expired access token using a valid refresh token.

This DTO is used when a member's access token expires (after 30 minutes) and they need to obtain a new access token without re-entering their credentials. The refresh operation validates the provided refresh token and issues new authentication tokens if the refresh token is valid and the member session remains active.

The refresh token must be associated with a valid, non-expired member session (discussion_board_member_sessions record). The system checks that the member account is still active, not suspended or deleted, and email verification status remains valid.

Optional security enhancement: The system may implement refresh token rotation, where successful refresh invalidates the old refresh token and issues a new one along with the new access token. This rotation mechanism limits the window of vulnerability if a refresh token is compromised.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ICreate.description:
Moderator registration request data for creating new moderator accounts.

This schema defines the request body for moderator registration (join) operations. New moderators provide their desired username, email address, and secure password to create an account. The system validates all inputs against strict requirements before creating the account.

Username must be 3-30 characters, containing only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens. It must be unique across all moderator accounts (case-insensitive check). Email must be valid format and unique. Password must meet complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character.

Upon successful registration, the system creates a moderator account with status pending_email_verification, email_verified set to false, generates a verification token, and sends a verification email. The system automatically assigns default values for system-managed fields including moderation_permissions (default permission set), profile_visibility ('public'), and activity_visibility ('public'). The moderator ID, creation timestamp, and update timestamp are all auto-generated by the database.

Optional profile fields (display_name, bio, location, website_url, profile_picture_url) allow moderators to complete their public profile during initial registration rather than requiring subsequent profile updates. These fields enhance moderator credibility and community trust by providing background information and professional context.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are included because this is a self-registration operation where the moderator themselves is creating their account and establishing their first authenticated session after email verification. The href and referrer fields are mandatory for session tracking, while ip is optional (server can extract from request headers).

IMPORTANT: This is a REQUEST schema for creating moderators. Response fields like id, timestamps, email_verified, status, moderation_permissions, profile_visibility, activity_visibility, and authentication tokens are NOT included here - they are returned in the IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized response schema after successful registration.

username.description:
Unique username for moderator identification and login.

This is the public identifier for the moderator account, used for login authentication and display in moderation actions. Usernames must be 3-30 characters long and contain only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens.

The system enforces case-insensitive uniqueness, meaning usernames 'Admin', 'admin', and 'ADMIN' are considered identical. Reserved usernames like 'admin', 'moderator', 'system', and 'anonymous' are prohibited.

Once created, usernames cannot be changed to maintain consistency in moderation audit trails and content attribution.

email.description:
Email address for authentication and notifications.

This is the primary contact method for the moderator account, used for login (alternative to username), email verification, password recovery, and moderation alerts. The email must be valid format according to RFC 5322 specifications and unique across all moderator accounts.

The system sends a verification email immediately after registration. Until the email is verified (email_verified set to true), the moderator account has limited privileges. The email address is kept private and never displayed publicly.

password.description:
Secure password for account authentication.

This is the plain text password provided during registration. The system validates password strength requiring minimum 8 characters with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character.

The password is immediately hashed using bcrypt or equivalent secure hashing algorithm before storage in the password_hash field. Plain text passwords are never stored in the database.

Common passwords and passwords matching the username or email are rejected. The system provides real-time password strength feedback during registration.

display_name.description:
Optional alternative display name for public presentation instead of username.

When provided during registration, this display name (1-50 characters) will be shown publicly instead of the username in moderation contexts, profile displays, and moderation action logs. If not provided or set to null, the system defaults to displaying the username in all public contexts.

Display names can contain any characters except control characters, providing flexibility for moderators to present themselves with their preferred name, real name, or professional identity. Unlike usernames, display names do not need to be unique across moderators, as the username remains the unique identifier.

Providing a display name during registration allows moderators to establish their public identity immediately without requiring a separate profile update step after account creation. This is particularly useful for moderators who want to maintain a professional or formal public presence distinct from their login username.

bio.description:
Optional moderator biography or self-description for the public profile.
