Provides space for new moderators to describe their background, expertise, areas of focus in economic and political topics, or moderation philosophy during the registration process. The bio is displayed on the moderator's public profile page and helps build community trust by providing transparency about moderator credentials and perspectives.

Limited to 500 characters to encourage concise self-description while providing sufficient space for meaningful context. The system preserves line breaks and basic text formatting in the bio field. HTML and script tags are sanitized to prevent XSS attacks while maintaining readability.

Providing a bio during registration enables immediate establishment of moderator credibility and transparency, though it can also be added or modified later through profile editing operations. For moderators affiliated with institutions or organizations, the bio can mention these credentials to build community confidence in moderation decisions.

location.description:
Optional geographic location of the moderator in free-text format.

Moderators can specify their city, country, region, or any geographic context they wish to share during registration. The location field is purely informational and not validated or geocoded - users enter location as plain text.

Limited to 100 characters. The location appears on the moderator's public profile and can provide context for their perspectives on regional economic or political issues. It also helps community members understand moderation coverage across different time zones and geographic regions.

No address verification or geographic data processing is performed on this field. Providing location during registration completes the profile immediately, though it can also be added later through profile updates. For distributed moderation teams, location transparency helps explain moderation availability patterns.

website_url.description:
Optional personal or professional website URL for the moderator.

If provided during registration, the website URL is displayed on the moderator's profile page as a clickable link, allowing moderators to direct community members to their personal blog, professional portfolio, institutional affiliation page, academic profile, or other online presence. This builds credibility and transparency in the moderation process.

The system validates that the URL is properly formatted with HTTP or HTTPS protocol. The URL can be up to 80,000 characters (VARCHAR limit) to accommodate very long URLs with query parameters, though typical URLs are much shorter. No verification is performed to check if the URL is accessible or valid beyond format validation.

Providing a website URL during registration enables immediate establishment of professional credentials and institutional affiliations, though it can also be added later through profile editing. For moderators representing organizations, think tanks, or academic institutions, the website link provides important context about their background and potential perspectives.

profile_picture_url.description:
Optional URL of the moderator's profile picture avatar image.

This URL points to a pre-uploaded profile picture image that represents the moderator visually throughout the discussion board. The profile picture is displayed next to the moderator's actions in moderation logs, in comment threads when the moderator participates in discussions, and on their profile page.

Following AutoBE's URL-only file upload pattern, clients must first upload the image file to the storage service (S3, CDN, etc.) to obtain a URL, then provide that URL during registration. The system does NOT accept binary image data or base64-encoded images in this field. This separation of file upload from entity creation enables better error handling, file validation, and storage flexibility.

If no profile picture URL is provided during registration, the system displays a default moderator avatar. Supported image formats for the referenced file should be JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP with a recommended maximum file size of 5MB and standard dimensions of 200x200 pixels for display optimization.

Providing a profile picture during registration creates a more complete and trustworthy moderator presence immediately, helping build community confidence in moderation team members. Profile pictures humanize moderators and make moderation actions feel more accountable and transparent. The picture can also be uploaded and set later through profile editing if not available during initial registration.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking.

This is an optional field that the client may provide for server-side rendering scenarios. If not provided, the server will extract the IP address from the HTTP request headers.

The IP address is recorded in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table for security auditing and rate limiting. It helps detect suspicious registration patterns and prevent abuse.

href.description:
Connection URL where registration is being performed.

This is the current page URL from which the moderator is initiating the registration request. It represents the location in the application where account creation is taking place.

This value is stored in the href field of the initial session record created upon successful registration. It is used for session tracking and analytics.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the registration page.

This is the previous page URL that directed the user to the registration interface. It helps track user acquisition sources and registration flow.

This value is stored in the referrer field of the initial session record created upon successful registration.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated moderator.

This is the primary key from the discussion_board_moderators table and uniquely identifies the moderator account across the system. This ID is used in all subsequent API requests to identify the authenticated user and is embedded in the JWT access token for authorization purposes.

The ID remains constant throughout the moderator's account lifetime and is used to associate content, moderation actions, and audit logs with this specific moderator.

username.description:
Unique username of the authenticated moderator.

This is the moderator's login identifier and public display name if no display_name is set. Usernames are 3-30 characters, containing only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens. The username is unique across all moderator accounts and is used for moderator identification in moderation logs and audit trails.

Used for display purposes in the UI and for moderator attribution in moderation actions and content management operations.

email.description:
Email address of the authenticated moderator.

This is the moderator's verified email address used for account notifications, security alerts, and communication regarding moderation activities. The email must be verified (email_verified = true) for the account to have full moderation privileges.

Email addresses are unique across all moderator accounts and serve as an alternative login identifier.

display_name.description:
Optional display name for the moderator.

If provided, this name is shown publicly instead of the username in moderation contexts and profile displays. Display names are 1-50 characters and can contain any characters except control characters. If null or not set, the username is used for all public displays.

This allows moderators to maintain a professional or preferred public identity separate from their login username.

bio.description:
Optional moderator biography or self-description.

This free-form text field (maximum 500 characters) allows moderators to provide information about themselves, their background, areas of expertise, or moderation philosophy. The bio is displayed on the moderator's public profile if profile_visibility allows.

Basic text formatting such as line breaks is preserved, but HTML tags are stripped to prevent XSS attacks.

location.description:
Optional geographic location of the moderator.

This is a free-text field (maximum 100 characters) where moderators can specify their city, country, region, or any geographic identifier they wish to share. No geocoding or validation is performed - it is purely informational and displayed on the moderator's public profile.

Location information helps community members understand moderator perspectives and time zones for moderation coverage.

website_url.description:
Optional personal or professional website URL.

Moderators can provide a link to their personal website, professional profile, or institutional affiliation. The URL must be properly formatted with http:// or https:// protocol and is displayed as a clickable link on the moderator's public profile.

This field enables moderators to share their credentials, background information, or other platforms where they are active, building trust with the community.

profile_picture_url.description:
URL of the moderator's profile picture.

This URL points to the moderator's avatar image, which is displayed in moderation interfaces, action logs, and when the moderator participates in discussions. If null, the system displays a default moderator avatar.

The profile picture helps humanize moderator interactions and provides visual identification in the community.

email_verified.description:
Indicates whether the moderator's email address has been verified.

Email verification is required before a moderator can perform moderation actions. The verification process involves sending a verification email with a unique token link that the moderator must click to confirm email ownership.

This field is set to false upon account creation and updated to true when the email verification link is successfully validated. Moderators with unverified emails have restricted access until verification is completed.

status.description:
Current status of the moderator account.

This field controls account lifecycle and access permissions. Valid status values include pending_email_verification for newly created accounts awaiting email confirmation, active for verified accounts in good standing with full moderation access, suspended for temporarily disabled accounts due to policy violations or administrative action, and deleted for accounts that have been soft-deleted and are pending permanent removal.

Status transitions are tracked and logged for audit purposes. Status changes affect authentication eligibility and permission grants throughout the system.

moderation_permissions.description:
JSON string defining specific moderation permissions and access levels.

This field contains a JSON-encoded object that specifies granular moderation capabilities for this moderator account. Permissions may include can_edit_articles, can_delete_articles, can_edit_comments, can_delete_comments, can_issue_warnings, can_suspend_users, can_ban_users, can_manage_reports, and can_manage_categories.

The JSON structure allows flexible permission management without database schema changes, supporting role-based access control and differentiated moderator capabilities. Permission checks are performed at the application layer when moderators attempt to execute moderation actions.

profile_visibility.description:
Controls who can view this moderator's profile information.

Valid values include public for profiles visible to all users including guests, members_only for profiles visible only to authenticated members and other moderators, and private for profiles visible only to other moderators and system administrators.

This privacy setting determines access to the moderator's profile page, bio, location, website, and other personal information. It does not affect the visibility of moderation actions or official moderator posts.

activity_visibility.description:
Controls who can view this moderator's activity history.

Valid values include public for activity visible to all users including guests, members_only for activity visible only to authenticated members and other moderators, and hidden for activity not displayed on the profile but still accessible through content search.

Activity visibility affects the display of the moderator's articles and comments on their profile page. Moderation actions are logged separately and are not controlled by this setting.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the moderator's most recent successful login.

This field is automatically updated each time the moderator successfully authenticates. It is used for account security monitoring, inactive account detection, and auditing moderator activity patterns.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information (stored as timestamptz in database). A null value indicates the moderator has never logged in since account creation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was originally created.

This is an immutable field set automatically during account registration. It is used for calculating account age, sorting moderators by seniority, and audit trail purposes.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, representing the exact moment the moderator record was inserted into the discussion_board_moderators table.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator profile was last modified.

This field is automatically updated whenever any moderator account information changes, including profile edits, password changes, permission updates, or status changes. It helps track account maintenance activity and identify stale or inactive accounts.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, representing the most recent modification to any field in the moderator record.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the moderator account.

When a moderator account is deleted, this field is set to the deletion timestamp rather than removing the record entirely. This enables account recovery during a grace period, maintains audit trail integrity for moderation actions, and preserves referential integrity for historical records.

A null value indicates the account is active. A non-null value indicates the account is soft-deleted and should be excluded from active moderator lists and prevented from authenticating. Permanent deletion may occur after a retention period.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized.description:
Response payload for successful moderator authentication or token refresh.

This type represents the complete authentication response returned when a moderator successfully logs in or refreshes their session tokens. It contains the moderator's essential profile information along with JWT tokens required for subsequent authenticated API requests.

The response provides everything a client application needs to establish and maintain an authenticated moderator session, including identity information for UI display and security tokens for API authorization. The included profile data reflects the moderator's current account state from the discussion_board_moderators table.

This structure is returned by both login operations (where a new session is created) and refresh operations (where an existing session is extended with new tokens). The moderator's full set of permissions is embedded in the JWT access token claims and enforced by the backend for all protected operations.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ILogin.description:
Login credentials for moderator authentication.

This schema defines the request body for moderator login operations. Moderators can authenticate using either their username or email address along with their password. The system performs case-insensitive lookup for username/email to improve usability.

Security measures include rate limiting (maximum 5 failed attempts within 15 minutes), generic error messages to prevent username enumeration, and validation that the account's email is verified and status is active before allowing login.

Upon successful authentication, the system validates the password against the stored password_hash, updates the last_login_at timestamp, creates a session record in discussion_board_moderator_sessions, and returns JWT tokens for subsequent authenticated requests.

username_or_email.description:
Username or email address for moderator identification during authentication.

This field provides flexible authentication by accepting either the moderator's unique username or their registered email address. The system performs case-insensitive lookup against both the username and email columns in the discussion_board_moderators table to find the matching account, improving user experience by allowing moderators to log in with whichever identifier they remember.

When a username is provided, it must match the format requirements of 3-30 characters containing only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens as defined in the Prisma schema and enforced during account registration. When an email address is provided, it must follow standard email format with @ symbol and valid domain structure.

The system validates the provided credential exists in the discussion_board_moderators table without revealing whether it's a username or email. For security, error messages remain generic ("Invalid username/email or password") to prevent account enumeration attacks where malicious actors could determine which usernames or emails are registered.

This dual-credential authentication approach balances security with usability, enabling moderators to use their preferred login identifier while maintaining protection against enumeration attacks through consistent error messaging regardless of which credential type fails validation.

password.description:
Password for moderator account authentication.

This is the plain text password provided by the moderator for verification. The system compares this against the stored password_hash using secure hashing comparison. Passwords are never stored or transmitted in plain text after this point.

For security reasons, incorrect password errors are generic and do not reveal whether the username/email exists or the password was wrong, preventing account enumeration attacks.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking.

This is an optional field that the client may provide for server-side rendering scenarios. If not provided, the server will extract the IP address from the HTTP request headers.

The IP address is recorded in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table for security auditing, detecting suspicious login patterns, and implementing IP-based rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks.

href.description:
Connection URL where the login is being performed.

This is the current page URL from which the moderator is initiating the login request. It represents the location in the application where authentication is taking place.

This value is stored in the href field of the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table and is used for session tracking, analytics, and security monitoring to understand login patterns and detect potential unauthorized access attempts.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the login page.

This is the previous page URL that directed the user to the login interface. It helps track the user's navigation path and can be used to redirect users back to their intended destination after successful authentication.

This value is stored in the referrer field of the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table for analytics and user experience optimization, allowing the system to understand how users arrive at the login page.

refresh_token.description:
The refresh token issued during the previous login or token refresh operation.

This token is long-lived (30 days expiration) and is used to obtain new access tokens when the short-lived access token expires. The refresh token must be valid, not expired, and not revoked. It contains the moderator's identity and is verified against the server's token store.

Refresh tokens are invalidated when the moderator changes their password, when the account is suspended or deleted, or when the moderator explicitly logs out from all devices.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRefresh.description:
Request payload for refreshing an expired access token.

This type represents the data required to refresh authentication tokens for a moderator. When the access token expires after 30 minutes, clients use this request to obtain a new access token without requiring the user to re-enter credentials. The refresh operation maintains continuous authenticated sessions while keeping access tokens short-lived for security.

The refresh token is the only required field and serves as proof of previous successful authentication. The system validates this token to ensure it hasn't expired, been revoked, or been invalidated due to security events like password changes or account suspension.

This operation does not create a new session record in discussion_board_moderator_sessions, as it extends an existing authenticated session rather than establishing a new one.

search.description:
Keyword search query for filtering categories by name or description.

When provided, the system searches for categories where the search term appears in the category name or description fields using case-insensitive partial matching. This enables users to quickly find relevant categories using natural language queries.

For example, searching for "economic" would match categories with names like "Economic Policy" or descriptions mentioning economic topics. The search uses PostgreSQL trigram matching for fuzzy matching capabilities.

If null or omitted, no keyword filtering is applied and all categories matching other criteria are returned.

name.description:
Exact or partial match filter for category name.

Filters categories based on the category name field from the discussion_board_categories table. Supports partial matching, so searching for "Policy" would match "Economic Policy", "Public Policy", "Fiscal Policy", etc.

Category names are human-readable labels displayed in the UI and used for primary category identification. This filter is case-insensitive and uses PostgreSQL's pattern matching capabilities.

If null or omitted, categories are not filtered by name.

slug.description:
Exact match filter for category slug.

Filters categories by their URL-friendly slug identifier. Slugs are unique, lowercase, hyphenated versions of category names (e.g., "economic-policy", "political-analysis") used in routes and permalinks for SEO-friendly URLs.

This filter performs exact matching as slugs are precise identifiers. It's typically used when looking up a specific category by its URL parameter or when validating category references.

If null or omitted, categories are not filtered by slug.

created_after.description:
Filter for categories created after the specified timestamp.

When provided, only categories with created_at timestamps later than this value are included in results. This enables filtering for recently added categories or finding categories created within a specific time window when combined with created_before.

The timestamp should be in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. This filter is inclusive of the exact timestamp provided.

If null or omitted, no lower bound is applied to the creation date filter.

created_before.description:
Filter for categories created before the specified timestamp.

When provided, only categories with created_at timestamps earlier than this value are included in results. Combined with created_after, this enables precise date range filtering for category discovery.

The timestamp should be in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. This filter is inclusive of the exact timestamp provided.

If null or omitted, no upper bound is applied to the creation date filter.

sort_by.description:
Field name to sort results by.

Specifies which category field to use for ordering the results. Valid values include "name" for alphabetical sorting, "created_at" for chronological sorting by creation date, "updated_at" for sorting by modification date, and "slug" for slug-based alphabetical ordering.

The sort field works in conjunction with sort_order to determine the final result ordering. If not specified, results are sorted by created_at in descending order by default (newest categories first).

If null or omitted, default sorting is applied.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for ordering results.

Specifies whether results should be sorted in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order based on the sort_by field. "asc" means smallest to largest, oldest to newest, or A to Z. "desc" means largest to smallest, newest to oldest, or Z to A.

Valid values are "asc" and "desc". If not specified, "desc" is used by default, showing newest or highest values first.

If null or omitted, descending order is applied by default.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve when the result set is larger than the page size. Page numbers are 1-indexed, where page 1 is the first page of results. This works in conjunction with the limit parameter to implement offset-based pagination.

For example, with limit=20, page=1 returns results 1-20, page=2 returns results 21-40, etc. If the requested page number exceeds the total number of pages, an empty result set is returned.

If null or omitted, defaults to page 1.

limit.description:
Number of categories to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, determining how many category records are included in a single response. Valid values range from 1 to 100, with a typical default of 20 categories per page.

Larger page sizes reduce the number of requests needed to retrieve all results but increase response payload size and processing time. Smaller page sizes enable faster initial responses and more granular pagination.

If null or omitted, defaults to 20 categories per page.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for retrieving discussion board categories.

This type defines the complete set of query parameters available for searching, filtering, sorting, and paginating the category list. It enables flexible category discovery through multiple search dimensions including keyword search across names and descriptions, exact slug matching, date range filtering, and customizable result ordering.

The request supports various use cases such as category selection interfaces during article creation, category browsing for content discovery, category management in administrative interfaces, and validation of category references. All parameters are optional, allowing for simple unfiltered category lists or complex multi-criteria searches.

Pagination parameters (page and limit) control result set size and enable efficient handling of the category taxonomy even as it grows. Sorting parameters (sort_by and sort_order) provide flexibility in how categories are presented, whether alphabetically by name, chronologically by creation date, or by other relevant criteria.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an article category for reference in article listings and navigation.

This lightweight DTO provides essential category information for display in article metadata, category browsing interfaces, and filtering controls. Categories are part of the systematic taxonomy structure that organizes economic and political discussion topics.

Used extensively in article summaries to show which categories an article belongs to, enabling users to understand the topical context and navigate to related content.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the category.

This UUID serves as the primary key and is used to reference the category in article-category relationships and API endpoints for category-based article filtering.

name.description:
Category display name shown in the user interface.

This is the human-readable label such as 'Economic Policy', 'Political Analysis', or 'International Trade'. The name must be unique across all categories and is used in navigation menus, article metadata displays, and category browsing pages.

slug.description:
URL-friendly identifier derived from the category name.

Used in routes and permalinks to create SEO-friendly URLs like '/categories/economic-policy'. The slug is unique, typically lowercase with hyphens replacing spaces, and provides human-readable category URLs for better user experience and search engine optimization.

description.description:
Detailed explanation of the category's purpose and scope.

This optional field provides context to help users and content creators understand what types of articles belong in this category. It guides appropriate categorization and helps users discover content aligned with their interests. The description may include examples of topics covered, boundaries with related categories, or guidelines for content classification.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this category was originally created.

This is automatically set by the system when the category record is first inserted into the discussion_board_categories table. It provides an immutable historical record of when this category was added to the taxonomy. The timestamp is stored in UTC with timezone information preserved.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this category was last modified.

This is automatically updated by the system whenever any field in the category record is changed (name, description, or slug updates). It provides an audit trail for category management and helps track when taxonomy changes occurred. The timestamp is stored in UTC with timezone information preserved.

id.description:
Primary unique identifier for the category.

This is a system-generated UUID that uniquely identifies each category across the discussion board. It is immutable once created and serves as the stable reference for category relationships in the discussion_board_article_categories junction table.

name.description:
Category display name shown in the user interface.

This is the human-readable label for the category (e.g., 'Economic Policy', 'Political Analysis'). It must be unique across all categories and is used for display in article creation forms, category browsing pages, and article metadata. The name should clearly convey the topic area covered by this category.

description.description:
Detailed explanation of the category's purpose and scope.

This optional field provides context to help users and content creators understand what types of articles belong in this category. It guides appropriate categorization and helps users discover content aligned with their interests. The description may include examples of topics covered, boundaries with related categories, or guidelines for content classification.

slug.description:
URL-friendly identifier derived from the category name.

This is a unique, lowercase, hyphenated string used in routes and permalinks for SEO-friendly URLs (e.g., 'economic-policy', 'political-analysis'). The slug is typically generated from the name but can be customized. It must be unique across all categories and remains stable even if the category name is updated.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this category was originally created.

This is automatically set by the system when the category record is first inserted into the discussion_board_categories table. It provides an immutable historical record of when this category was added to the taxonomy. The timestamp is stored in UTC with timezone information preserved.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this category was last modified.

This is automatically updated by the system whenever any field in the category record is changed (name, description, or slug updates). It provides an audit trail for category management and helps track when taxonomy changes occurred. The timestamp is stored in UTC with timezone information preserved.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.description:
Complete category entity representing an article category in the discussion board taxonomy.

Categories provide the primary organizational structure for economic and political discussion topics. They enable users to browse articles by subject area and help content creators classify their articles appropriately. Each category has a unique name and slug, with an optional description explaining its scope and purpose.

Categories are managed by moderators who can create, update, and organize the taxonomy as the discussion board evolves. Articles associate with categories through the many-to-many relationship in the discussion_board_article_categories junction table, allowing articles to belong to multiple categories for flexible organization.

This entity corresponds to the discussion_board_categories table in the Prisma schema and supports the category-based content organization and discovery features specified in the Article Management and Search and Discovery requirements documents.

name.description:
Category display name to be shown in user interfaces.

Human-readable label representing the subject area of this new category, such as 'Economic Policy', 'Political Analysis', or 'International Trade'. This name will appear in category selection dropdowns during article creation, in category browsing pages, and throughout the discussion board navigation.

The name must be unique across all existing categories to prevent confusion and ensure clear content organization. The system validates name uniqueness before creating the category record, rejecting creation attempts if a category with the same name already exists.

Choose descriptive, clear names that accurately represent the scope of discussions expected in this category. Names should be concise yet informative, helping both content creators and readers understand the category's purpose at a glance.

description.description:
Detailed explanation of the category's purpose, scope, and content guidelines.

Provides comprehensive information helping users understand what types of articles and discussions belong in this category, the boundaries of the subject area, examples of appropriate topics, and guidance for proper categorization. This description will appear on category browsing pages and may be shown as tooltips or help text in article creation interfaces.

While optional, providing a clear description is highly recommended for categories that might be ambiguous or that cover specialized subject areas. Good descriptions help content creators select the most appropriate category for their articles and help readers understand what to expect when browsing the category.

The description can be omitted (set to null) for self-explanatory categories where the name alone clearly conveys the scope, such as 'General Discussion'.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new article category in the discussion board system.

This schema defines the data required to create a new category in the primary taxonomy structure for organizing economic and political discussion topics. Categories are fundamental to content organization, enabling users to browse articles systematically by subject area and facilitating content discovery through category-based filtering and navigation.

The creation request accepts a category display name and an optional detailed description. The system automatically generates additional fields during category creation, including a unique UUID identifier, a URL-friendly slug derived from the name for SEO-optimized routing, and timestamps marking creation and last update times. These auto-generated fields are managed by the backend and not included in the request body.

Category creation is restricted to moderators only, as category management shapes the entire content taxonomy and is an administrative function. The moderator's identity is captured from the authentication context (JWT token) rather than being supplied in the request body. The system validates that the provided category name is unique across all existing categories, rejecting creation attempts if a duplicate name is detected. This ensures unambiguous category identification and prevents user confusion during article categorization and browsing workflows.

Once created, the category becomes immediately available in article creation and editing interfaces, allowing members to classify their articles under this new subject area. The category also appears in browsing views, search filters, and navigation menus, integrated into the content discovery system defined in the Search and Discovery requirements.

name.description:
Updated category display name.

When provided, this updates the human-readable label for the category. The new name must be unique across all categories. If the name is changed significantly, the system may regenerate the slug to maintain URL-friendliness and SEO alignment.

The name should clearly convey the topic area and help users understand what content belongs in this category. Examples include 'Economic Policy', 'Political Analysis', 'International Trade'.

description.description:
Updated detailed explanation of the category's purpose and scope.

When provided, this updates the description that helps users understand what types of articles belong in this category. The description can be set to null to remove it, or updated with new text to refine the category's definition.

Updating the description is useful when refining category boundaries, adding examples of appropriate content, or clarifying the distinction between similar categories.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for modifying an existing category in the discussion board taxonomy.

This DTO enables moderators to refine category definitions, correct naming issues, or expand category descriptions as the discussion board evolves and community needs change. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates to modify only the specific aspects that need changing.

When a category is updated, the changes apply immediately to all article displays, category browsing pages, and search filters. Existing article-category associations in the discussion_board_article_categories junction table remain intact, so articles already in this category continue to be associated with it under the updated name or description.

The operation validates that updated names don't conflict with existing categories and maintains data integrity across the taxonomy system. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time when any changes are saved.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

This specifies which page of results to retrieve in the paginated result set. The first page is numbered 1, not 0. If omitted, defaults to page 1.

Pagination enables efficient browsing of large result sets by dividing articles into manageable chunks, improving performance and user experience.

limit.description:
Number of articles to return per page.

This controls the page size for pagination, with a minimum of 1 and maximum of 100 articles per page. Common values are 10, 20, 50, or 100. If omitted, defaults to 20 articles per page as specified in the performance requirements.

Larger page sizes reduce the number of requests needed to browse many articles but increase response payload size and load time. Smaller page sizes load faster but require more requests for extensive browsing.

search.description:
Keyword search query for filtering articles by title and body content.

When provided, this performs full-text search across article titles and body content using PostgreSQL trigram indexes. The search is case-insensitive and supports partial word matching, so searching for 'econom' matches 'economics', 'economy', 'economic', etc.

Multiple keywords separated by spaces are treated as AND conditions, returning only articles that contain all the keywords anywhere in the searchable content. Title matches are ranked higher than body content matches in the relevance-based result ordering.

The search respects the maximum query length of 200 characters and minimum length of 2 characters as defined in the Search and Discovery requirements.

category_slugs.description:
Array of category slug identifiers for filtering articles by categories.

When provided, this filters the article list to include only articles that belong to any of the specified categories (OR condition). Category slugs are URL-friendly identifiers like 'economic-policy', 'political-analysis', 'international-trade'.

This enables category-based content discovery, allowing users to narrow results to specific topic areas within economic and political discourse. The filter works by joining with the discussion_board_article_categories junction table and matching the category slugs.

tag_slugs.description:
Array of tag slug identifiers for filtering articles by tags.

When provided, this filters the article list to include only articles that have all of the specified tags applied (AND condition). Tag slugs are URL-friendly identifiers like 'monetary-policy', 'healthcare-reform', 'climate-policy'.

This enables granular topic-based filtering, allowing users to find articles on very specific subjects within the broader category taxonomy. The filter works by joining with the discussion_board_article_tags junction table and matching the tag slugs.

author_username.description:
Username of the article author for filtering articles by specific member.

When provided, this filters the article list to include only articles authored by the member with the specified username. This enables users to explore all content created by a particular author, useful for following specific writers or researchers in the discussion board.

The filter matches against the discussion_board_member_id foreign key by first resolving the username to a member ID through the discussion_board_members table.

status.description:
Publication status filter for articles.

When provided, this filters articles by their current status. Valid values are 'published' (publicly visible articles), 'draft' (unpublished articles visible only to authors), and 'archived' (older articles moved to archive status).

For guest and member users, only 'published' articles should be accessible. For members viewing their own articles, they can filter to see their drafts. For moderators, all statuses are accessible for moderation purposes.

created_after.description:
Filter for articles created on or after this timestamp.

When provided, this limits results to articles where created_at is greater than or equal to this date-time value. This enables date range filtering such as 'articles from the last month' or 'articles published this year'.

The timestamp should be in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. This filter is often combined with created_before to define a specific date range.

created_before.description:
Filter for articles created on or before this timestamp.

When provided, this limits results to articles where created_at is less than or equal to this date-time value. This enables date range filtering when combined with created_after.

The timestamp should be in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. This is useful for finding articles published during specific time periods or before certain dates.

min_view_count.description:
Minimum view count threshold for filtering articles.

When provided, this filters the article list to include only articles with view_count greater than or equal to this value. This enables discovery of popular or widely-read articles that have attracted significant readership.

This can be combined with max_view_count to define a view count range, useful for finding moderately popular articles or filtering out both very new articles and viral posts.

max_view_count.description:
Maximum view count threshold for filtering articles.

When provided, this filters the article list to include only articles with view_count less than or equal to this value. This can be used to find newer or less-discovered articles when combined with min_view_count.

min_comment_count.description:
Minimum comment count threshold for filtering articles.

When provided, this filters the article list to include only articles with comment_count greater than or equal to this value. This enables discovery of highly discussed articles that have generated significant community engagement.

Finding articles with many comments helps users locate active discussions and controversial topics that are generating debate.

max_comment_count.description:
Maximum comment count threshold for filtering articles.

When provided, this filters the article list to include only articles with comment_count less than or equal to this value. This can be used to find articles with moderate discussion levels when combined with min_comment_count.

has_images.description:
Filter for articles with image attachments.

When set to true, this filters the article list to include only articles that have at least one associated image attachment in the discussion_board_article_images table (where deleted_at IS NULL).

This is useful for users looking for visually-supported content such as articles with charts, graphs, or infographics that provide visual evidence for economic or political arguments.

has_documents.description:
Filter for articles with document attachments.

When set to true, this filters the article list to include only articles that have at least one associated document attachment in the discussion_board_article_documents table (where deleted_at IS NULL).

This helps users find articles with supporting research materials, policy documents, or data files that provide additional context and evidence.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort articles by.

This specifies which metric to use for ordering the article results. Available options are:
- 'created_at': Sort by publication date (newest or oldest first based on sort_order)
- 'updated_at': Sort by last modification date (recently updated first)
- 'view_count': Sort by popularity based on number of views
- 'comment_count': Sort by discussion activity based on number of comments
- 'relevance': Sort by search relevance score (only applicable when search keywords are provided)

The default is 'created_at' when no search keywords are provided, or 'relevance' when keyword search is active.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for ordering results.

This specifies whether to sort in ascending (oldest/lowest first) or descending (newest/highest first) order. Valid values are:
- 'asc': Ascending order (oldest dates first, lowest counts first)
- 'desc': Descending order (newest dates first, highest counts first)

The default is 'desc' for most sort fields (newest first, most viewed first, most commented first). For relevance-based sorting, this parameter is ignored as relevance always uses descending order (most relevant first).

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request parameters for article discovery and listing.

This DTO enables comprehensive article search functionality combining keyword search, category and tag filtering, author filtering, date range constraints, engagement metrics, attachment presence, sorting options, and pagination. It supports the advanced content discovery features specified in the Search and Discovery requirements.

All parameters are optional, allowing flexible query construction from simple browsing (no filters) to highly specific searches (multiple combined filters). When no filters are applied, the operation returns all published articles in the default sort order. The request body is used with PATCH method to support complex search criteria that would exceed URL length limits if passed as query parameters.

This request structure is used across multiple search operations including general article search, category-specific article listing, tag-specific article listing, and member-specific article listing. The same comprehensive filtering capabilities apply in all contexts with appropriate scope filtering (category, tag, or author) added by the operation.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a discussion board article optimized for list views and embeddings.

This lightweight DTO provides essential article information for display in article listings, search results, and category browsing without the overhead of full content and nested relationships. It includes contextual references to the author and categories to provide necessary context while maintaining performance.

Designed for efficient data transfer in paginated lists where dozens of articles may be displayed simultaneously, this summary excludes heavy fields like full body content, complete snapshots history, and attachment arrays.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the article.

This UUID serves as the primary key and is used in article URLs, API endpoints, and as a reference in related entities like comments, snapshots, and attachments.

title.description:
Article title displayed prominently in listings and article pages.

The title serves as the primary identifier for users browsing content. It is validated to be between 5 and 200 characters, trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace, and must contain meaningful alphanumeric content to prevent titles consisting only of special characters.

summary.description:
Optional brief summary or excerpt of the article, maximum 500 characters.

When provided, this summary is displayed in article listings and previews to help users quickly assess article relevance. If not provided by the author, list views may display the first 200 characters of the body content instead.

status.description:
Publication status of the article.

Indicates the current lifecycle state of the article. Valid values are 'published' for publicly visible articles, 'draft' for unpublished articles being prepared, and 'archived' for articles removed from active circulation but retained for historical purposes.

This status controls article visibility in public listings and search results, with only 'published' articles appearing to regular users.

view_count.description:
Total number of times this article has been viewed.

Incremented each time a user accesses the article page. This metric provides engagement feedback to authors and helps identify popular content. The count includes views from all user types (guests, members, and moderators).

comment_count.description:
Cached count of comments associated with this article.

Maintained as a denormalized field for performance, updated when comments are added or soft-deleted. This count is displayed in article listings to indicate discussion activity level and help users find active conversations.

author.description:
Summary information about the member who authored this article.

Provides essential author context including username, display name, and profile information. This reference enables users to understand who created the content and navigate to the author's profile for more articles and information.

The author reference uses ISummary to prevent circular expansion and maintain performance in list views.

categories.description:
Array of categories this article is classified under.

Articles can belong to multiple categories for flexible organization (e.g., an article might be categorized under both 'Economic Policy' and 'International Trade'). Categories provide the primary taxonomy structure for content browsing and discovery.

Each category reference includes basic information like name and slug, allowing users to filter and navigate to category-specific article lists.

tags.description:
Array of topic tags applied to this article for detailed classification.

Tags provide granular, user-generated keywords that complement the formal category structure (e.g., 'monetary-policy', 'climate-change', 'taxation'). Articles can have up to 5 tags as per business requirements.

Tags enable detailed content filtering and topic-based discovery, allowing users to find articles on specific subtopics within broader categories.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the article was originally created.

This immutable timestamp marks the article's publication time and is used for chronological sorting in article listings. Displayed to users as relative time ('2 hours ago') or absolute date depending on context.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the article was last modified.

Updated whenever the article content, title, category, tags, or other editable fields are changed. When displayed alongside created_at, this helps users identify articles that have been revised or updated after initial publication.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the article.

When set to a timestamp, indicates the article has been soft-deleted and is hidden from public view but retained for audit purposes. A null value indicates the article is active and publicly accessible.

This field is particularly important for moderation contexts where moderators need to review deleted articles, understand deletion history, and potentially restore articles that were removed in error. In public list views, articles with non-null deleted_at are filtered out, but the field is included in the summary schema to support moderation dashboards and audit interfaces.

IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary.description:
Lightweight representation of a discussion board member for efficient embedding in lists and references.

This summary view provides essential member identification and display information without the full profile details. It is optimized for contexts where basic member information is needed, such as showing article authors, comment authors, or report submitters.

The summary includes only the most frequently displayed fields: unique identifier, username, optional display name, and profile picture. It excludes sensitive information like email addresses, privacy settings, and detailed profile data.

This type is used throughout the system for member references in articles, comments, reports, and activity displays, ensuring consistent lightweight member representation with minimal data payload.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this member.

This UUID serves as the primary key and is used across all system components to reference this specific member. It remains constant throughout the member's account lifecycle.

username.description:
Unique username for member identification.

The username is the member's primary public identifier, used for login, mentions, and public display. It must be 3-30 characters, containing only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens.

Usernames are unique across all members and case-insensitive for consistency.

display_name.description:
Optional display name shown publicly instead of username.

When provided, the display name is shown in user interfaces instead of the username for a more personalized presentation. Limited to 50 characters and can contain any characters except control characters.

If null, the username is used for all public displays.

profile_picture_url.description:
URL of the member's profile picture.

Provides the avatar image displayed alongside the member's content and in user interfaces. The URL points to a processed and optimized image stored in the system's file storage.

If null, a default avatar should be displayed by client applications.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve in the paginated response. Page numbering starts at 1 for the first page. This parameter works in conjunction with the limit parameter to control result pagination.

For example, with limit=20, page=1 returns items 1-20, page=2 returns items 21-40, and so on. When not specified, defaults to page 1.

limit.description:
Number of items per page.

Specifies how many tag records to return in a single page of results. This controls the size of the paginated response and affects both performance and user experience.

Typical values range from 10 to 100 items per page. Smaller page sizes provide faster response times and are suitable for mobile devices, while larger page sizes reduce the number of requests needed to browse many tags. When not specified, defaults to a reasonable value such as 20 or 50 items per page.

search.description:
Keyword search term for filtering tags by name.

Enables partial matching search against tag names using case-insensitive comparison. The search supports substring matching, so searching for 'econom' will return tags like 'economic-policy', 'economics', and 'macroeconomics'.

This parameter leverages the PostgreSQL trigram index on the discussion_board_tags.name field for efficient full-text search performance. Useful for users exploring the tag taxonomy or looking for specific topics within the economic and political discussion space.

oneOf.description:
Sorting criterion for ordering tag results.

Determines how the returned tags are ordered in the response. Available sorting options include:

- name_asc: Alphabetically by tag name (A to Z), useful for browsing the complete tag list
- name_desc: Reverse alphabetically by tag name (Z to A)
- created_at_asc: Chronologically by creation date (oldest first), useful for finding established tags
- created_at_desc: Reverse chronologically by creation date (newest first), useful for discovering new topics
- usage_desc: By popularity based on article count (most used first), useful for finding trending discussion topics

When not specified, defaults to a logical ordering such as usage_desc to highlight popular tags or name_asc for alphabetical browsing.
