created_after.description:
Filter tags created after this timestamp.

Restricts results to tags that were created after the specified date and time. This parameter is useful for discovering newly added tags or tracking tag creation over time.

The timestamp should be provided in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. This parameter can be combined with created_before to define a specific date range for tag creation.

created_before.description:
Filter tags created before this timestamp.

Restricts results to tags that were created before the specified date and time. This parameter is useful for historical tag analysis or excluding recently created tags from results.

The timestamp should be provided in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. This parameter can be combined with created_after to define a specific date range for tag creation.

IDiscussionBoardTag.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for tag retrieval.

This request schema defines the query parameters used to search, filter, sort, and paginate through discussion board tags. Tags are flexible topic labels that provide granular keyword-based organization complementing the formal category structure defined in discussion_board_categories.

The request supports pagination through page and limit parameters, enabling efficient browsing of large tag collections. Search functionality allows partial name matching to help users discover relevant tags. Multiple sorting options enable users to browse tags alphabetically, chronologically, or by popularity.

Date range filtering through created_after and created_before parameters enables temporal analysis of tag creation patterns, useful for identifying emerging discussion topics or tracking the evolution of the tag taxonomy over time.

IDiscussionBoardTag.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a discussion topic tag for reference in article listings and tag browsing.

This lightweight DTO provides essential tag information for display in article metadata, tag clouds, and filtering interfaces. Tags are user-generated keywords that provide granular topic classification beyond the formal category structure.

Tags enable detailed content discovery, allowing users to find articles on specific subtopics like 'monetary-policy', 'healthcare-reform', or 'climate-change' within broader categories.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the tag.

This UUID serves as the primary key and is used to reference the tag in article-tag relationships and API endpoints for tag-based article filtering and discovery.

name.description:
Tag name normalized to lowercase for consistency.

This is the keyword used for tagging and filtering, such as 'monetary-policy', 'healthcare-reform', or 'taxation'. Tags are normalized to lowercase to prevent duplicate tags with different capitalization (e.g., 'Economics' and 'economics' become the same tag).

The name must be unique and is displayed in tag clouds, article metadata, and tag-based browsing interfaces.

slug.description:
URL-friendly identifier derived from the tag name.

Used in routes and permalinks to create SEO-friendly URLs for tag-based browsing like '/tags/monetary-policy'. The slug is unique and provides human-readable tag URLs for better navigation and search engine optimization.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this tag was first created in the discussion board system.

This value is automatically set by the system when the tag record is initially inserted into the discussion_board_tags table and remains immutable throughout the tag's lifecycle. It provides an audit trail showing when each tag was added to the taxonomy and helps track the evolution of discussion topics over time.

The timestamp is stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, typically in UTC. This field is useful for displaying tag age to users (e.g., 'tag created 2 weeks ago'), sorting tags by creation date to find newest or oldest tags, and analyzing temporal patterns in tag creation to identify emerging discussion topics in economic and political discourse.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this tag was last modified.

This value is automatically updated by the system whenever the tag record is edited, such as when the tag name is changed, the slug is regenerated, or the tag is merged with another tag. For newly created tags, this timestamp initially matches the created_at value.

The timestamp is stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, typically in UTC. This field helps track tag maintenance activity, identify recently updated tags, and maintain audit trails for taxonomy management operations. When displayed alongside created_at, it reveals whether a tag has been modified since its initial creation, indicating active curation of the tag taxonomy.

name.description:
Updated tag name for the discussion board tag.

This field allows moderators to modify the display label of an existing tag. When updated, the system will normalize the new name to lowercase for consistency, validate that the new name is unique across all tags (no other tag has the same normalized name), and regenerate the URL-friendly slug if the name changes.

Updating the tag name affects how the tag appears in the UI, search results, and article metadata across the entire discussion board. All articles currently associated with this tag through the discussion_board_article_tags junction table maintain their relationship, ensuring continuity of tag-based content organization.

The name must be between 2 and 30 characters in length. This field is optional in update operations, allowing partial updates where only specified fields are modified.

IDiscussionBoardTag.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing tag in the discussion board system.

This DTO enables moderators to modify properties of an existing tag identified by its slug. All fields are optional, following the partial update pattern where only provided fields are modified while others remain unchanged.

When the tag name is updated, the system performs several automated operations including normalizing the name to lowercase, validating uniqueness across all existing tags, and regenerating the URL-friendly slug to maintain SEO-friendly URLs. These updates immediately reflect across all areas of the discussion board where the tag appears.

Tag updates are typically performed to refine the tag taxonomy, merge similar tags by updating one tag's name to match another (followed by cleanup), correct naming inconsistencies, or improve the SEO-friendliness of tag slugs. All articles currently tagged with this tag maintain their association, ensuring no disruption to tag-based content organization and discovery.

id.description:
Primary key uniquely identifying this tag in the discussion board system.

This is a system-generated UUID assigned at tag creation time and remains immutable throughout the tag's lifecycle.

name.description:
Tag name normalized to lowercase for consistency.

This field represents the display label for the tag as it appears in the UI, search results, and article metadata. Tag names are normalized to lowercase to prevent duplicate tags with different capitalization (e.g., 'Monetary-Policy' and 'monetary-policy' are treated as the same tag).

Tag names must be unique across the entire system and typically represent specific topics within economic and political discourse such as 'monetary-policy', 'climate-change', 'taxation', 'healthcare-reform', or 'international-trade'.

slug.description:
URL-friendly identifier derived from the tag name.

The slug is used in routes, permalinks, and tag browsing pages to create SEO-friendly URLs. It is automatically generated from the tag name by converting to lowercase, replacing spaces and special characters with hyphens, and ensuring uniqueness across all tags.

Example: A tag named 'Monetary Policy' would generate a slug 'monetary-policy', resulting in URLs like '/tags/monetary-policy'.

The slug is unique across all tags and provides stable, readable URLs for tag-based content discovery.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this tag was first created in the discussion board system.

This value is automatically set by the system when the tag is initially added and remains immutable. It provides an audit trail showing when each tag entered the system's taxonomy.

The timestamp is stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, typically in UTC.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this tag was last modified.

This value is automatically updated by the system whenever the tag is edited, such as when the name is changed, the slug is regenerated, or the tag is merged with another tag.

The timestamp is stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, typically in UTC. For newly created tags, this will initially match the created_at timestamp.

IDiscussionBoardTag.description:
Complete representation of a discussion board tag entity.

Tags provide flexible, user-generated keywords that complement the formal category structure in the discussion board. They enable granular content filtering and discovery on economic and political topics, allowing users to find articles tagged with specific keywords like 'monetary-policy', 'climate-change', 'taxation', or 'healthcare-reform'.

Tags are normalized to lowercase for consistency and uniqueness, preventing duplicate tags with different capitalization. Each tag has a URL-friendly slug used in routes and permalinks for SEO optimization. Tags are referenced by articles through the discussion_board_article_tags junction table, establishing many-to-many relationships.

This type is used when returning complete tag information in responses, such as when listing all tags, viewing tag details, or displaying tags associated with articles.

name.description:
Tag name to be created in the discussion board system.

This is the display label for the tag as it will appear in the UI, search results, and article metadata. The name should represent a specific topic within economic and political discourse such as 'Monetary Policy', 'Climate Change', 'Taxation', 'Healthcare Reform', or 'International Trade'.

The system will automatically normalize this name to lowercase for consistency and storage. Tag names must be unique across the entire discussion board to prevent duplicate tags.

The name must be between 2 and 30 characters in length and should use alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores. Spaces are allowed in the input but will be converted to hyphens during slug generation.

IDiscussionBoardTag.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new tag in the discussion board system.

This DTO contains the minimal information required to create a new tag. The tag name is the only required field, as other properties like the slug, ID, and timestamps are automatically generated by the system.

The system will normalize the provided tag name to lowercase to prevent duplicate tags with different capitalization, validate uniqueness across all existing tags, and generate a URL-friendly slug derived from the name for SEO-friendly tag browsing pages.

Once created, the tag becomes immediately available for members and moderators to apply to articles during article creation and editing workflows, enhancing content discoverability through tag-based search, filtering, and browsing.

username.description:
Unique username for member identification and login.

Must be between 3 and 30 characters long, containing only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens. The username is used for authentication, public display, and content attribution throughout the discussion board system.

The system validates username uniqueness against the discussion_board_members table using a case-insensitive comparison, enforced by the @@unique([username]) constraint. Reserved usernames including 'admin', 'moderator', 'system', 'anonymous', and 'deleted' are prohibited to prevent confusion with system entities.

email.description:
Email address for authentication, notifications, and account recovery.

Must be a valid email address following standard email format specifications (contains @ symbol and valid domain structure). The email address serves as a primary authentication identifier and contact method for the member account.

The system validates email uniqueness against the discussion_board_members table, enforced by the @@unique([email]) constraint. Email verification is required before the account can be fully activated - the system sends a verification email containing a unique token link valid for 24 hours to confirm email ownership.

password.description:
Authentication password for securing the member account.

Must be at least 8 characters long and contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character to meet security requirements. The password is submitted as plain text during registration but is immediately hashed using a secure one-way hashing algorithm (bcrypt or equivalent) before storage.

The system stores only the hashed password in the password_hash column of the discussion_board_members table. Plain text passwords are never stored or logged. The password is used for authentication during login and must be provided again for sensitive operations like email changes or account deletion.

display_name.description:
Optional alternative name for public display instead of username.

If provided, the display name is shown in article bylines, comment author labels, and profile pages instead of the username. The display name can be between 1 and 50 characters and allows any characters except control characters, providing flexibility for users to present themselves with their preferred name, including international characters and special formatting.

If not provided during registration, the system uses the username for all public displays. Users can add or modify their display name later through profile editing. The display name does not need to be unique across users, as the username remains the unique identifier.

bio.description:
Optional member biography or self-description for the user profile.

Provides space for members to describe their interests, expertise, perspective, or background relevant to economic and political discussions. The bio is displayed on the member's profile page and helps other users understand the member's viewpoint and areas of knowledge.

Limited to 500 characters to encourage concise self-description while providing sufficient space for meaningful context. The system preserves line breaks and basic text formatting in the bio field. HTML and script tags are sanitized to prevent XSS attacks while maintaining readability.

location.description:
Optional geographic location of the member in free-text format.

Members can specify their city, country, region, or any geographic context they wish to share. The location field is purely informational and not validated or geocoded - users enter location as plain text.

Limited to 100 characters. The location appears on the member's profile page and can provide context for their perspectives on regional economic or political issues. No address verification or geographic data processing is performed on this field.

website_url.description:
Optional personal or professional website URL for the member.

If provided, the website URL is displayed on the member's profile page as a clickable link, allowing members to direct visitors to their personal blog, professional portfolio, organizational website, or other online presence.

The system validates that the URL is properly formatted with HTTP or HTTPS protocol. The website URL can be up to the maximum VARCHAR length supported by the database. No verification is performed to check if the URL is accessible or valid beyond format validation.

profile_picture_url.description:
Optional URL of the member's profile picture avatar image.

This URL points to a pre-uploaded profile picture image that represents the member visually throughout the discussion board. The profile picture is displayed next to the member's articles, comments, and on their profile page.

Following AutoBE's URL-only file upload pattern, clients must first upload the image file to the storage service (S3, CDN, etc.) to obtain a URL, then provide that URL during registration or profile updates. The system does NOT accept binary image data or base64-encoded images in this field.

If no profile picture URL is provided, the system displays a default avatar for the member. Supported image formats for the referenced file should be JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP with a recommended maximum file size of 5MB and standard dimensions of 200x200 pixels for display optimization.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.
Null when IP address is not provided by the client.

ip.description:
Client IP address for the initial session creation during registration.

This field is OPTIONAL - the server can extract the IP address from the HTTP request headers automatically, but clients MAY provide it explicitly for cases like server-side rendering (SSR) where the actual client IP needs to be forwarded.

The IP address is used to populate the discussion_board_member_sessions table for security monitoring, rate limiting, and audit trail purposes. It helps track login patterns, detect suspicious activity, and enforce security policies such as rate limiting on failed login attempts.

href.description:
Connection URL where the registration was initiated - the current page URL.

This is MANDATORY session context metadata that must be provided by the client. The server cannot infer this value as it represents the specific page or application state where the user completed registration.

The href is used to populate the discussion_board_member_sessions table, providing context about where users registered from. This information is valuable for analytics, understanding user registration sources, and security monitoring. The href helps track which pages or flows lead to successful registrations.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the registration page - the previous page URL.

This is MANDATORY session context metadata that must be provided by the client. The server cannot infer this value as it represents how the user navigated to the registration page.

The referrer is used to populate the discussion_board_member_sessions table, providing valuable marketing attribution and user journey data. This tracks what sources (search engines, social media, direct links, internal navigation) bring users to register. The referrer can be an empty string for direct access to the registration page.

IDiscussionBoardMember.ICreate.description:
Request body for registering a new member account in the discussion board system.

This DTO contains the core registration credentials and profile information needed to create a new member account. It implements the complete registration workflow as defined in the User Actors and Authentication requirements document section 2.1, including mandatory authentication fields, optional profile customization, and session context for security tracking.

The registration process creates a new record in the discussion_board_members table with status set to 'pending_email_verification' until email verification is completed. After account creation, the system generates a verification token and sends a verification email to the provided email address.

SECURITY CRITICAL: The password field accepts plain text password input which is immediately hashed by the backend using secure one-way hashing (bcrypt, Argon2, or equivalent) before storage in the password_hash column. The client NEVER sends pre-hashed passwords. The password_hash, verification tokens, and other authentication-sensitive data are never exposed in API responses.

REQUIRED session context fields (ip is optional, href and referrer are required) enable the backend to create the initial session record in discussion_board_member_sessions table with proper connection metadata for security auditing and analytics. These fields are NOT authentication credentials but connection context metadata provided by the client.

Optional profile fields (display_name, bio, location, website_url, profile_picture_url) can be provided during registration to complete the user profile immediately, or left empty and filled in later through profile editing. All text fields are sanitized by the backend to prevent XSS attacks while preserving basic formatting.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the member account.

This is the primary key from the discussion_board_members table, generated by the system upon account creation. The ID is immutable and used throughout the system to reference this member in relationships such as article authorship, comment posting, session tracking, and moderation records.

username.description:
Unique username for member identification and login.

This username must be 3-30 characters in length, containing only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens. The username is unique across all member accounts (enforced case-insensitively) and serves as both a login identifier and the default public display name unless a separate display_name is provided.

The username is immutable after account creation to maintain consistency in content attribution and user identity.

email.description:
Email address for authentication, notifications, and account recovery.

This email must be unique across all member accounts and must be verified before the member can create articles or post comments. The email is used for password recovery, account verification, comment notifications, and system communications.

Email addresses are never exposed publicly to protect user privacy. Only the account owner and moderators (for moderation purposes) can view this field.

password_hash.description:
Securely hashed password for authentication.

This field stores the one-way hashed representation of the member's password using secure hashing algorithms (bcrypt, Argon2, or equivalent). The password is never stored in plain text format.

CRITICAL SECURITY NOTE: This field MUST be excluded from all API response bodies to prevent password hash exposure. It is included in the entity schema for completeness but should always be filtered out before sending responses to clients.

display_name.description:
Optional alternative display name for public-facing member identification.

When provided, this display name (1-50 characters) is shown instead of the username in public contexts such as article authorship, comment attribution, and user profiles. If null or not provided, the system falls back to displaying the username.

Display names allow members to present themselves with a preferred name or pseudonym while keeping their username as a stable login identifier.

bio.description:
Optional member biography or self-description.

This free-form text field (maximum 500 characters) allows members to describe themselves, their interests, expertise, or perspective on economic and political topics. The bio is displayed on the member's public profile if profile_visibility allows.

Basic text formatting such as line breaks is preserved, but HTML tags are stripped to prevent XSS attacks. This helps other community members understand the author's background when reading their contributions.

location.description:
Optional geographic location of the member.

This is a free-text field (maximum 100 characters) where members can specify their city, country, region, or any geographic identifier they wish to share. No geocoding or validation is performed - it is purely informational and displayed on the member's public profile.

Location information provides context for members' perspectives on regional economic policies or political developments.

website_url.description:
Optional personal or professional website URL.

Members can provide a link to their personal blog, professional profile, research page, or other web presence. The URL must be properly formatted with http:// or https:// protocol and is displayed as a clickable link on the member's public profile.

This field enables members to share their credentials, additional writings, or institutional affiliations with the community.

profile_picture_url.description:
URL of the member's profile picture or avatar.

This URL points to the member's uploaded profile picture, which is displayed throughout the platform in article bylines, comment attribution, and the member's profile page. If null, the system displays a default avatar image.

Profile pictures are uploaded through a separate file upload endpoint and stored in the file storage system. This field contains only the URL reference to the stored image.

email_verified.description:
Indicates whether the member's email address has been verified.

Email verification is required before a member can create articles or post comments. The verification process involves sending a verification email with a unique token link that the member must click to confirm email ownership.

This field is set to false upon account creation and updated to true when the email verification link is successfully validated. Members with unverified emails can log in but have restricted content creation capabilities until verification is completed.

status.description:
Current status of the member account.

This field controls account lifecycle and access permissions. Valid status values include pending_email_verification for newly created accounts awaiting email confirmation, active for verified accounts in good standing with full member access, suspended for temporarily disabled accounts due to moderation action, and deleted for accounts that have been soft-deleted and are pending permanent removal.

Status transitions are tracked and logged for audit purposes. Status changes affect authentication eligibility and content creation permissions throughout the system.

profile_visibility.description:
Controls who can view this member's profile information.

Valid values include public for profiles visible to all users including guests, members_only for profiles visible only to authenticated members and moderators, and private for profiles visible only to moderators (for moderation purposes).

This privacy setting determines access to the member's profile page, bio, location, website, and other personal information. It does not affect the visibility of the member's articles or comments, which remain publicly accessible.

activity_visibility.description:
Controls who can view this member's activity history.

Valid values include public for activity visible to all users including guests, members_only for activity visible only to authenticated members and moderators, and hidden for activity not displayed on the profile but still accessible through article and comment listings.

Activity visibility affects the display of the member's articles and comments list on their profile page. Individual articles and comments remain accessible through normal browsing and search regardless of this setting.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the member's most recent successful login.

This field is automatically updated each time the member successfully authenticates. It is used for account security monitoring, inactive account detection, and activity analytics.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information (stored as timestamptz in database). A null value indicates the member has never logged in since account creation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the member account was originally created.

This is an immutable field set automatically during account registration. It is used for calculating account age, displaying member since information, sorting members by join date, and audit trail purposes.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, representing the exact moment the member record was inserted into the discussion_board_members table.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the member profile was last modified.

This field is automatically updated whenever any member account information changes, including profile edits, password changes, privacy setting updates, or status changes. It helps track account maintenance activity and identify recently updated profiles.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, representing the most recent modification to any field in the member record.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the member account.

When a member deletes their account, this field is set to the deletion timestamp rather than immediately removing the record. This enables account recovery during a grace period (typically 14-30 days), maintains referential integrity for authored articles and comments, and preserves audit trail for moderation records.

A null value indicates the account is active. A non-null value indicates the account is soft-deleted, should be excluded from active member lists, and prevented from authenticating. After the grace period expires, the account may be permanently deleted or anonymized according to content retention policies.

IDiscussionBoardMember.description:
Complete member entity representing a registered user account in the discussion board system.

This schema represents the full member record as stored in the discussion_board_members table of the Prisma database schema. Members are registered and authenticated users who can create articles, post comments, and engage in economic and political discussions on the platform. This entity includes all member account fields including credentials, profile information, privacy settings, and account metadata.

IMPORTANT SECURITY NOTE: While this schema includes the password_hash field for completeness and alignment with the Prisma schema, the password_hash MUST be excluded from all API responses. Response serialization should filter out this sensitive field before sending data to clients. The password_hash is included here to represent the complete database entity structure but should never be exposed in actual HTTP responses.

The member account lifecycle progresses through multiple statuses: pending_email_verification for newly created accounts awaiting email confirmation, active for verified accounts in good standing, suspended for accounts temporarily restricted by moderators, and deleted for soft-deleted accounts in grace period before permanent removal. Email verification is mandatory before members can create content.

Members control their privacy through profile_visibility (who can see their profile page) and activity_visibility (who can see their articles and comments list). These settings provide granular privacy controls while maintaining the public nature of discussion board content.

This complete entity type is used in operations that return full member information, such as retrieving a specific member's profile by username. For list views and embedded references, use IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary instead for performance. For member updates, use IDiscussionBoardMember.IUpdate which includes only editable fields.

page.description:
Page number for pagination of member search results.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve, starting from 1. Used in conjunction with limit to implement offset-based pagination. When page is not specified or set to null, defaults to 1 (first page).

Pagination enables efficient browsing of large member directories by dividing results into manageable chunks.

limit.description:
Number of member records to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination. Valid values are 10, 20, 50, or 100 members per page. When not specified or set to null, defaults to 20 members per page.

Larger values reduce the number of requests needed but increase response payload size. Smaller values provide faster initial response but require more requests for extensive browsing.

search.description:
Keyword search query for finding members by username, display name, or bio content.

Supports fuzzy matching using trigram-based similarity search (leveraging GIN indexes on username, display_name, and bio fields). Searches are case-insensitive and find partial matches. Minimum 2 characters required for search when provided.

Example searches: 'john' finds usernames like 'john_doe', 'johnny123'; 'economics' finds members with 'economics' in their bio or display name.

When null or not provided, no keyword filtering is applied.

status.description:
Filter members by account status.

When specified, returns only members with the matching status value. Valid statuses include:
- 'pending_email_verification': New accounts awaiting email confirmation
- 'active': Verified accounts in good standing
- 'suspended': Accounts temporarily disabled by moderation
- 'deleted': Accounts marked for deletion

When null or not provided, returns members of all statuses (subject to privacy filtering).

profile_visibility.description:
Filter members by profile visibility setting.

When specified, returns only members with the matching visibility preference. Valid values:
- 'public': Profiles visible to all users including guests
- 'members_only': Profiles visible only to authenticated members
- 'private': Profiles visible only to moderators

Note that privacy filtering is automatically applied based on requester authentication - this filter allows further refinement within the already-filtered set.

When null or not provided, includes members with all visibility settings (subject to automatic privacy filtering).

created_after.description:
Filter to include only members who registered on or after this timestamp.

Enables date range filtering for finding recently joined members or members from specific time periods. When combined with created_before, defines a registration date range.

Example use case: Find all members who joined in the last month to identify new community members.

When null or not provided, no lower bound is applied to the registration date filter.

created_before.description:
Filter to include only members who registered before this timestamp.

Enables date range filtering for finding established members or members from specific time periods. When combined with created_after, defines a registration date range.

Example use case: Find long-standing community members who joined before a certain date.

When null or not provided, no upper bound is applied to the registration date filter.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort member results by.

Determines the ordering of returned member records. Valid sort fields include:
- 'created_at': Sort by registration date (newest or oldest members)
- 'username': Alphabetical sorting by username
- 'display_name': Alphabetical sorting by display name (members without display names use username)
- 'last_login_at': Sort by most recent login activity

Default is 'created_at' when not specified.

Sort direction for the results.

Controls whether results are sorted in ascending or descending order based on the sort_by field:
- 'asc': Ascending order (A-Z for names, oldest first for dates)
- 'desc': Descending order (Z-A for names, newest first for dates)

Default is 'desc' for created_at and last_login_at (newest first), 'asc' for username and display_name (alphabetical).

Default is 'desc' for created_at and last_login_at (newest first), 'asc' for username and display_name (alphabetical).

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRequest.description:
Search criteria, filters, pagination parameters, and sorting options for member discovery and directory browsing.

This request type defines all possible parameters for searching and filtering the member directory. It supports flexible member discovery through keyword search, status and visibility filtering, date range selection, and configurable sorting. The request enables various use cases including finding new members, searching for specific users, browsing active contributors, and administrative member management.

Pagination is implemented through page and limit parameters, supporting efficient navigation through large member bases. The default pagination shows 20 members per page, with options for 10, 50, or 100 per page to accommodate different viewing preferences and use cases.

Search functionality uses trigram-based similarity matching (GIN indexes) on username, display_name, and bio fields, enabling fuzzy search that finds partial matches and handles typos gracefully. This provides better user experience than exact-match-only search.

Filtering capabilities include account status (to find active vs suspended members), profile visibility preferences (useful for moderators), and registration date ranges (to identify new or established members). Filters can be combined to create precise member queries.

Sorting options enable organizing results by different criteria: chronological by join date, alphabetical by name, or by recent activity. The sort_order parameter controls ascending vs descending direction.

All parameters are optional, allowing simple requests (return all members with defaults) or complex queries (search for active members with public profiles who joined in the last month, sorted alphabetically). The system applies automatic privacy filtering based on the requester's authentication status regardless of specified parameters.

display_name.description:
Optional display name shown publicly instead of username.

When provided, this name appears in article bylines, comments, and profile displays. If set to null, the system reverts to displaying the username. Must be between 1 and 50 characters when provided. Can contain any characters except control characters.

bio.description:
Optional member biography or self-description.

A brief text field for members to describe their interests, expertise, or perspective on economic and political topics. Maximum 500 characters. Line breaks are preserved for basic formatting. HTML and script tags are sanitized to prevent XSS attacks.

location.description:
Optional geographic location.

Free-text field where members can specify city, country, or region. No validation or geocoding performed. Maximum 100 characters. Setting to null removes location information from profile.

website_url.description:
Optional personal or professional website URL.

Must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL when provided. Appears on member's profile page. Setting to null removes the website link from profile. The system validates URL format before accepting updates.

profile_picture_url.description:
URL of the member's profile picture.

This URL points to an uploaded avatar image. When updated, the new image must be in JPEG, PNG, or GIF format with maximum 5MB size. The system resizes images to 200x200 pixels for display. Setting to null reverts to the default avatar. Profile picture uploads typically occur through a separate file upload operation that returns the URL.
