IDiscussionBoardMember.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating member profile information.

This DTO accepts optional fields that members can modify about their own profiles. All fields are optional, following the partial update pattern where only provided fields are updated. Members can update their display name, biography, location, website URL, profile picture URL, and privacy settings. The operation validates all provided fields against the constraints defined in the requirements and applies changes atomically.

Important fields that are NOT included in this update DTO:
- username: Immutable after registration, cannot be changed
- email: Requires separate email change verification flow
- password_hash: Changed through dedicated password change endpoint
- id, created_at: System-managed, immutable
- updated_at: Automatically set by system on successful update
- email_verified: System-managed based on verification process
- status: Changed through moderation actions, not direct updates
- last_login_at: Automatically updated on login
- deleted_at: Set through account deletion process

All text fields are sanitized to prevent XSS attacks. URLs are validated for proper format. Privacy setting changes take effect immediately.

username.description:
Desired unique username for the new member account.

The username serves as both a login identifier and the default public display name for the member. It must be between 3 and 30 characters in length and can only contain alphanumeric characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9), underscores (_), and hyphens (-).

The system validates username uniqueness using case-insensitive comparison against all existing usernames in the discussion_board_members table. Reserved usernames (admin, moderator, system, anonymous, deleted, user) are prohibited to prevent confusion with system entities.

The username is immutable after registration to maintain consistency in content attribution and user identity throughout the platform.

email.description:
Email address for the new member account.

The email address must be a valid format according to RFC 5322 standards and must be unique across all member accounts (case-insensitive comparison). This email is used for account verification, authentication, password recovery, and system notifications.

Upon registration, the system sends a verification email with a unique token link that the user must click to activate their account. The email_verified field remains false and status remains 'pending_email_verification' until this verification step is completed.

Email addresses are stored in the email field of the discussion_board_members table and are never exposed publicly to protect user privacy.

password.description:
Secure password for account authentication.

The password must meet complexity requirements including minimum 8 characters in length, at least one uppercase letter (A-Z), at least one lowercase letter (a-z), at least one digit (0-9), and at least one special character from the set (!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>?).

The system validates password strength server-side and rejects commonly compromised passwords from known breach databases. The password is never stored in plain text - it is securely hashed using industry-standard algorithms (bcrypt, Argon2, or PBKDF2) before being stored in the password_hash field of the discussion_board_members table.

Password complexity requirements balance security with usability, preventing weak passwords that could be easily compromised while remaining memorable for users.

display_name.description:
Optional alternative display name for public presentation during registration.

When provided, this display name (1-50 characters) will be shown in public contexts such as article authorship, comment attribution, and user profiles instead of the username. If not provided or set to null, the system defaults to displaying the username.

Display names can contain any characters except control characters, providing flexibility for users to present themselves with their preferred name, real name, or pseudonym. Unlike usernames, display names do not need to be unique across users, as the username remains the unique identifier.

Providing a display name during registration allows immediate profile personalization without requiring a separate profile update step after account creation.

bio.description:
Optional member biography or self-description for the user profile.

Provides space for new members to describe their interests, expertise, perspective, or background relevant to economic and political discussions during the registration process. The bio is displayed on the member's profile page and helps other users understand the member's viewpoint and areas of knowledge.

Limited to 500 characters to encourage concise self-description while providing sufficient space for meaningful context. The system preserves line breaks and basic text formatting in the bio field. HTML and script tags are sanitized to prevent XSS attacks while maintaining readability.

Providing a bio during registration completes the member profile immediately, though it can also be added or modified later through profile editing operations.

location.description:
Optional geographic location of the member in free-text format.

Members can specify their city, country, region, or any geographic context they wish to share during registration. The location field is purely informational and not validated or geocoded - users enter location as plain text.

Limited to 100 characters. The location appears on the member's profile page and can provide context for their perspectives on regional economic or political issues. No address verification or geographic data processing is performed on this field.

Providing location during registration completes the profile immediately, though it can also be added later through profile updates.

website_url.description:
Optional personal or professional website URL for the member.

If provided during registration, the website URL is displayed on the member's profile page as a clickable link, allowing members to direct visitors to their personal blog, professional portfolio, organizational website, or other online presence.

The system validates that the URL is properly formatted with HTTP or HTTPS protocol. No verification is performed to check if the URL is accessible or valid beyond format validation.

Providing a website URL during registration enables immediate professional credibility establishment, though it can also be added later through profile editing.

profile_picture_url.description:
Optional URL of the member's profile picture avatar image.

This URL points to a pre-uploaded profile picture image that represents the member visually throughout the discussion board. The profile picture is displayed next to the member's articles, comments, and on their profile page.

Following AutoBE's URL-only file upload pattern, clients must first upload the image file to the storage service (S3, CDN, etc.) to obtain a URL, then provide that URL during registration. The system does NOT accept binary image data or base64-encoded images in this field.

If no profile picture URL is provided during registration, the system displays a default avatar for the member. Supported image formats for the referenced file should be JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP with a recommended maximum file size of 5MB and standard dimensions of 200x200 pixels for display optimization.

Providing a profile picture during registration creates a more complete member presence immediately, though it can also be uploaded and set later through profile editing.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.
Null when IP address is not provided by the client.

ip.description:
Client IP address for the initial session creation during registration.

This field is OPTIONAL - the server can extract the IP address from the HTTP request headers automatically, but clients MAY provide it explicitly for cases like server-side rendering (SSR) where the actual client IP needs to be forwarded.

The IP address is used to populate the discussion_board_member_sessions table for security monitoring, rate limiting, and audit trail purposes. It helps track login patterns, detect suspicious activity, and enforce security policies such as rate limiting on failed login attempts.

href.description:
Connection URL (current page URL) - MANDATORY.

This field captures the full URL of the page where the registration form was submitted. It is used for session tracking, referral analytics, and security monitoring to understand the user's entry point into the registration flow.

When a session is created upon successful registration and email verification, this URL is stored in the href field of the discussion_board_member_sessions table, following the standardized session table pattern.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page URL) - MANDATORY.

This field captures the URL of the page that led the user to the registration page. It can be an external referrer (search engine, social media) or an internal page (article view, homepage). An empty string indicates direct navigation to the registration page.

This information is valuable for understanding user acquisition sources and optimizing registration conversion paths. When a session is created upon successful registration and email verification, this URL is stored in the referrer field of the discussion_board_member_sessions table.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRegister.description:
Registration request data for creating a new member account.

This schema defines the information required when a new user registers for a member account on the discussion board platform. Registration is the process of converting guest visitors into authenticated members who can create articles, post comments, and fully participate in economic and political discussions.

The registration process creates a new record in the discussion_board_members table with email_verified set to false and status set to 'pending_email_verification'. Default values are assigned including role 'member', profile_visibility 'public', and activity_visibility 'public'. The account remains in pending status until the user clicks the email verification link sent to their registered email address.

Security measures include validating username and email uniqueness using case-insensitive comparison, enforcing password complexity requirements, secure password hashing before storage, input sanitization to prevent injection attacks, and validation against reserved usernames. Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are required for proper session tracking when the account is activated and the user logs in for the first time.

Optional profile fields (display_name, bio, location, website_url, profile_picture_url) can be provided during registration to complete the user profile immediately, or left empty and filled in later through profile editing. All text fields are sanitized by the backend to prevent XSS attacks while preserving basic formatting.

password.description:
Current account password for deletion confirmation.

For security verification, members must provide their current password to confirm account deletion. This prevents unauthorized account deletion in case of session hijacking or compromised tokens. The password is verified against the stored password hash before proceeding with deletion.

deletion_reason.description:
Optional explanation for why the member is deleting their account.

This feedback helps the platform understand user churn reasons and improve the service. Maximum 1000 characters. Not required but valuable for product improvement. This information is stored temporarily for analytics but deleted along with the account.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IDeleteRequest.description:
Request body for member account deletion confirmation.

This DTO is used when a member initiates the permanent deletion of their account. It requires password verification as a security measure to prevent unauthorized account deletion. The deletion process is irreversible after the grace period (if implemented) and results in permanent removal of all personal data in compliance with GDPR requirements.

The deletion operation removes: email address, password hash, profile information (display name, bio, location, website), profile picture, privacy settings, notification preferences, login history, and activity history. Published articles and comments are either anonymized (author changed to 'Deleted User') or completely removed based on the content policy configuration.

This operation cannot be performed by:
- Guests: Must be authenticated
- Other members: Can only delete own account
- Moderators on behalf of users: Account deletion is self-service only

The password field is validated against the current password hash. If the password is incorrect, the deletion request is rejected. The optional deletion_reason provides feedback for platform improvement but is not required to complete the deletion.

current_password.description:
The member's current password for verification and security confirmation.

This field is required to verify that the authenticated user has knowledge of the current password before allowing the password change. This prevents unauthorized password changes even if an attacker has gained temporary session access through a stolen JWT token or compromised browser session.

The system validates this password against the stored password_hash in the discussion_board_members table. If the current password is incorrect, the password change request is rejected with an appropriate error message.

Validation rules for this field:
- Required field, cannot be empty or null
- Must match the member's existing password exactly
- Validated using the same secure hashing comparison used for login authentication

Security considerations:
- This field is transmitted over HTTPS to protect the password in transit
- The password is never logged or stored in plain text
- Failed verification attempts are logged for security monitoring and potential account protection measures

new_password.description:
The new password that will replace the current password.

This field must meet comprehensive password strength requirements to ensure account security. The password is validated against multiple criteria before being accepted, and the system provides real-time feedback on password strength during the change process.

Password strength requirements enforced by the system:
- Minimum 8 characters in length (no maximum specified, but reasonable limits apply)
- Must contain at least one uppercase letter (A-Z)
- Must contain at least one lowercase letter (a-z)
- Must contain at least one numeric digit (0-9)
- Must contain at least one special character from the set: !@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>?
- Must differ from the current password (cannot reuse the same password)
- Should not match common compromised passwords (validated against breach databases)
- Should not contain the username or email address

Password strength feedback:
The system calculates password strength based on length, character variety, and predictability, providing feedback as weak, medium, or strong. While strong passwords are encouraged, medium-strength passwords meeting the minimum requirements are accepted.

Security implementation:
When this password is accepted, it is hashed using a secure one-way hashing algorithm (bcrypt, Argon2, or equivalent) with appropriate work factors and unique salts. The resulting password_hash is stored in the discussion_board_members table, replacing the old hash. The plain text password is never stored or logged.

new_password_confirmation.description:
Confirmation of the new password to prevent typos and ensure intentional password selection.

This field must exactly match the new_password field character-for-character. The confirmation requirement prevents users from accidentally setting a password they didn't intend due to typing errors, which could lock them out of their account.

Validation rules:
- Required field, cannot be empty or null
- Must match new_password exactly (case-sensitive comparison)
- No additional validation beyond exact matching

If the new_password and new_password_confirmation fields do not match, the system rejects the password change request and displays an error message: "Passwords do not match. Please ensure both password fields are identical."

User experience considerations:
The system provides real-time validation feedback, indicating whether the confirmation matches as the user types. This immediate feedback helps users correct mismatches before form submission, improving the user experience and reducing frustration.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IPasswordUpdate.description:
Password change request DTO for authenticated member self-service password management.

This DTO represents the complete information required for a member to securely update their account password. The password change operation is a critical security function that must balance security requirements with user convenience, implementing verification of current password knowledge, enforcement of password strength requirements, and prevention of common password-related mistakes.

The three-field structure follows security best practices for password change interfaces:
1. Current password verification ensures the authenticated user has actual account access (not just a stolen session token)
2. New password field captures the desired new password with strength validation
3. Confirmation field prevents typos that could lock users out of their accounts

This DTO is used in the PUT /discussionBoard/member/members/{memberUsername}/password operation, which requires the authenticated member to be updating their own password (verified by comparing the JWT token's member ID with the member identified by the memberUsername path parameter). Members cannot use this operation to change other members' passwords.

Security context:
The password change operation triggers several security actions beyond updating the password_hash field. All existing JWT refresh tokens are invalidated across all devices and sessions, forcing re-authentication everywhere except the current session. This prevents attackers who may have compromised old refresh tokens from maintaining access after a password change. A confirmation email is sent to the registered email address, enabling the legitimate account owner to detect unauthorized password changes.

Data flow:
The DTO values are validated according to the business rules defined in the Error Handling and Validation document. Current password is verified against the stored hash. New password is validated for strength requirements. Confirmation is verified to match the new password. If all validations pass, the new password is securely hashed and stored, replacing the old password_hash in the discussion_board_members table.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member account whose password was successfully changed.

This UUID corresponds to the discussion_board_members.id field and confirms which account was modified by the password change operation. The ID is included in the response for client-side verification and logging purposes, ensuring the frontend can confirm the correct account was updated.

The ID value matches the authenticated member's ID from the JWT token, as members can only change their own passwords through this self-service operation.

token.description:
New JWT token information issued after successful password change.

When a member changes their password, the system invalidates all existing JWT refresh tokens across all devices and sessions as a security measure. This prevents attackers who may have compromised old tokens from maintaining access after the password change.

A new refresh token is immediately issued for the current session to maintain the user's authenticated state. The member does not need to log in again on the current device, but all other sessions (other browsers, devices) are terminated and require fresh authentication with the new password.

The token object contains:
- access_token: Short-lived JWT for API authentication (30-minute expiration)
- refresh_token: Long-lived JWT for obtaining new access tokens (14-day expiration)
- expires_at: Timestamp when the access token expires

Clients should replace their stored tokens with these new values immediately upon receiving this response to ensure continued authenticated access.

sessions_invalidated_count.description:
Number of active sessions that were invalidated across all devices as a result of the password change.

This count represents how many active login sessions existed for the member account before the password change operation. All of these sessions have been terminated (their refresh tokens invalidated), except for the current session which received new tokens.

The count provides transparency to the user about the security impact of their password change:
- 0: No other active sessions (user was only logged in on current device)
- 1: One other session was terminated (e.g., user was logged in on desktop and mobile)
- 2+: Multiple other sessions were terminated (user was logged in across many devices)

This information helps users understand the scope of the security action and confirms that potential unauthorized sessions have been terminated. If the count is higher than expected, it may indicate unauthorized access that has now been blocked.

From a security perspective, this metric is valuable for security auditing and user awareness, helping members recognize when their account may have been compromised if they see session counts that don't match their expected usage patterns.

password_updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the password was successfully changed.

This ISO 8601 formatted datetime (e.g., 2025-01-15T10:30:00Z) records the exact moment the password_hash field in the discussion_board_members table was updated with the new password hash. The timestamp serves multiple purposes:

1. Security Audit Trail: Provides precise timing for security event logging, enabling investigation of potential unauthorized password changes and correlating password changes with other security events.

2. User Confirmation: Gives the member a specific reference point for when their password was changed, useful for verifying the change occurred as expected and for reporting purposes if the change was unauthorized.

3. Session Management: Marks the cutoff point before which all refresh tokens were invalidated. Any refresh token issued before this timestamp is no longer valid.

4. Compliance and Logging: Supports security compliance requirements for tracking authentication credential changes and maintaining detailed audit logs.

The timestamp is also included in the confirmation email sent to the member's registered email address, providing an additional security verification mechanism. If the member did not initiate the password change, they can see exactly when the unauthorized change occurred and take immediate action to secure their account.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the member account record was last modified in the database.

This corresponds to the updated_at field in the discussion_board_members table, which is automatically updated by the system whenever any field in the member record changes. In the context of a password change response, this timestamp reflects when the password_hash field was updated and should match the password_updated_at value.

Including this field in the response maintains consistency with the member entity schema and provides complete account state information. The updated_at timestamp serves as a general-purpose modification tracker for the entire member record, while password_updated_at specifically tracks the password change event.

This field enables clients to maintain synchronized state with the server, detect concurrent modifications to the account, and provide accurate last-modified information in user interface displays. The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, typically in UTC, matching the database storage format (timestamptz).

IDiscussionBoardMember.IPasswordChange.description:
Successful password change confirmation response with new authentication tokens and security action details.

This response DTO confirms that the member's password has been successfully updated and provides all necessary information for the client to continue authenticated access with the new credentials. The response includes new JWT tokens to replace the invalidated ones, a count of terminated sessions to inform the user of the security impact, and a timestamp for audit trail purposes.

Security workflow completed:
When this response is returned, the following security actions have been successfully completed:
1. Current password was verified against the stored password_hash
2. New password was validated against all strength requirements and security policies
3. New password was securely hashed using bcrypt or equivalent algorithm with appropriate work factor
4. password_hash field in discussion_board_members table was updated with the new hash
5. All existing JWT refresh tokens (except current session) were invalidated and marked as expired
6. New access token and refresh token were generated for the current session
7. Security event was logged with timestamp, IP address, and session information
8. Confirmation email was sent to the member's registered email address

Client responsibilities upon receiving this response:
1. Replace stored access_token with the new token.access_token value
2. Replace stored refresh_token with the new token.refresh_token value
3. Update token expiration tracking with token.expires_at
4. Display success confirmation to the user
5. Optionally inform user that other sessions were logged out (using sessions_invalidated_count)

Session continuity:
The member remains logged in on the current device and session because new tokens are provided. However, all other devices and sessions are terminated and will require the user to log in again with the new password. This security measure ensures that any potentially compromised sessions are immediately invalidated when the password changes.

Error scenarios:
If the password change fails, this response is not returned. Instead, the API returns appropriate error responses:
- 401 Unauthorized if current_password verification fails
- 400 Bad Request if new_password fails strength validation
- 403 Forbidden if the member attempts to change another member's password
- 500 Internal Server Error if the password update or token invalidation process encounters a system error

This response type is critical for maintaining account security while providing a seamless user experience during password changes, a balance achieved through the token refresh mechanism that keeps the current session active while protecting all other sessions.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.description:
Search criteria, filtering options, and pagination parameters for retrieving discussion board comments.

This request type enables comprehensive querying of comments with support for keyword search, author filtering, date range constraints, and flexible sorting. It is used across multiple endpoints including retrieving all comments for an article, finding comments by a specific member, and browsing reply threads.

The search functionality supports partial text matching within comment content to find specific discussions or topics. Filtering capabilities include narrowing results by author type (member or moderator), specific author identifiers, date ranges for temporal analysis, and comment status to include or exclude deleted content based on permissions.

Pagination parameters control result set size and navigation through large comment collections. Sorting options enable viewing comments in different orders such as chronological (newest or oldest first) or by last update timestamp to surface recently modified discussions.

oneOf.description: Optional filter to retrieve comments belonging to a specific article.
Null when not filtering by article (returns comments across all articles).

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Optional filter to retrieve comments belonging to a specific article.

When provided, restricts results to comments where the discussion_board_article_id foreign key matches this value, showing only comments posted on the specified article. This filter is essential for article-specific comment retrieval, displaying all discussion activity under a particular article.

In endpoint contexts where the article ID is provided via path parameter (e.g., /articles/{articleId}/comments), this filter may be redundant as the backend automatically scopes the query to that article. However, in broader search contexts where comments are queried across multiple articles, this filter enables narrowing results to a specific article's discussion thread.

When set to null or omitted, the operation returns comments across all articles (subject to other filters and permissions). This enables cross-article comment search scenarios such as finding all comments by a specific member across the entire platform or searching for discussions containing specific keywords regardless of which article they appear under.

The field references the discussion_board_articles.id primary key and must be a valid UUID of an existing, non-deleted article when provided. The system validates the article existence and accessibility before executing the query.

search.description:
Optional keyword search term to filter comments by content.

When provided, the system performs partial text matching against comment content using PostgreSQL trigram indexes for efficient search. This enables users to find specific discussions, topics, or phrases within comment text.

The search is case-insensitive and supports finding comments containing the search term anywhere in the content field.

author_type.description:
Optional filter to retrieve comments only from specific author types.

Valid values are 'member' or 'moderator' based on the author_type discriminator field in the discussion_board_comments table. When specified, only comments created by the selected author type are returned.

This filter is useful for analyzing discussion patterns, identifying moderator interventions, or focusing on community member contributions.

discussion_board_member_id.description:
Optional filter to retrieve comments authored by a specific member.

When provided, only comments where the discussion_board_member_id matches this value are returned. This is particularly useful when the endpoint path does not specify a member context but filtering by member is desired.

This filter respects the member's activity visibility settings as defined in their profile.

discussion_board_moderator_id.description:
Optional filter to retrieve comments authored by a specific moderator.

When provided, only comments where the discussion_board_moderator_id matches this value are returned. This enables tracking moderator participation in discussions and reviewing moderator comment activity.

Useful for moderation oversight and understanding moderator engagement patterns.

from_date.description:
Optional start date for filtering comments by creation timestamp.

When provided, only comments created on or after this date are included in results. Combined with to_date, this enables date range filtering for temporal analysis of discussions.

Timestamps are compared against the created_at field in the discussion_board_comments table.

to_date.description:
Optional end date for filtering comments by creation timestamp.

When provided, only comments created on or before this date are included in results. Combined with from_date, this enables date range filtering for temporal analysis of discussions.

Timestamps are compared against the created_at field in the discussion_board_comments table.

include_deleted.description:
Optional flag to include soft-deleted comments in results.

When true, comments with non-null deleted_at timestamps are included in the response. This is typically restricted to moderators for audit and review purposes. Regular members and guests should not see deleted comments.

Defaults to false when not specified, filtering out all soft-deleted comments.

sort_by.description:
Optional field name to sort results by.

Supported values include 'created_at' for chronological ordering, 'updated_at' for recently modified comments, and other comment fields. The sort direction is controlled by the sort_order parameter.

Defaults to 'created_at' when not specified.

sort_order.description:
Optional sort direction for ordering results.

Valid values are 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). When sorting by created_at with descending order, newest comments appear first. When sorting with ascending order, oldest comments appear first.

Defaults to 'desc' when not specified, showing newest content first.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Indicates which page of results to retrieve. Combined with limit, this determines the offset into the result set. For example, page 2 with limit 20 retrieves results 21-40.

Defaults to 1 when not specified.

limit.description:
Number of comments to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination. Maximum value should be enforced to prevent excessive data transfer (typically 100 items maximum). Minimum value is 1.

Defaults to 20 when not specified, as per the performance requirements for comment listing.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a discussion board comment for use in list views and embedded references.

This summary provides essential comment information without the full detail of the complete comment entity, optimizing for performance in contexts where multiple comments are displayed or where comment data is embedded within other entities.

The summary includes the core identification, content preview, authorship information, and timestamps necessary for displaying comments in lists, activity feeds, and other summary contexts.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the comment.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the comment and is used for direct comment access, linking, and reference in URLs and API endpoints.

content.description:
The text content of the comment.

This is the actual user-submitted comment text, limited to 5,000 characters. The content is sanitized to prevent XSS attacks while preserving basic text formatting such as line breaks.

For summary views, this contains the full comment text since comments are already limited in length and designed for complete display in discussion threads.

author_type.description:
Discriminator indicating the type of author who created this comment.

Valid values are 'member' or 'moderator'. This field determines which author reference (memberAuthor or moderatorAuthor) is populated and should be used when displaying author information.

This discriminator is essential for proper author attribution and for applying appropriate styling or badges to moderator comments.

memberAuthor.description:
Summary information of the member who authored this comment, if the comment was created by a member.

This field is populated when author_type is 'member' and is null when author_type is 'moderator'. The member summary provides essential identification information (username, display name, profile picture) for displaying comment authorship.

This reference enables users to identify who wrote the comment and navigate to the author's profile for more information.

moderatorAuthor.description:
Summary information of the moderator who authored this comment, if the comment was created by a moderator.

This field is populated when author_type is 'moderator' and is null when author_type is 'member'. The moderator summary provides essential identification information for displaying moderator comment authorship with appropriate moderator badges or styling.

This reference enables users to identify moderator participation in discussions and recognize official moderation responses.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was originally created and posted.

This timestamp represents when the comment was first submitted to the system. It is immutable after creation and is used for chronological sorting of comments, displaying relative time ('2 hours ago'), and tracking discussion timeline.

Timestamps are stored in UTC and should be converted to the user's timezone for display.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was last modified or updated.

This timestamp is updated whenever the comment content is edited by the author or a moderator. If this differs from created_at, it indicates the comment has been edited, and the system should display an 'edited' indicator.

This field enables tracking of comment modifications and displaying edit information to users for transparency.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRequest.description:
Search criteria, filtering parameters, sorting options, and pagination settings for querying discussion board moderators.

This request type enables comprehensive searching and filtering of the moderator user base with support for username pattern matching, email domain filtering, display name search, account status filtering, email verification status, and date range constraints on account creation. It provides flexible querying capabilities for administrative operations, moderator management, and system oversight.

The search functionality leverages PostgreSQL trigram indexes on display_name and bio fields for efficient partial text matching. Multiple filter criteria can be combined to narrow results precisely. Sorting options enable ordering results by various moderator attributes in ascending or descending order.

Pagination parameters control result set size and navigation through potentially large moderator lists, ensuring performant queries even as the moderator count grows over time.

username.description:
Optional filter to search moderators by username pattern.

Supports partial matching to find moderators whose usernames contain this substring. Case-insensitive search enables flexible moderator discovery.

Useful for quickly locating moderators when only part of their username is known.

email.description:
Optional filter to search moderators by email address or email domain.

Supports exact matching or partial matching for email domain filtering (e.g., '@company.com'). Enables finding moderators from specific organizations or email providers.

Email searches are case-insensitive for user convenience.

display_name.description:
Optional filter to search moderators by display name pattern.

Leverages PostgreSQL trigram index for efficient partial text matching. Supports finding moderators by their public display names even with incomplete or fuzzy matching.

Case-insensitive search across the display_name field.

status.description:
Optional filter to retrieve moderators with specific account status.

Valid values include 'pending_email_verification', 'active', 'suspended', or 'deleted' as defined in the Prisma schema. Enables filtering for active moderators, identifying suspended accounts, or reviewing deleted moderator records.

When not specified, all statuses are included in results.

email_verified.description:
Optional filter to retrieve moderators based on email verification status.

When true, only moderators with verified email addresses are returned. When false, only unverified accounts are returned. When omitted, verification status is not used as a filter.

Useful for identifying moderators who haven't completed email verification.

created_from.description:
Optional start date for filtering moderators by account creation timestamp.

When provided, only moderators whose accounts were created on or after this date are included. Combined with created_to, enables date range filtering for temporal analysis of moderator onboarding.

Timestamps are compared against the created_at field.

created_to.description:
Optional end date for filtering moderators by account creation timestamp.

When provided, only moderators whose accounts were created on or before this date are included. Combined with created_from, enables date range filtering for temporal analysis.

Timestamps are compared against the created_at field.

sort_by.description:
Optional field name to sort moderator results by.

Supported values include 'created_at' for registration date ordering, 'last_login_at' for recent activity, 'username' for alphabetical ordering, 'updated_at' for recently modified profiles, and other moderator fields.

Defaults to 'created_at' when not specified.

sort_order.description:
Optional sort direction for ordering moderator results.

Valid values are 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Controls whether results are sorted in ascending or descending order based on the sort_by field.

Defaults to 'desc' when not specified, showing newest or highest values first.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Indicates which page of results to retrieve. Combined with limit, determines the offset into the result set. For example, page 2 with limit 25 retrieves results 26-50.

Defaults to 1 when not specified.

limit.description:
Number of moderators to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination. Reasonable maximum should be enforced to prevent excessive data transfer (typically 100 items maximum). Minimum value is 1.

Defaults to 25 when not specified for moderator list views.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a moderator for display in references and lists.

Provides essential moderator identification including username and display name for attribution in moderation actions, reports, and content management. Used when showing who performed specific moderation actions without exposing full profile details.

This lightweight representation is optimized for embedding in other entities like warnings, suspensions, and moderation action logs.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this moderator account.

Primary key used to reference this moderator across the system. Generated automatically during moderator account creation.

username.description:
Unique username for moderator identification.

The primary identifier displayed in moderation contexts. Must be 3-30 characters containing only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens.

Used for moderator attribution in moderation actions, reports, and audit logs.

display_name.description:
Optional alternative name for public display instead of username.

When provided this is shown in place of the username in moderation contexts. Allows moderators to use a more formal or professional display name while maintaining a simpler username for login.

Length is 1-50 characters when present.

profile_picture_url.description:
URL of the moderator's profile picture.

When present displays the moderator's custom avatar in moderation contexts. Falls back to a default avatar icon if null.

Used to provide visual identification of moderators in moderation dashboards and action logs.

email_verified.description:
Indicates whether the moderator's email address has been verified.

Email verification is required before a moderator can perform moderation actions. Set to false upon account creation and updated to true when the email verification link is validated.

status.description:
Current status of the moderator account.

Valid status values include pending_email_verification for newly created accounts awaiting email confirmation, active for verified accounts in good standing with full moderation access, suspended for temporarily disabled accounts, and deleted for accounts that have been soft-deleted.

moderation_permissions.description:
JSON string defining specific moderation permissions and access levels.

Contains JSON-encoded object specifying granular moderation capabilities such as can_edit_articles, can_delete_articles, can_edit_comments, can_delete_comments, can_issue_warnings, can_suspend_users, can_ban_users, can_manage_reports, and can_manage_categories.

profile_visibility.description:
Controls who can view this moderator's profile information.

Valid values include public for profiles visible to all users including guests, members_only for profiles visible only to authenticated members and other moderators, and private for profiles visible only to other moderators and system administrators.

activity_visibility.description:
Controls who can view this moderator's activity history.

Valid values include public for activity visible to all users including guests, members_only for activity visible only to authenticated members and other moderators, and hidden for activity not displayed on the profile but still accessible through content search.

bio.description:
Optional moderator biography or self-description.

Free-form text field (maximum 500 characters) allowing moderators to provide information about themselves, their background, areas of expertise, or moderation philosophy. Basic text formatting such as line breaks is preserved, but HTML tags are stripped to prevent XSS attacks.

location.description:
Optional geographic location of the moderator.

Free-text field (maximum 100 characters) where moderators can specify their city, country, region, or any geographic identifier they wish to share. No geocoding or validation is performed.

website_url.description:
Optional personal or professional website URL.

Moderators can provide a link to their personal website, professional profile, or institutional affiliation. Must be properly formatted with http:// or https:// protocol.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the moderator's most recent successful login.

Automatically updated each time the moderator successfully authenticates. Used for account security monitoring, inactive account detection, and auditing moderator activity patterns. Null indicates the moderator has never logged in since account creation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was originally created.

Immutable field set automatically during account registration. Used for calculating account age, sorting moderators by seniority, and audit trail purposes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator profile was last modified.

Automatically updated whenever any moderator account information changes, including profile edits, password changes, permission updates, or status changes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the moderator account.

When set, indicates the account is soft-deleted. Null indicates the account is active. Soft deletion enables account recovery during a grace period, maintains audit trail integrity, and preserves referential integrity for historical records.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the moderator account.

This is the primary key from the discussion_board_moderators table, generated by the system upon account creation. The ID is immutable and used throughout the system to reference this moderator in relationships such as session tracking, moderation actions, article edits, and comment management.

username.description:
Unique username for moderator identification and login.

This username must be 3-30 characters in length, containing only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens. The username is unique across all moderator accounts (enforced case-insensitively) and serves as both a login identifier and the public display name unless a separate display_name is provided.

The username is immutable after account creation to maintain consistency in moderation action attribution and content ownership.

email.description:
Email address for authentication, notifications, and moderation alerts.

This email must be unique across all moderator accounts and must be verified before the moderator can perform moderation actions. The email is used for password recovery, security notifications, moderation queue alerts, and system communications.

Email addresses are never exposed publicly to protect moderator privacy. Only the account owner and system administrators can view this field.

password_hash.description:
Securely hashed password for authentication.

This field stores the one-way hashed representation of the moderator's password using secure hashing algorithms (bcrypt, Argon2, or equivalent). The password is never stored in plain text format.

CRITICAL SECURITY REQUIREMENT: This field MUST be excluded from all API response bodies through serialization filtering to prevent password hash exposure. While included in the entity schema for completeness and to match the Prisma database structure (discussion_board_moderators.password_hash), this field should NEVER be sent to clients in any HTTP response.

The field is necessary in the schema for proper backend code generation, entity mapping, and database operations. Runtime serialization filters or response transformation middleware must remove this field before responses are sent to clients. This approach maintains schema completeness while enforcing security through application-layer controls.

display_name.description:
Optional alternative display name for public-facing moderator identification.

When provided, this display name (1-50 characters) is shown instead of the username in public contexts such as moderation action logs, edited content indicators, and moderator posts. If null or not provided, the system falls back to displaying the username.

Display names allow moderators to maintain a professional public presence while keeping their username private or using a more formal name for official moderation activities.

bio.description:
Optional moderator biography or self-description.

This free-form text field (maximum 500 characters) allows moderators to provide information about themselves, their background, areas of expertise, or moderation philosophy. The bio is displayed on the moderator's public profile if profile_visibility allows.

Basic text formatting such as line breaks is preserved, but HTML tags are stripped to prevent XSS attacks.

location.description:
Optional geographic location of the moderator.

This is a free-text field (maximum 100 characters) where moderators can specify their city, country, region, or any geographic identifier they wish to share. No geocoding or validation is performed - it is purely informational and displayed on the moderator's public profile.

Location information helps community members understand moderator perspectives and time zones for moderation coverage.

website_url.description:
Optional personal or professional website URL.

Moderators can provide a link to their personal website, professional profile, or institutional affiliation. The URL must be properly formatted with http:// or https:// protocol and is displayed as a clickable link on the moderator's public profile.

This field enables moderators to share their credentials, background information, or other platforms where they are active, building trust with the community.

profile_picture_url.description:
URL of the moderator's profile picture or avatar.

This URL points to the moderator's uploaded profile picture, which is displayed throughout the platform in moderation logs, edited content indicators, and the moderator's profile page. If null, the system displays a default avatar image.

Profile pictures are uploaded through a separate file upload endpoint and stored in the file storage system. This field contains only the URL reference to the stored image.

email_verified.description:
Indicates whether the moderator's email address has been verified.

Email verification is required before a moderator can perform moderation actions. The verification process involves sending a verification email with a unique token link that the moderator must click to confirm email ownership.

This field is set to false upon account creation and updated to true when the email verification link is successfully validated. Moderators with unverified emails have restricted access until verification is completed.

status.description:
Current status of the moderator account.

This field controls account lifecycle and access permissions. Valid status values include pending_email_verification for newly created accounts awaiting email confirmation, active for verified accounts in good standing with full moderation access, suspended for temporarily disabled accounts due to policy violations or administrative action, and deleted for accounts that have been soft-deleted and are pending permanent removal.

Status transitions are tracked and logged for audit purposes. Status changes affect authentication eligibility and permission grants throughout the system.

moderation_permissions.description:
JSON string defining specific moderation permissions and access levels.

This field contains a JSON-encoded object that specifies granular moderation capabilities for this moderator account. Permissions may include can_edit_articles, can_delete_articles, can_edit_comments, can_delete_comments, can_issue_warnings, can_suspend_users, can_ban_users, can_manage_reports, and can_manage_categories.

The JSON structure allows flexible permission management without database schema changes, supporting role-based access control and differentiated moderator capabilities. Permission checks are performed at the application layer when moderators attempt to execute moderation actions.

profile_visibility.description:
Controls who can view this moderator's profile information.

Valid values include public for profiles visible to all users including guests, members_only for profiles visible only to authenticated members and other moderators, and private for profiles visible only to other moderators and system administrators.

This privacy setting determines access to the moderator's profile page, bio, location, website, and other personal information. It does not affect the visibility of moderation actions or official moderator posts.

activity_visibility.description:
Controls who can view this moderator's activity history.

Valid values include public for activity visible to all users including guests, members_only for activity visible only to authenticated members and other moderators, and hidden for activity not displayed on the profile but still accessible through content search.

Activity visibility affects the display of the moderator's articles and comments on their profile page. Moderation actions are logged separately and are not controlled by this setting.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the moderator's most recent successful login.

This field is automatically updated each time the moderator successfully authenticates. It is used for account security monitoring, inactive account detection, and auditing moderator activity patterns.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information (stored as timestamptz in database). A null value indicates the moderator has never logged in since account creation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was originally created.

This is an immutable field set automatically during account registration. It is used for calculating account age, sorting moderators by seniority, and audit trail purposes.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, representing the exact moment the moderator record was inserted into the discussion_board_moderators table.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator profile was last modified.

This field is automatically updated whenever any moderator account information changes, including profile edits, password changes, permission updates, or status changes. It helps track account maintenance activity and identify stale or inactive accounts.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, representing the most recent modification to any field in the moderator record.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the moderator account.

When a moderator account is deleted, this field is set to the deletion timestamp rather than removing the record entirely. This enables account recovery during a grace period, maintains audit trail integrity for moderation actions, and preserves referential integrity for historical records.

A null value indicates the account is active. A non-null value indicates the account is soft-deleted and should be excluded from active moderator lists and prevented from authenticating. Permanent deletion may occur after a retention period.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.description:
Complete moderator account information returned from authentication and profile operations.

This schema represents a moderator user in the discussion board system - a trusted user with elevated permissions to manage content, enforce community guidelines, and oversee discussions. Moderators can edit or delete any content, review reported content, issue warnings and suspensions, and maintain discussion quality.

Moderators have the same base account structure as members (username, email, profile information) plus additional moderation_permissions that grant them elevated capabilities. Moderator accounts require email verification and support the same authentication mechanisms as member accounts.

Security considerations include never exposing the password_hash field in API responses, protecting email addresses from public display, and logging all moderator actions for accountability. Moderators can configure profile_visibility and activity_visibility to control who can view their personal information and posting history.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating moderator profile and account information.

This schema defines the fields that can be modified when updating a moderator profile through the PUT /discussionBoard/moderator/moderators/{moderatorUsername} endpoint. All fields are optional following the partial update pattern, allowing clients to update only the specific fields that need modification without affecting other profile data.

The update operation validates all provided fields against the same business rules as moderator account creation. Display names are limited to 50 characters, biographies to 500 characters, locations to 100 characters, and URLs must be properly formatted. Email changes trigger a verification workflow to confirm ownership of the new address.

This DTO is used when moderators update their own profiles or when administrators modify moderator settings. The operation requires authentication and proper authorization - moderators can update their own profiles, while administrative users can update other moderators' profiles and permission configurations.

Security considerations: The password_hash field is never included in update operations (password changes use a dedicated endpoint). Actor identity fields (discussion_board_member_id, created_by_member_id) are not included as they are immutable or managed by authentication context. System-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, last_login_at) are excluded as they are controlled by the backend.

display_name.description:
Optional display name shown publicly instead of username.

When provided, this name appears in article attributions, comment displays, and moderation action logs. Can be 1-50 characters and may contain any characters except control characters. Setting to null reverts to using the username for display.

Updating the display name changes how the moderator is identified in all public-facing contexts while maintaining the immutable username for authentication and system references.

bio.description:
Optional moderator biography or self-description.

A brief text field (maximum 500 characters) where moderators can describe their background, expertise, areas of focus, or moderation philosophy. Supports basic text with preserved line breaks. The system sanitizes input to prevent XSS attacks.

Setting to null clears the biography. Full-text search is supported via trigram indexing for profile discovery.

location.description:
Optional geographic location as free-text field.

Moderators can specify their city, country, region, or general geographic area. No validation or geocoding is performed. Maximum 100 characters. Setting to null clears the location.

Location provides geographic context for moderation perspectives on regional political or economic topics.

website_url.description:
Optional personal or professional website URL.

Must be a properly formatted URL with HTTP or HTTPS protocol. Used to link to the moderator's personal blog, professional website, academic profile, or other online presence. Setting to null removes the website link.

The system validates URL format but does not verify destination accessibility. Stored as VARCHAR(80000) to accommodate long URLs.

profile_picture_url.description:
URL of the moderator's profile picture or avatar image.

References a pre-uploaded image in the file storage system. When set to null, the system displays a default avatar. Images should be uploaded separately before updating this field.

Profile pictures are typically resized to standard dimensions (e.g., 200x200 pixels) for display. Accepted formats include JPEG, PNG, and GIF.

email.description:
Updated email address for authentication and notifications.

When changing email, the system triggers a verification workflow requiring the moderator to confirm ownership of the new email address. The email change is not finalized until verification completes.

Email addresses must be unique across all moderator accounts. The system validates email format and enforces uniqueness before accepting updates.

moderation_permissions.description:
Updated JSON string defining specific moderation permissions and access levels.

This field allows administrative users to modify the moderator's permission set, enabling fine-grained control over moderation capabilities. The JSON structure defines which moderation actions this moderator can perform.

Typical permission categories include content management (edit, delete), user management (warn, suspend, ban), category administration, and report review access. The exact JSON schema is flexible based on system implementation.
