Values include 'published' for publicly visible articles, 'draft' for unpublished work-in-progress content, and 'archived' for older content that has been removed from primary circulation but retained for historical purposes. Only published articles appear in public listings and search results.

view_count.description:
Number of times this article has been viewed.

A system-managed counter that increments each time a user accesses the article detail page. This metric helps identify popular content and provides engagement statistics. The count is initialized to 0 when an article is created and is automatically incremented by the system on each article view.

comment_count.description:
Cached count of comments on this article.

A system-managed counter tracking the total number of comments (including both top-level comments and replies) associated with this article. This count is initialized to 0 when the article is created and is automatically updated when comments are added or removed. The cached count enables efficient display of engagement metrics without requiring expensive database queries.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the article was originally created.

Records the exact date and time when this article was first published to the discussion board. This timestamp is immutable after creation and serves as the primary sorting criterion for article chronological ordering. It provides historical context and helps users understand the timeliness of the content.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the article was last modified.

Records the most recent date and time when any aspect of the article was updated, including title changes, body content edits, metadata updates, or attachment modifications. This field is automatically updated by the system on each edit operation and helps readers identify recently revised content.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the article.

When an article is deleted by its author or a moderator, this field is set to the deletion timestamp rather than permanently removing the record from the database. A null value indicates the article is active and publicly accessible. A non-null timestamp indicates the article has been soft-deleted and should be hidden from public view.

Soft deletion provides several critical capabilities. It enables content recovery if articles are deleted in error or if moderation decisions are reversed. It maintains referential integrity for comments, snapshots, attachments, and moderation logs that reference the article. It preserves audit trails showing when content was removed and by whom. It supports compliance with data retention policies and legal requirements for content tracking.

When deleted_at is set, the article is excluded from public search results, category browsing, and article listings. However, moderators may retain access to deleted articles for audit and investigation purposes. The article's associated comments are typically hidden along with the article to maintain discussion coherence.

The deletion timestamp works in conjunction with the article's status field. Typically, articles are marked as deleted through the deleted_at timestamp rather than changing the status field, though implementation may vary. The updated_at timestamp is also updated when deletion occurs to reflect the most recent change to the article record.

author.description:
Member who created this article.

Reference to the author's member account providing context about who published this content. The author information includes public profile fields such as username, display name, and profile picture for proper attribution and credibility. The relationship is established through the discussion_board_member_id foreign key in the articles table.

lastModifiedByModerator.description:
Moderator who last modified this article, if applicable.

When a moderator edits an article (rather than the original author), this field references the moderator's account to track moderator intervention. This provides transparency about content that has been modified by platform administrators and supports moderation audit trails. The field is null for articles that have only been edited by their original authors.

categories.description:
Categories assigned to this article for organization and discovery.

A collection of predefined topic categories (e.g., Economic Policy, Political Analysis) that classify this article's subject matter. Articles must have at least one category and can belong to multiple categories for flexible organization. Categories enable users to browse related articles and filter content by topic area.

tags.description:
Flexible topic tags for detailed article labeling.

User-generated keywords that provide granular topic classification beyond formal categories. Tags enable detailed content filtering and discovery (e.g., monetary-policy, climate-change, taxation). Articles can have up to 5 tags, each normalized to lowercase for consistency. Tags are optional but highly recommended for improved discoverability.

images.description:
Image attachments associated with this article.

Collection of images uploaded as supporting visual content including charts, graphs, infographics, and photographs. Each image includes metadata such as original filename, dimensions, file size, and storage information. Images are displayed inline within the article view and can be viewed at full resolution. Maximum 10 images per article with 5MB maximum per image.

documents.description:
Document attachments associated with this article.

Collection of document files uploaded as supplementary materials including research papers, policy documents, and data files. Each document includes metadata such as original filename, MIME type, and file size. Documents are presented as downloadable links with file type indicators. Maximum 5 documents per article with 10MB maximum per document.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description:
Complete article entity representing a discussion board article with all content, metadata, and relationships.

This is the primary content type in the discussion board system, representing economic and political analysis, commentary, and discussions published by members and moderators. Articles contain rich text content with support for formatting, multiple category and tag classifications for organization, and multimedia attachments including images and documents for evidence-based discussions.

Articles are created by members (tracked via discussion_board_member_id) and can be edited by their authors or by moderators (tracked via last_modified_by_moderator_id). Each article maintains a complete version history through the discussion_board_article_snapshots table, enabling audit trails and potential rollback capabilities.

The article lifecycle supports multiple statuses including published (publicly visible), draft (work in progress), and archived (removed from circulation). Articles use soft deletion (deleted_at timestamp) allowing content recovery and maintaining data integrity for audit purposes.

Engagement is tracked through system-managed counters including view_count (incremented on each article access) and comment_count (updated when comments are added or removed). These metrics provide insights into article popularity and discussion activity without requiring expensive real-time calculations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the image attachment.

This is the primary key generated by the system when the image is uploaded and stored in the discussion_board_article_images table. The ID uniquely identifies this image attachment across the entire system and is used for all subsequent operations on this image (retrieval, deletion, management).

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Reference to the parent article that this image is attached to.

This foreign key establishes the ownership relationship between the image and its parent article in the discussion_board_articles table. Every image must belong to exactly one article, and this association is immutable once created. When the parent article is deleted, all associated images are automatically deleted (cascade delete).

uploaded_by_member_id.description:
Member who uploaded this image attachment.

This foreign key references the discussion_board_members table and tracks which authenticated member uploaded this image. This is automatically captured from the authenticated session context and is never provided by the client in request bodies. The uploader information is used for permissions checking, audit trails, and attribution purposes.

url.description:
Download URL for accessing the actual image file.

This URL provides direct access to the stored image file, enabling users to view and download the image. Following AutoBE's URL-only file handling pattern, this field is CRITICAL for file access and must be included in all image attachment responses.

The URL is constructed from the stored_name field which contains the unique system-generated filename in the storage system (S3, CDN, or file server). It represents the complete, ready-to-use URL that clients can use immediately to display images inline in articles, provide download links in the user interface, enable full-resolution image viewing in modals or lightboxes, and implement image preloading for performance optimization.

Security considerations: The URL may be a signed URL with expiration for private content, or a public CDN URL for published article attachments. Access control is enforced at the URL generation level based on article visibility and user permissions. The URL should be treated as opaque by clients and not parsed or manipulated.

Without this URL field, clients have no way to access the actual image file content. The stored_name field alone is insufficient because it is an internal storage identifier, not a complete access path. This URL field is what enables the entire file download and display functionality in the discussion board system.

original_name.description:
Original filename of the uploaded image as provided by the user.

This is the filename that the user's file had when it was selected for upload (e.g., 'economic_chart_2024.png', 'trade_statistics.jpg'). The original filename is preserved for display purposes so users can identify their uploaded files easily. Maximum length is typically 255 characters to accommodate filesystem limitations.

stored_name.description:
Unique filename used for storage to prevent conflicts and ensure security.

This is the system-generated filename used to store the image file in the backend storage system. It is typically a UUID or hash-based name that ensures uniqueness and prevents filename collisions, path traversal attacks, and other security issues. This stored filename is never exposed to end users but is essential for internal file retrieval and management.

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the image file for validation and proper content delivery.

Specifies the exact format of the image using standard MIME type notation. Valid values are 'image/jpeg' for JPEG/JPG images, 'image/png' for PNG images, 'image/gif' for GIF images, and 'image/webp' for WebP images. The MIME type is validated against both the file extension and actual file content to prevent format spoofing. This field is essential for setting proper Content-Type headers when serving images to browsers.

size_bytes.description:
File size in bytes.

The total size of the image file measured in bytes. This is validated during upload to ensure it does not exceed the 5MB (5,242,880 bytes) maximum limit for individual images. The size information is displayed to users alongside download links so they can make informed decisions about downloading files, particularly on metered or slow connections.

width.description:
Image width in pixels.

The horizontal dimension of the image in pixels. Used for validation during upload (minimum 50px, maximum 8000px) and for display optimization. The width information allows the system to generate appropriately sized thumbnails, apply responsive image techniques, and inform users about image dimensions before downloading or viewing full resolution versions.

height.description:
Image height in pixels.

The vertical dimension of the image in pixels. Used for validation during upload (minimum 50px, maximum 8000px) and for display optimization. Combined with width, this provides the complete aspect ratio of the image, enabling proper thumbnail generation, responsive display, and layout calculations in the article view.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the image was uploaded to the system.

Records the exact date and time when this image attachment was created and stored in the system. This timestamp is automatically set by the system during the upload operation and is immutable after creation. It is used for sorting attachments, tracking upload history, and audit trail purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the image was soft deleted.

When an image is removed by the article author or a moderator, this field is set to the deletion timestamp instead of permanently removing the database record. Null indicates the image is active and available. Soft deletion enables recovery if images are removed in error and maintains audit trails for moderation purposes. Images with non-null deleted_at are hidden from public view and treated as unavailable.

uploader.description:
Summary information about the member who uploaded this image attachment.

This relationship expansion provides identification of who added this visual supporting material to the article, including the uploader's username, display name, and basic profile information. This attribution is important for accountability, especially when images are added during article editing or when moderators enhance articles with additional visual evidence.

The uploader reference is derived from the uploaded_by_member_id foreign key, which points to the discussion_board_members table. The summary format prevents excessive nesting while providing essential user identification. This information helps readers understand content provenance and enables proper attribution of contributed visual materials.

For images uploaded during initial article creation, the uploader will be the same as the article author. For images added later through editing or by moderators enhancing content, the uploader may differ from the original article author. This distinction is valuable for tracking contributions and understanding content evolution over time.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.description:
Complete image attachment entity representing an uploaded image associated with a discussion board article.

This schema represents the full structure of an image attachment as stored in the discussion_board_article_images table. Image attachments serve as visual supporting evidence for economic and political discussions, enabling members to include charts, graphs, infographics, photographs, and other visual materials in their articles.

Every image attachment is permanently associated with a parent article through the discussion_board_article_id foreign key. When the parent article is deleted, all associated images are automatically removed through cascade deletion. Images are uploaded by members (tracked via uploaded_by_member_id) and support soft deletion through the deleted_at timestamp, allowing recovery and audit trail maintenance.

The schema captures both user-facing metadata (original filename, dimensions, file size) and internal storage details (stored filename, MIME type) necessary for secure file management. Image dimensions are validated during upload to ensure they meet minimum readable size (50x50 pixels) and do not exceed maximum practical size (8000x8000 pixels). File sizes are limited to 5MB per image to balance quality with storage and bandwidth considerations.

This response schema is returned when retrieving image details, after successful image uploads, and when listing article attachments. It provides clients with complete information needed for display, download, and management operations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the document attachment.

This is the primary key automatically generated by the system when a document is uploaded and attached to an article. It serves as the permanent reference for this specific document attachment throughout its lifecycle.

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Reference to the parent article this document is attached to.

This foreign key links the document to its parent article in the discussion_board_articles table. Every document attachment must belong to exactly one article. The relationship is enforced with cascade deletion - when an article is deleted, all its document attachments are automatically removed.

Kept as raw ID because this is a hierarchical parent FK - the parent article already contains this document in its documents array, so the child should not expand back to the parent to prevent circular references.

uploaded_by_member_id.description:
Reference to the member who uploaded this document attachment.

This foreign key tracks accountability for document uploads, linking to the discussion_board_members table. It records which user added this supporting material to the article, which is essential for moderation purposes and understanding content provenance. The uploader may be the article author or a moderator adding documentation to enhance the discussion.

original_name.description:
Original filename of the uploaded document as provided by the user.

This preserves the document's original name exactly as it appeared on the user's system (e.g., 'Federal_Reserve_Report_2024.pdf', 'Economic_Analysis.docx'). The original filename is displayed to users when viewing attachments and used as the default filename when downloading the document, maintaining familiarity and context for readers.

stored_name.description:
Unique filename used for internal storage to prevent conflicts and ensure security.

This is a system-generated filename (typically a UUID or hash-based name) used to store the file in the backend storage system. Using unique stored names prevents filename collisions when multiple users upload files with the same name, enhances security by obscuring actual file locations, and enables efficient file management. This field is for internal system use and typically not displayed to end users.

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the document file for validation and proper content delivery.

Indicates the document format such as 'application/pdf' for PDF files, 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document' for DOCX files, 'application/msword' for DOC files, 'text/plain' for TXT files, 'application/rtf' for RTF files, or 'application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text' for ODT files. This information is used to validate that the uploaded file matches supported formats, set appropriate HTTP Content-Type headers when serving the file, and help browsers handle the file correctly (inline viewing for PDFs, download prompt for Word documents, etc.).

size_bytes.description:
File size in bytes of the document attachment.

Represents the exact size of the document file stored in the system. This value is used to enforce the maximum file size limit of 10MB (10,485,760 bytes) per document during upload validation, calculate total attachment size to enforce the 100MB limit per article, and display file size information to users before they download documents (helping users make informed decisions about downloads, especially on limited bandwidth connections). The size is measured in bytes for precision.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the document was uploaded to the system.

Automatically recorded when the document attachment record is created in the database. This timestamp indicates when the document was added to the article, which may be during initial article creation or later through editing. The timestamp is displayed to users to provide context about when supporting materials were added and is used for sorting attachments chronologically in article views.

deleted_at.description:
Soft delete timestamp marking when the document was removed from the article.

When a document is deleted (by the article author, moderator, or through article deletion), this field is set to the deletion timestamp rather than permanently removing the record. Null indicates the document is currently active and accessible. Soft deletion enables audit trails for moderation actions, potential recovery of accidentally deleted documents, and maintaining referential integrity in moderation logs. Soft-deleted documents are excluded from normal queries and not accessible to regular users, but moderators may view them for audit purposes.

uploader.description:
Summary information about the member who uploaded this document attachment.

Provides identification of who added this supporting material to the article, including the uploader's username, display name, and basic profile information. This attribution is important for accountability, especially when documents are added by moderators during content enhancement or when multiple contributors work on an article. The summary format prevents excessive nesting while providing essential user identification.

IDiscussionBoardArticleDocument.description:
Complete representation of a document attachment within a discussion board article.

This entity represents document files (PDF, DOCX, DOC, TXT, RTF, ODT) that members attach to their articles as supporting evidence, research papers, policy documents, or reference materials for economic and political discussions. Document attachments enhance articles by providing downloadable resources that readers can review for detailed information, data, or primary sources.

Each document attachment maintains comprehensive metadata including the original filename for user display, a unique stored filename for secure internal storage, MIME type for proper content delivery, file size for user information and validation, upload tracking information, and soft deletion support for audit trails. The entity tracks both the article it belongs to (via discussion_board_article_id) and the member who uploaded it (via uploader reference), enabling proper access control and accountability.

Document attachments are subject to validation rules including maximum 10MB per document file, maximum 5 document attachments per article, total attachment limit of 100MB per article (combined images and documents), and allowed formats limited to PDF, Word documents, and text-based formats. The system validates files by both MIME type and actual content to prevent format spoofing.

This entity supports the core platform value proposition of evidence-based discussion by enabling users to attach authoritative documents directly to their articles, making supporting materials immediately accessible without requiring external links or separate hosting. Documents are displayed as downloadable links with file metadata, helping readers access and verify the evidence underlying article claims.

title.description:
Updated article title or headline.

The article title must be between 5 and 200 characters long. When updating the title, the system validates length constraints and ensures the title contains meaningful content rather than only whitespace or special characters. The updated title will be reflected in all article listings and the article detail page.

body.description:
Updated main article content and body text.

The full text content of the article must be between 20 and 50,000 characters. When updating the body, the system preserves paragraph breaks and basic formatting while sanitizing HTML input to prevent security vulnerabilities. The updated content becomes the current version of the article.

summary.description:
Updated article excerpt or summary.

An optional brief summary or excerpt, limited to 500 characters maximum. This field can be updated to provide a better preview for article listings and search results. Setting this to null removes any existing summary.

oneOf.description:
Updated publication status of the article.

Changes the article's lifecycle state. Transitioning from 'published' to 'draft' removes the article from public view. Changing to 'archived' moves the article out of primary circulation. Only published articles appear in standard listings and search results.

Updated publication status of the article.

Changes the article's lifecycle state. Transitioning from 'published' to 'draft' removes the article from public view. Changing to 'archived' moves the article out of primary circulation. Only published articles appear in standard listings and search results.

status.description:
Updated publication status of the article.

Changes the article's lifecycle state. Transitioning from 'published' to 'draft' removes the article from public view. Changing to 'archived' moves the article out of primary circulation. Only published articles appear in standard listings and search results.

category_ids.description:
Updated category associations for this article.

Array of category IDs from the discussion_board_categories table to classify this article's subject matter. Articles must have at least one category. When updating, the system replaces all existing category associations (via discussion_board_article_categories junction table) with the new set of categories provided.

tag_ids.description:
Updated tag associations for this article.

Array of tag IDs from the discussion_board_tags table providing granular topic keywords. Maximum 5 tags allowed per article. When updating, the system replaces all existing tag associations (via discussion_board_article_tags junction table) with the new set of tags. This field is optional and can be an empty array to remove all tags.

add_image_ids.description:
Image attachments to add to the article.

Array of image IDs from the discussion_board_article_images table to attach to this article. The system validates that adding these images will not exceed the maximum limit of 10 images per article. Each referenced image must exist and must not already be associated with another article.

remove_image_ids.description:
Image attachments to remove from the article.

Array of image IDs currently associated with this article that should be removed. The system soft-deletes these images by setting their deleted_at timestamp, removing them from the article view while preserving records for audit purposes. Removed images are deleted from file storage.

add_document_ids.description:
Document attachments to add to the article.

Array of document IDs from the discussion_board_article_documents table to attach to this article. The system validates that adding these documents will not exceed the maximum limit of 5 documents per article. Each referenced document must exist and must not already be associated with another article.

remove_document_ids.description:
Document attachments to remove from the article.

Array of document IDs currently associated with this article that should be removed. The system soft-deletes these documents by setting their deleted_at timestamp, removing them from the article view while preserving records for audit purposes. Removed documents are deleted from file storage.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate.description:
Update request for modifying an existing discussion board article.

This type defines the structure for article update operations, allowing modification of article content, metadata, categorization, and attachment management. All fields are optional, enabling partial updates where only specific aspects of the article are changed. The operation enforces strict ownership validation ensuring only the original author or moderators can update articles.

When an article is updated, the system creates a snapshot in the discussion_board_article_snapshots table to preserve the previous version for audit trail and version control purposes. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time while preserving the immutable created_at timestamp.

Content updates support modifying the title (5-200 characters), body text (20-50,000 characters), and optional summary (max 500 characters). All text content is validated and sanitized to prevent security vulnerabilities while preserving user-intended formatting.

Categorization updates allow reassigning articles to different categories by providing a new set of category IDs. The system validates that all referenced categories exist in the discussion_board_categories table and maintains the many-to-many relationship through the discussion_board_article_categories junction table. At least one category must be assigned.

Tag updates enable adding, removing, or replacing tags by providing a new set of tag IDs. Maximum 5 tags are allowed per article. The system validates tag references against the discussion_board_tags table and manages associations through the discussion_board_article_tags junction table.

Attachment management supports independent addition and removal of images and documents through separate array fields. When adding attachments, the system validates against maximum limits (10 images, 5 documents) including existing attachments. When removing attachments, the system soft-deletes the referenced files by setting deleted_at timestamps and cleans up storage resources.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve in the paginated response. Page numbering starts at 1 for the first page. When combined with limit, this determines the offset for result retrieval.

Must be a positive integer. Defaults to 1 if not specified.

limit.description:
Number of items per page.

Specifies how many image attachment records to return in a single page of results. This controls the page size for pagination and affects response payload size and loading performance.

Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20 if not specified. Lower values improve initial response time, while higher values reduce the number of requests needed to retrieve all results.

search.description:
Keyword search term for filtering images.

Searches across image metadata fields including original filename. Enables users to find specific images by name or keyword. Search is case-insensitive and supports partial matching.

Optional parameter. When not provided, no keyword filtering is applied.

mime_type.description:
Filter by specific MIME type.

Restricts results to images with the specified MIME type such as image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, or image/webp. Enables filtering by image format.

Optional parameter. When not provided, all supported image formats are included in results.

min_width.description:
Minimum image width in pixels.

Filters results to include only images with width greater than or equal to this value. Useful for finding images of sufficient resolution for specific display purposes.

Optional parameter. Must be a non-negative integer if provided.

max_width.description:
Maximum image width in pixels.

Filters results to include only images with width less than or equal to this value. Useful for finding smaller images or excluding very large images.

Optional parameter. Must be a non-negative integer if provided. Should be greater than min_width if both are specified.

min_height.description:
Minimum image height in pixels.

Filters results to include only images with height greater than or equal to this value. Useful for finding images of sufficient resolution for specific display purposes.

Optional parameter. Must be a non-negative integer if provided.

max_height.description:
Maximum image height in pixels.

Filters results to include only images with height less than or equal to this value. Useful for finding smaller images or excluding very large images.

Optional parameter. Must be a non-negative integer if provided. Should be greater than min_height if both are specified.

min_size_bytes.description:
Minimum file size in bytes.

Filters results to include only images with file size greater than or equal to this value. Useful for finding higher quality images or excluding very small images.

Optional parameter. Must be a non-negative integer if provided.

max_size_bytes.description:
Maximum file size in bytes.

Filters results to include only images with file size less than or equal to this value. Useful for finding smaller images or excluding very large images. Cannot exceed 5MB (5,242,880 bytes), which is the system maximum for individual image files.

Optional parameter. Must be a non-negative integer if provided. Should be greater than min_size_bytes if both are specified.

uploaded_after.description:
Filter images uploaded after this timestamp.

Restricts results to images with created_at timestamp after the specified date and time. Useful for finding recently added images or images added within a specific timeframe.

Optional parameter. Must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string if provided.

uploaded_before.description:
Filter images uploaded before this timestamp.

Restricts results to images with created_at timestamp before the specified date and time. Useful for finding older images or images added within a specific timeframe.

Optional parameter. Must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string if provided. Should be later than uploaded_after if both are specified.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort results by.

Specifies which field to use for ordering the results. Supported sort fields include created_at (upload timestamp), size_bytes (file size), width (image width in pixels), and height (image height in pixels).

Optional parameter. Defaults to created_at if not specified. Must be used with sort_order to control ascending or descending order.

Field to sort results by.

Specifies which field to use for ordering the results. Supported sort fields include created_at (upload timestamp), size_bytes (file size), width (image width in pixels), and height (image height in pixels).

Optional parameter. Defaults to created_at if not specified. Must be used with sort_order to control ascending or descending order.

Field to sort results by.

Specifies which field to use for ordering the results. Supported sort fields include created_at (upload timestamp), size_bytes (file size), width (image width in pixels), and height (image height in pixels).

Optional parameter. Defaults to created_at if not specified. Must be used with sort_order to control ascending or descending order.

Field to sort results by.

Specifies which field to use for ordering the results. Supported sort fields include created_at (upload timestamp), size_bytes (file size), width (image width in pixels), and height (image height in pixels).

Optional parameter. Defaults to created_at if not specified. Must be used with sort_order to control ascending or descending order.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by.

Specifies which field to use for ordering the results. Supported sort fields include created_at (upload timestamp), size_bytes (file size), width (image width in pixels), and height (image height in pixels).

Optional parameter. Defaults to created_at if not specified. Must be used with sort_order to control ascending or descending order.

oneOf.description:
Sort order direction.

Specifies whether results should be sorted in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order based on the sort_by field. Ascending order shows smallest/earliest values first, descending shows largest/latest values first.

Optional parameter. Defaults to desc (descending) if not specified, showing newest/largest values first.

Sort order direction.

Specifies whether results should be sorted in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order based on the sort_by field. Ascending order shows smallest/earliest values first, descending shows largest/latest values first.

Optional parameter. Defaults to desc (descending) if not specified, showing newest/largest values first.

sort_order.description:
Sort order direction.

Specifies whether results should be sorted in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order based on the sort_by field. Ascending order shows smallest/earliest values first, descending shows largest/latest values first.

Optional parameter. Defaults to desc (descending) if not specified, showing newest/largest values first.

include_deleted.description:
Whether to include soft-deleted images in the results.

When false or omitted (default), only active images (deleted_at is null) are returned. When set to true, the results include both active and soft-deleted images. This parameter is primarily useful for moderators reviewing image deletion history or recovering accidentally deleted attachments.

Regular users should always see only active images, so this should typically be restricted to moderator access or ignored for non-moderator requests. Images with non-null deleted_at timestamps are considered soft-deleted and normally excluded from query results to maintain content integrity and user experience.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and filtering parameters for querying article image attachments.

This request DTO provides comprehensive filtering, pagination, and sorting capabilities for retrieving image attachments associated with a specific discussion board article. It supports queries based on image metadata including dimensions, file size, MIME type, upload date, and other properties. The request parameters enable users to efficiently browse and search through article images with flexible filtering options.

All properties are optional, allowing for simple queries (retrieve all images) as well as complex filtered searches. When multiple filters are specified, they are combined with AND logic - results must match all specified criteria. The pagination parameters (page and limit) control result set size and offset, while sort parameters determine the ordering of returned records.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the article image attachment.

This is the primary key that uniquely identifies this specific image attachment record within the discussion board system.

url.description:
Download URL for accessing the actual image file.

This URL provides direct access to the stored image file, enabling users to view and download the image. The URL is constructed from the stored_name field which contains the unique system-generated filename in the storage system (S3, CDN, or file server).

The URL follows AutoBE's URL-only file handling pattern where file references are exposed as complete URLs rather than requiring clients to construct paths. This approach simplifies client implementation and enables flexible storage backend changes without affecting API contracts.

Security considerations: The URL may be a signed URL with expiration for private content, or a public CDN URL for published article attachments. Access control is enforced at the URL generation level based on article visibility and user permissions. The URL should be treated as opaque by clients and not parsed or manipulated.

Clients use this URL to display images inline in articles, provide download links in the user interface, enable full-resolution image viewing in modals or lightboxes, and implement image preloading for performance optimization. Without this URL field, clients cannot access the actual image file content.

original_name.description:
Original filename of the uploaded image as provided by the user.

This preserves the user's original file naming for display purposes and helps users identify the image content. The filename is stored separately from the system-generated stored_name used for actual file storage.

Example values: 'economic_chart_2024.png', 'policy_analysis_graph.jpg', 'trade_data_visualization.webp'

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the image file for validation and proper content delivery.

Valid values include image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, and image/webp. This ensures the browser handles the image correctly and allows the system to validate file types during upload.

The MIME type is validated against both the file extension and actual file content to prevent security issues.

size_bytes.description:
File size in bytes for the uploaded image.

Maximum allowed size is 5MB (5,242,880 bytes) for images as defined in the file storage requirements. This information is displayed to users so they can make informed decisions before downloading.

Used for validation during upload and for displaying human-readable file sizes in the UI (e.g., '2.3 MB', '450 KB').

width.description:
Image width in pixels.

Used for validation (minimum 50px, maximum 8000px as per requirements) and display optimization. This helps the system determine appropriate display sizes and ensures images meet quality standards.

The width is extracted during upload and stored for efficient image rendering without needing to read the file each time.

height.description:
Image height in pixels.

Used for validation (minimum 50px, maximum 8000px as per requirements) and display optimization. Combined with width, this allows calculation of aspect ratio for proper image scaling.

The height is extracted during upload and stored for efficient image rendering and layout calculations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the image was uploaded to the system.

Automatically set when the image attachment is created. This timestamp helps track when supporting materials were added to articles and can be used for sorting attachments chronologically.

Displayed in ISO 8601 format for consistency across the API.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp marking when the image was removed from the article.

When a image is deleted by the article author, a moderator, or through parent article deletion, this field is set to the deletion timestamp rather than permanently removing the database record. A null value indicates the image is currently active and accessible to users.

Soft deletion enables several important capabilities including maintaining audit trails for moderation actions (tracking when and why images were removed), potential recovery of accidentally deleted images if removal was in error, preserving referential integrity in moderation logs and activity history, and supporting data retention policies for compliance purposes.

Images with non-null deleted_at timestamps are excluded from normal queries and article displays, hidden from public view, and treated as unavailable for download. However, moderators may have access to view soft-deleted images for audit and investigation purposes. The soft deletion approach balances data retention requirements for accountability with user expectations that deleted content is no longer accessible.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an article image attachment for efficient display in lists and embedded contexts.

This schema provides essential information about image attachments without including full relationship data or sensitive details. It includes the core identification fields, file metadata, display properties, and critically the URL for accessing the actual image file. This enables clients to render image attachments in article views, create download links, and display image galleries without requiring additional API calls.

Used in contexts where image attachment information is embedded within article responses or when listing attachments. Contains all information necessary to display and download the image, following AutoBE's URL-only file handling pattern where file access is provided through complete URLs rather than requiring path construction.

The summary excludes relational data like uploader information and parent article references to keep the payload lightweight, as these are typically available from the surrounding context. The inclusion of the url field is critical for file access and aligns with the pattern established in IDiscussionBoardArticleDocument.ISummary for consistency across file attachment types.

page.description:
Page number for pagination of document attachment results.

Specifies which page of document attachments to retrieve from the filtered result set. Page numbering starts at 1. Used in conjunction with limit to implement offset-based pagination. For example, page 1 with limit 20 retrieves documents 1-20, page 2 retrieves documents 21-40, and so on.

limit.description:
Maximum number of document attachments to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, determining how many document summary records are included in a single response. Typical values are 20, 50, or 100 depending on the use case. Lower values (20) provide faster response times and are suitable for initial views, while higher values (100) reduce the number of requests needed for large attachment lists. The maximum limit of 100 prevents excessive payload sizes and maintains reasonable response times.

search.description:
Keyword search query for filtering documents by filename or content metadata.

Enables searching within document original filenames to find specific attachments. For example, searching for 'budget' would return documents with names like 'Federal_Budget_Report.pdf' or 'Budget_Analysis_2024.docx'. The search is case-insensitive and supports partial matching to find documents even when users don't remember the exact filename. Minimum 2 characters prevents overly broad searches.

mime_types.description:
Filter documents by one or more MIME types to narrow results to specific file formats.

Allows filtering to show only certain document types. For example, specifying ['application/pdf'] returns only PDF attachments, while ['application/pdf', 'text/plain'] returns both PDFs and text files. Useful when users want to find documents in a specific format or exclude certain file types. The array can contain any combination of the supported document MIME types.

min_size_bytes.description:
Minimum file size filter in bytes for document attachments.

Filters results to include only documents with file size greater than or equal to this value. Useful for finding substantial documents while excluding small files. For example, setting this to 1048576 (1MB) would exclude smaller reference files and show only larger, more comprehensive documents.

max_size_bytes.description:
Maximum file size filter in bytes for document attachments.

Filters results to include only documents with file size less than or equal to this value. Useful for finding documents within specific size ranges. For example, setting this to 5242880 (5MB) would exclude very large files. The maximum possible value is 10MB (10,485,760 bytes) as this is the system-wide limit for document attachments.

uploaded_after.description:
Filter documents uploaded after this timestamp.

Enables date range filtering by specifying the earliest upload date to include in results. Documents uploaded at or after this timestamp will be included. Useful for finding recently added documents or tracking document additions over time. For example, setting this to the beginning of the current month shows all documents uploaded this month.

uploaded_before.description:
Filter documents uploaded before this timestamp.

Enables date range filtering by specifying the latest upload date to include in results. Documents uploaded at or before this timestamp will be included. Combined with uploaded_after, this creates a date range filter. For example, filtering for documents uploaded between two dates helps track document additions during a specific period or find historical attachments.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort document attachment results by.

Determines the primary sorting criterion for ordering results. Options include: 'created_at' to sort by upload date (most common, shows newest or oldest documents first), 'size_bytes' to sort by file size (useful for finding largest or smallest documents), and 'original_name' to sort alphabetically by filename (useful for organized browsing). The sort direction is controlled by the sort_order parameter.

Options include: 'created_at' to sort by upload date (most common, shows newest or oldest documents first), 'size_bytes' to sort by file size (useful for finding largest or smallest documents), and 'original_name' to sort alphabetically by filename (useful for organized browsing). The sort direction is controlled by the sort_order parameter.

Options include: 'created_at' to sort by upload date (most common, shows newest or oldest documents first), 'size_bytes' to sort by file size (useful for finding largest or smallest documents), and 'original_name' to sort alphabetically by filename (useful for organized browsing). The sort direction is controlled by the sort_order parameter.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort document attachment results by.

Determines the primary sorting criterion for ordering results. Options include: 'created_at' to sort by upload date (most common, shows newest or oldest documents first), 'size_bytes' to sort by file size (useful for finding largest or smallest documents), and 'original_name' to sort alphabetically by filename (useful for organized browsing). The sort direction is controlled by the sort_order parameter.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for ordering document attachment results.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order based on the sort_by field. For created_at sorting, 'desc' shows newest documents first (most common), while 'asc' shows oldest first. For size_bytes, 'desc' shows largest files first, while 'asc' shows smallest. For original_name, 'desc' provides reverse alphabetical (Z-A), while 'asc' provides standard alphabetical (A-Z) ordering.
