Specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order based on the sort_by field. For created_at sorting, 'desc' shows newest documents first (most common), while 'asc' shows oldest first. For size_bytes, 'desc' shows largest files first, while 'asc' shows smallest. For original_name, 'desc' provides reverse alphabetical (Z-A), while 'asc' provides standard alphabetical (A-Z) ordering.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for ordering document attachment results.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order based on the sort_by field. For created_at sorting, 'desc' shows newest documents first (most common), while 'asc' shows oldest first. For size_bytes, 'desc' shows largest files first, while 'asc' shows smallest. For original_name, 'desc' provides reverse alphabetical (Z-A), while 'asc' provides standard alphabetical (A-Z) ordering.

include_deleted.description:
Whether to include soft-deleted documents in the results.

When false or omitted (default), only active documents (deleted_at is null) are returned. When set to true, the results include both active and soft-deleted documents. This parameter is primarily useful for moderators reviewing document deletion history or recovering accidentally deleted attachments. Regular users should always see only active documents, so this should typically be restricted to moderator access.

IDiscussionBoardArticleDocument.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching, filtering, sorting, and paginating document attachments within an article.

This DTO defines the request parameters for retrieving a filtered and paginated list of document attachments associated with a specific article. It supports comprehensive search and filtering capabilities to help users find specific documents among an article's attachments based on various criteria including filename keywords, file formats, file sizes, and upload dates.

All parameters in this DTO are optional, providing flexibility in how users query document attachments. When no parameters are specified, the operation returns all active (non-deleted) documents for the article in the default sort order (newest first, based on created_at descending). Users can combine multiple filter parameters to create precise queries, such as finding all PDF documents larger than 1MB uploaded in the last month.

Pagination parameters (page and limit) control result set size and enable efficient navigation through large attachment collections. The default pagination (page 1, limit 20) provides a reasonable balance between payload size and user convenience. For articles with many documents, users can adjust the limit or navigate through pages to explore all attachments.

Search capabilities allow filtering by original filename, enabling users to quickly locate specific documents without scanning through all attachments. The MIME type filter helps users find documents in particular formats, which is useful when looking for downloadable reports (PDFs) versus editable documents (DOCX) or plain text references.

File size filtering supports finding documents within specific size ranges, helpful for users on limited bandwidth who want to identify smaller documents or for those seeking comprehensive reports which tend to be larger files. Date range filtering enables temporal queries such as finding documents added recently or tracking when supporting materials were attached to an article.

Sorting options provide different views of the document collection. Sorting by upload date (created_at) shows chronological addition order, sorting by file size helps identify the largest or smallest documents, and alphabetical sorting by filename aids in organized browsing when documents follow naming conventions.

The include_deleted parameter is a special flag for moderators to view deletion history and audit trails. Regular users should never see soft-deleted documents, so this parameter should be restricted to moderator endpoints or ignored for non-moderator requests.

Security considerations: This DTO does not include the parent article ID or uploader member ID as filters because the article ID comes from the path parameter (ensuring the query is scoped to a specific article), and filtering by uploader should be done through other mechanisms if needed. The DTO does not accept any user identity fields from the request body, maintaining secure access control through path parameters and authentication context.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the article document attachment.

This is the primary key that uniquely identifies this specific document attachment record within the discussion board system.

url.description:
Download URL for accessing the actual document file.

This URL provides direct access to the stored document file, enabling users to download or view the attachment. The URL is constructed from the stored_name field which contains the unique system-generated filename in the storage system (S3, CDN, or file server).

The URL follows AutoBE's URL-only file handling pattern where file references are exposed as complete URLs rather than requiring clients to construct paths. This approach simplifies client implementation and enables flexible storage backend changes without affecting API contracts.

Security considerations: The URL may be a signed URL with expiration for private content, or a public CDN URL for published article attachments. Access control is enforced at the URL generation level based on article visibility and user permissions. The URL should be treated as opaque by clients and not parsed or manipulated.

Clients use this URL to provide download links in the user interface, enable document preview in browsers for supported formats like PDF, and implement download functionality for formats that browsers download directly like DOCX or TXT files.

original_name.description:
Original filename of the uploaded document as provided by the user.

This preserves the user's original file naming for display purposes and helps users identify the document content. The filename is stored separately from the system-generated stored_name used for actual file storage.

Example values: 'research_paper.pdf', 'policy_proposal.docx', 'economic_data.txt'

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the document file for validation and proper content delivery.

Valid values include application/pdf, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document (DOCX), application/msword (DOC), text/plain (TXT), application/rtf (RTF), and application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text (ODT).

This ensures the browser handles the document correctly and allows the system to validate file types during upload. The MIME type is validated against both the file extension and actual file content to prevent security issues.

size_bytes.description:
File size in bytes for the uploaded document.

Maximum allowed size is 10MB (10,485,760 bytes) for documents as defined in the file storage requirements. This information is displayed to users so they can make informed decisions before downloading.

Used for validation during upload and for displaying human-readable file sizes in the UI (e.g., '8.5 MB', '1.2 MB', '500 KB').

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the document was uploaded to the system.

Automatically set when the document attachment is created. This timestamp helps track when supporting materials were added to articles and can be used for sorting attachments chronologically.

Displayed in ISO 8601 format for consistency across the API.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp marking when the document was removed from the article.

When a document is deleted by the article author, a moderator, or through parent article deletion, this field is set to the deletion timestamp rather than permanently removing the database record. A null value indicates the document is currently active and accessible to users.

Soft deletion enables several important capabilities including maintaining audit trails for moderation actions (tracking when and why documents were removed), potential recovery of accidentally deleted documents if removal was in error, preserving referential integrity in moderation logs and activity history, and supporting GDPR compliance by allowing document removal while maintaining enforcement records.

Documents with non-null deleted_at timestamps are excluded from normal queries and article displays, hidden from public view, and treated as unavailable for download. However, moderators may have access to view soft-deleted documents for audit and investigation purposes. The soft deletion approach balances data retention requirements for accountability with user expectations that deleted content is no longer accessible.

IDiscussionBoardArticleDocument.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an article document attachment for efficient display in lists and embedded contexts.

This schema provides essential information about document attachments without including full relationship data or sensitive details. It includes the core identification fields and file metadata needed for rendering document attachments in article views and providing download functionality.

Used in contexts where document attachment information is embedded within article responses or when listing attachments. Contains all information necessary to display file details and enable downloads.

The summary excludes relational data like uploader information and parent article references to keep the payload lightweight, as these are typically available from the surrounding context. Unlike image attachments, documents do not have dimension properties (width/height) as they are provided as downloadable links rather than inline displays.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the comment.

This system-generated UUID serves as the primary key for the comment record in the discussion_board_comments table. It uniquely identifies this comment across the entire system and is used for referencing the comment in edit operations, delete operations, reply threading, and moderation actions.

The ID is automatically generated upon comment creation and remains immutable throughout the comment's lifecycle.

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Unique identifier of the parent article this comment belongs to.

This foreign key reference links the comment to its parent article in the discussion_board_articles table. Every comment must be associated with a specific article, as comments represent user responses and discussions about article content.

This field is immutable after comment creation and ensures referential integrity. When the parent article is deleted, all associated comments are cascade deleted to maintain data consistency.

discussion_board_parent_comment_id.description:
Unique identifier of the parent comment for single-level reply threading.

This optional foreign key reference enables the single-level threading feature of the comment system. When null, the comment is a top-level comment (direct response to the article). When populated, the comment is a reply to another top-level comment.

The system enforces single-level threading by ensuring that if this field is populated, it must reference a top-level comment (a comment where discussion_board_parent_comment_id is null). Replies to replies are not supported - the system prevents deep nesting by posting such comments as replies to the original top-level comment instead.

This field is immutable after comment creation to maintain thread structure integrity.

discussion_board_member_id.description:
Member author identifier when the comment was created by a member.

This foreign key references discussion_board_members.id and is populated when author_type is 'member'. The field is mutually exclusive with discussion_board_moderator_id - exactly one must be populated based on the author_type discriminator.

When author_type is 'member', this field contains the UUID of the member who created the comment, and discussion_board_moderator_id is null. When author_type is 'moderator', this field is null and discussion_board_moderator_id is populated instead.

This field works in conjunction with the author_type discriminator to implement polymorphic authorship, allowing comments to be created by either members or moderators while maintaining proper referential integrity and enabling efficient author information retrieval through the appropriate actor table.

discussion_board_moderator_id.description:
Moderator author identifier when the comment was created by a moderator.

This foreign key references discussion_board_moderators.id and is populated when author_type is 'moderator'. The field is mutually exclusive with discussion_board_member_id - exactly one must be populated based on the author_type discriminator.

When author_type is 'moderator', this field contains the UUID of the moderator who created the comment, and discussion_board_member_id is null. When author_type is 'member', this field is null and discussion_board_member_id is populated instead.

This field works in conjunction with the author_type discriminator to implement polymorphic authorship, allowing comments to be created by either members or moderators while maintaining proper referential integrity and enabling efficient author information retrieval through the appropriate actor table.

author_type.description:
Discriminator indicating the type of author who created this comment.

Valid values are 'member' or 'moderator'. This field determines which author foreign key is populated: when author_type is 'member', the discussion_board_member_id field contains the author's ID and discussion_board_moderator_id is null; when author_type is 'moderator', the discussion_board_moderator_id field contains the author's ID and discussion_board_member_id is null.

This discriminator pattern enables polymorphic authorship where comments can be created by either members or moderators while maintaining referential integrity and proper attribution.

content.description:
Comment text content submitted by the user.

This field contains the full text of the comment, representing the user's response to the article or their reply to another comment. Content length is validated to be between 1 and 5000 characters, excluding leading and trailing whitespace. The system preserves line breaks and basic text formatting while sanitizing HTML input to prevent XSS attacks.

Comments provide a mechanism for discussion and engagement on economic and political topics, allowing users to share perspectives, ask questions, and debate article content. The content is displayed chronologically in the comment section of the parent article, with replies visually indented beneath their parent comments.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was originally posted.

This system-generated timestamp records when the comment was first created and submitted to the discussion board. It is automatically set upon comment creation and remains immutable throughout the comment's lifecycle.

The creation timestamp is used for chronological ordering of comments (default sort: oldest first for conversation flow), display of relative posting times to users (e.g., '2 hours ago'), and audit trail tracking of discussion timelines.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was last modified.

This system-managed timestamp is automatically updated whenever the comment content is edited by the author or a moderator. When the comment has never been edited, this value equals created_at. When edits occur, this timestamp advances to reflect the most recent modification.

The updated_at timestamp is used to display 'edited' indicators to readers, track modification history in conjunction with comment snapshots, and sort comments by most recently active when that sorting option is selected.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the comment was deleted.

When null, the comment is active and visible to users. When set to a timestamp, the comment has been soft-deleted and is hidden from public view while retained in the database for audit trail and potential recovery purposes.

Comments can be deleted by their original author or by moderators. When a top-level comment is deleted, all its replies are also hidden to maintain thread coherence. Soft deletion enables moderation review, comment recovery if deletion was inappropriate, and maintains referential integrity for moderation logs and snapshots.

memberAuthor.description:
Summary information of the member who authored this comment.

This field is populated when author_type is 'member', providing essential profile information about the comment author for display purposes. The summary includes the member's username, display name, profile picture URL, and basic metadata.

When author_type is 'moderator', this field is null and the moderatorAuthor field is populated instead. This mutual exclusivity is enforced by the author_type discriminator pattern.

moderatorAuthor.description:
Summary information of the moderator who authored this comment.

This field is populated when author_type is 'moderator', providing essential profile information about the moderator author for display purposes. The summary includes the moderator's username, display name, profile picture URL, and basic metadata.

When author_type is 'member', this field is null and the memberAuthor field is populated instead. This mutual exclusivity is enforced by the author_type discriminator pattern.

IDiscussionBoardComment.description:
Complete discussion board comment entity with full content, metadata, and author information.

This DTO represents a comment on a discussion board article in its entirety, including the comment text, authorship attribution, threading relationship, timestamps, and deletion status. Comments are the primary mechanism for user engagement and discussion on economic and political topics shared through articles.

The comment system supports single-level threading where comments can be top-level responses to articles (discussion_board_parent_comment_id is null) or replies to other top-level comments (discussion_board_parent_comment_id references another comment). This threading structure enables focused discussions while maintaining simplicity by preventing deep nested conversation chains.

Comments can be authored by either members or moderators, with the author_type field acting as a discriminator to determine which author reference is populated. When author_type is 'member', the discussion_board_member_id field contains the member's UUID, the memberAuthor field contains the member's profile summary, the discussion_board_moderator_id field is null, and the moderatorAuthor field is null. When author_type is 'moderator', the discussion_board_moderator_id field contains the moderator's UUID, the moderatorAuthor field contains the moderator's profile summary, the discussion_board_member_id field is null, and the memberAuthor field is null.

Comment lifecycle includes creation with automatic timestamping, optional editing by the author or moderators with tracked updates, soft deletion that hides the comment from public view while preserving it for audit purposes, and snapshot creation for every edit to maintain complete version history. The deleted_at timestamp indicates whether a comment is active (null) or has been soft-deleted (timestamp present).

Comments are displayed chronologically beneath their parent articles, with replies visually indented beneath their parent comments to show the discussion structure. Each comment displays the author's profile information, posting time, content, and an 'edited' indicator if the updated_at timestamp differs from created_at.

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Unique identifier of the parent article this comment belongs to.

This field references the discussion_board_articles.id and establishes which article the comment is posted on. While this value is typically derived from the articleId path parameter in API operations, it represents a fundamental part of the comment's data model and is stored in the discussion_board_comments table.

The system validates that the referenced article exists, is accessible (published status), and is not soft-deleted before allowing comment creation. This ensures comments are only posted on valid, active articles.

discussion_board_parent_comment_id.description:
Optional reference to parent comment for single-level reply threading.

When creating a top-level comment (direct response to the article), this field should be null. When creating a reply to an existing comment, this field should contain the UUID of the parent comment. The system enforces single-level threading by validating that parent comments are themselves top-level (have null parent_comment_id).

content.description:
Text content of the comment to be created.

Must be between 1 and 5000 characters as per system requirements. The content is sanitized by the backend to prevent XSS attacks while preserving basic text formatting. This field contains the user's response to the article or reply to another comment, supporting substantive discussion on economic and political topics.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a new comment on a discussion board article.

This schema defines the minimal information needed from the client to post a comment. The backend automatically populates several fields from the authentication context and system state: the author_type discriminator and corresponding discussion_board_member_id or discussion_board_moderator_id are set based on the authenticated user's role from the JWT token, and system timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are automatically generated.

The discussion_board_article_id identifies the parent article and is typically provided via the articleId path parameter in API operations, though it is included here for completeness as it is a required field in the discussion_board_comments table. The discussion_board_parent_comment_id field is optional - it should be null for top-level comments and contain the parent comment UUID for replies. The system validates this field to ensure single-level threading constraints are respected.

Security note: The authenticated user's identity is never accepted from the request body but always extracted from the verified JWT token to prevent impersonation attacks.

content.description:
Updated comment text content.

This field contains the revised text of the comment. The content must be between 1 and 5000 characters in length, as specified in the comment system requirements. All user-submitted content is sanitized to prevent XSS attacks while preserving basic text formatting such as line breaks and paragraph structure.

The system validates that the content is not empty or composed only of whitespace characters. When a comment is successfully updated, the system records the modification timestamp and creates a snapshot in discussion_board_comment_snapshots to maintain a complete audit trail of all edits.

If the edit is performed by a moderator on another user's comment, the moderation action is logged separately in the discussion_board_moderation_actions table for accountability and audit purposes.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing discussion board comment.

This DTO represents the data required to modify the content of a previously posted comment on a discussion board article. It supports the comment editing functionality where members can edit their own comments and moderators can edit any comment regardless of authorship.

The update operation is intentionally minimal, allowing only content modification. Other comment properties such as the parent article, parent comment (for reply threading), author information, and timestamps are immutable and managed by the system. This design ensures data integrity and maintains accurate audit trails.

All fields in this update DTO are optional following the partial update pattern, allowing clients to send only the fields they wish to modify. However, in practice, comment updates typically involve content changes, as other metadata cannot be altered through this operation.

oneOf.description:
Filter by the specific member who submitted the report.

When provided, restricts results to reports where the discussion_board_member_id matches this value. This is useful for investigating reporting patterns by specific members, assessing reporter credibility and history, or following up on concerns raised by particular community members.

The filter performs exact UUID matching against the reporter's member ID in the discussion_board_reports table. This differs from reporter_username which filters by username string - this field provides more precise filtering when the member ID is already known.

When null or omitted, returns reports from all members.
Null when filtering by reporter member ID is not desired.

discussion_board_member_id.description:
Filter by the specific member who submitted the report.

When provided, restricts results to reports where the discussion_board_member_id matches this value. This is useful for investigating reporting patterns by specific members, assessing reporter credibility and history, or following up on concerns raised by particular community members.

The filter performs exact UUID matching against the reporter's member ID in the discussion_board_reports table. This differs from reporter_username which filters by username string - this field provides more precise filtering when the member ID is already known.

When null or omitted, returns reports from all members.

status.description:
Filter by report status.

This optional field allows moderators to filter the report queue by the current status of reports. Valid status values include: 'pending' for reports that have not yet been reviewed by any moderator, 'under_review' for reports currently being examined by a moderator, 'resolved' for reports where moderation action has been taken, and 'dismissed' for reports where no violation was found and no action was taken.

Status filtering is essential for efficient queue management, allowing moderators to focus on pending reports requiring attention, view reports being handled by colleagues, or reference previously resolved cases for consistency in decision-making.

report_reason.description:
Filter by the violation category reported.

This optional field enables filtering reports by the reason category selected by the reporter when submitting the report. Valid reason categories include: 'spam' for spam or advertising content, 'harassment' for harassment or bullying, 'hate_speech' for hate speech or discrimination, 'misinformation' for false or misleading information, 'off_topic' for irrelevant content, 'profanity' for inappropriate language, 'personal_info' for personal information disclosure, and 'other' for violations not covered by predefined categories.

Reason filtering helps moderators specialize or prioritize specific types of violations, identify patterns of abuse, and ensure consistent enforcement of specific community guidelines.

target_type.description:
Filter by the type of content being reported.

Valid values are 'article' or 'comment'. When set to 'article', only reports targeting discussion board articles (via reported_article_id) are returned. When set to 'comment', only reports targeting comments (via reported_comment_id) are returned.

This filter enables moderators to focus on specific content types, as article moderation may require different consideration than comment moderation. It helps organize the moderation workflow by content type.

from_date.description:
Start of date range filter for report submission time.

When provided, only reports created at or after this timestamp are included in results. Used in combination with to_date to filter reports within specific timeframes.

Date range filtering helps moderators review reports from specific time periods, identify temporal patterns in violations, and manage historical moderation data.

to_date.description:
End of date range filter for report submission time.

When provided, only reports created at or before this timestamp are included in results. Used in combination with from_date to filter reports within specific timeframes.

This enables moderators to focus on reports from recent periods or review historical moderation patterns.

reporter_username.description:
Filter by the username of the member who submitted the report.

This optional field enables moderators to view all reports submitted by a specific member. This is useful for investigating report abuse patterns, assessing reporter credibility, or following up on specific member concerns.

The username filter performs exact matching (case-insensitive) against the reporter's current username.

reviewing_moderator_username.description:
Filter by the username of the moderator currently reviewing or who resolved the report.

This optional field allows filtering to see which reports are assigned to specific moderators. It helps with workload distribution, enables moderators to find their assigned reports quickly, and allows senior moderators to review decisions made by specific team members.

The username filter performs exact matching (case-insensitive) against the reviewing moderator's current username.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by.

Valid values include: 'priority' to sort by report count (most-reported content first) for urgent cases, 'created_at' to sort chronologically by report submission time, 'updated_at' to sort by most recent activity or status changes, and 'status' to group reports by their current status.

The default sort order when not specified is 'priority' to ensure moderators address the most reported content first.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for the results.

Valid values are 'asc' for ascending order or 'desc' for descending order. When combined with sort_by, this determines the final ordering of results.

Default sort order depends on sort_by field: priority sorting defaults to descending (highest priority first), created_at sorting defaults to ascending (oldest first to prevent neglect), updated_at sorting defaults to descending (most recent activity first).

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve, with page numbering starting at 1. Combined with limit to implement offset-based pagination. When null or not provided, defaults to page 1.

Pagination is essential for moderation queue management, as the report list can grow large over time and loading all reports simultaneously would impact performance.

limit.description:
Number of reports to return per page.

Specifies the page size for pagination, with valid values of 25, 50, or 100 reports per page. The default when not specified is 50 reports per page, which balances moderator efficiency with manageable screen content.

Larger page sizes (100) are useful for experienced moderators who can process reports quickly, while smaller page sizes (25) may be preferred when reviewing complex cases requiring detailed examination.

IDiscussionBoardReport.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for retrieving moderation reports.

This DTO defines the query parameters for filtering, sorting, and paginating the moderation report queue. It enables moderators to efficiently manage their workload by focusing on specific report types, statuses, or time periods.

All filter fields are optional, allowing moderators to view all reports when no filters are applied or create highly focused views by combining multiple filters. The flexible filtering system supports various moderation workflows including reviewing pending reports by priority, following up on specific violation types, checking reports from particular time periods, investigating reporter patterns, and reviewing decisions made by specific moderators.

The sorting system provides multiple options optimized for moderation workflows: priority sorting surfaces reports with multiple submissions first (most urgent), chronological sorting ensures older reports are not neglected, recent activity sorting helps moderators track ongoing cases, and status-based sorting enables batch processing of similar cases.

Pagination parameters (page and limit) control the result set size, balancing moderator efficiency with system performance. The default configuration (page 1, limit 50, sort by priority) is optimized for the most common moderation workflow: reviewing the most urgent pending reports first.

IDiscussionBoardReport.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a content report submitted by a member flagging articles or comments that potentially violate community guidelines.

This lightweight view is optimized for displaying reports in moderation queues and administrative dashboards. It provides essential information about the report including the reporter, reported content type, report reason, current status, and timestamps.

The summary includes content reference fields (reported_article_id and reported_comment_id) to enable moderators to navigate directly to the reported content without additional API calls. It also includes the report_details field providing access to the detailed explanation provided by the reporter beyond the categorical report_reason.

This type is used in report listing endpoints, moderation dashboards, and as embedded references in other moderation-related responses.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this report.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the report record and is used in all API operations that reference this specific report. It remains constant throughout the report's lifecycle from submission through resolution.

reporter.description:
Member who submitted this report.

Provides essential context about who flagged the content, including their username and basic profile information. This enables moderators to assess the reporter's credibility and track reporting patterns. The reporter's identity is visible to moderators for accountability but may be hidden from other users.

oneOf.description: Unique identifier of the reported article if this report targets an article.
Null when the report targets a comment instead of an article.

reported_article_id.description:
Reference to the reported article, if the report targets an article.

This field is populated with the article UUID when reported_content_type is 'article' and the report concerns an entire article. It is null when reported_content_type is 'comment' and the report targets a specific comment instead.

This direct reference enables moderators to navigate immediately to the reported article for review without requiring additional API calls to resolve the content. The field works in conjunction with reported_comment_id, where exactly one of these fields is non-null for each report, determined by the reported_content_type discriminator.

oneOf.description: Unique identifier of the reported comment if this report targets a comment.
Null when the report targets an article instead of a comment.

reported_comment_id.description:
Reference to the reported comment, if the report targets a comment.

This field is populated with the comment UUID when reported_content_type is 'comment' and the report concerns a specific comment. It is null when reported_content_type is 'article' and the report targets an entire article instead.

This direct reference enables moderators to navigate immediately to the reported comment in its article context for review without requiring additional API calls. The field works in conjunction with reported_article_id, where exactly one of these fields is non-null for each report, determined by the reported_content_type discriminator.

oneOf.description:
Type of content being reported.

Indicates whether the report targets an article or a comment, determining which content entity should be reviewed. This discriminator helps moderators understand the context and navigate to the appropriate content management interface.

Valid values are 'article' for reported articles or 'comment' for reported comments.

Type of content being reported.

Indicates whether the report targets an article or a comment, determining which content entity should be reviewed. This discriminator helps moderators understand the context and navigate to the appropriate content management interface.

Valid values are 'article' for reported articles or 'comment' for reported comments.

reported_content_type.description:
Type of content being reported.

Indicates whether the report targets an article or a comment, determining which content entity should be reviewed. This discriminator helps moderators understand the context and navigate to the appropriate content management interface.

Valid values are 'article' for reported articles or 'comment' for reported comments.

report_reason.description:
Category of the violation being reported.

Predefined violation category selected by the reporter from standard options such as spam, harassment, misinformation, offensive content, or off-topic. This categorization helps moderators prioritize reviews and apply consistent enforcement.

Common values include spam, harassment, hate_speech, misinformation, off_topic, inappropriate_language, personal_information_disclosure, and other.

oneOf.description: Detailed explanation provided by the reporter describing the specific violation.
Null when the reporter did not provide additional details beyond the category.

report_details.description:
Optional detailed explanation from the reporter describing why the content violates guidelines.

This field contains additional context beyond the categorical report_reason, providing moderators with the reporter's specific concerns and observations. When report_reason is 'other', this field typically contains the required explanation of the violation type. For other categories, it may provide helpful specifics like quotes of offensive language, explanation of why content is misleading, or context about why content is off-topic.

The report_details field aids moderator decision-making by offering the reporter's perspective and reasoning. It can highlight specific aspects of the content that moderators should focus on during review. While optional (can be null if the reporter provided no additional context), when present it significantly enhances the moderator's ability to understand and assess the reported violation quickly and accurately.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the report in the moderation workflow.

Tracks the report's progression through the review process. 'pending' indicates awaiting moderator review, 'under_review' means a moderator is actively examining the report, 'resolved' indicates action was taken on the violation, and 'dismissed' means no violation was found.

Status changes are recorded in the updated_at timestamp for tracking review times.

Status changes are recorded in the updated_at timestamp for tracking review times.

Status changes are recorded in the updated_at timestamp for tracking review times.

Tracks the report's progression through the review process. 'pending' indicates awaiting moderator review, 'under_review' means a moderator is actively examining the report, 'resolved' indicates action was taken on the violation, and 'dismissed' means no violation was found.

Status changes are recorded in the updated_at timestamp for tracking review times.

oneOf.description: Notes from the moderator explaining the decision or action taken on this report.
Null when the report has not yet been resolved or dismissed.

resolution_notes.description:
Moderator's explanation of the decision or action taken on this report.

Provides transparency and accountability for moderation decisions. When a report is resolved, these notes typically describe what enforcement action was taken such as content deleted, user warned, content edited to remove violations, or user suspended. When a report is dismissed, these notes explain why no violation was found such as content does not violate guidelines, report appears to be invalid, or context review shows no violation occurred.

These notes are visible to other moderators for consistency and training purposes, helping maintain uniform enforcement standards across the moderation team. Resolution notes may also be shared with the content author in some cases to explain why their content was modified or removed, supporting transparency in the moderation process.

This field is null for reports that are still pending or under review and have not yet reached a final decision. Once a moderator resolves or dismisses a report, they should provide clear resolution notes documenting their reasoning and any actions taken.

oneOf.description: Moderator currently reviewing or who resolved this report.
Null when the report is in pending status and has not been assigned.

reviewing_moderator.description:
Moderator currently reviewing or who resolved this report.

Provides information about which moderator claimed or processed this report. Null when the report is in pending status and has not been assigned. When populated, indicates the responsible moderator for accountability and workload tracking.

This field is set when a moderator opens the report for review and remains associated with the moderator who ultimately resolved or dismissed it.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the report was submitted.

Records the exact date and time the member flagged the content. This timestamp is crucial for measuring response times, prioritizing older reports, and tracking moderation performance metrics.

Reports pending for extended periods may be highlighted in moderation dashboards based on time elapsed since this timestamp.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the report was last modified.

Records when the report status changed, a moderator was assigned, or resolution was recorded. This timestamp helps track how long reports remain in each status and measures overall moderation response efficiency.

Updated whenever status transitions occur or moderator assignments change.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the report was soft deleted from the moderation system.
Null when the report is active and visible in moderation queues.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the report record.

When set, the report is hidden from active moderation queues but preserved in the system for historical audit trail and compliance purposes. A null value indicates the report is active and should appear in moderation dashboards and queue listings.

Reports may be soft deleted when they are determined to be spam reports, duplicate reports for the same content, or administrative cleanup of very old resolved reports. Soft deletion maintains referential integrity for related moderation actions and enables recovery if reports were deleted in error.

This field follows the soft deletion pattern used throughout the discussion board system for maintaining comprehensive audit trails while allowing content cleanup.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the content report.

This is the primary key auto-generated by the system when a report is submitted. It uniquely identifies each report throughout its lifecycle from submission through review to resolution or dismissal.

discussion_board_member_id.description:
Unique identifier of the member who submitted this report.

References the discussion_board_members table. This tracks which community member flagged the content as potentially violating guidelines. The reporter's identity is preserved for accountability and to prevent duplicate reports from the same user on the same content.

reported_article_id.description:
Unique identifier of the reported article, if the report targets an article.

References the discussion_board_articles table. This field is mutually exclusive with reported_comment_id - exactly one must be set to identify what content is being reported. When populated, this indicates the report concerns an entire article rather than a specific comment.

reported_comment_id.description:
Unique identifier of the reported comment, if the report targets a comment.

References the discussion_board_comments table. This field is mutually exclusive with reported_article_id - exactly one must be set to identify what content is being reported. When populated, this indicates the report concerns a specific comment rather than the entire article.

reviewing_moderator_id.description:
Unique identifier of the moderator currently reviewing or who resolved this report.

References the discussion_board_moderators table. This field is null when the report is in pending status and has not yet been claimed by a moderator. It is set when a moderator begins review (under_review status) and remains set after resolution or dismissal to track who handled the report.

report_reason.description:
Category of the violation being reported.

Predefined categories include: spam or advertising, harassment or bullying, hate speech or discrimination, misinformation or false information, off-topic or irrelevant content, inappropriate language or profanity, personal information disclosure, or other (requires explanation). This categorization helps moderators prioritize and route reports efficiently.

report_details.description:
Detailed explanation provided by the reporter describing why the content violates guidelines.

Optional additional context beyond the report_reason category. When report_reason is 'other', this field is required to explain the specific concern. For other categories, this field provides helpful context that assists moderators in understanding the reporter's perspective and making informed decisions.

status.description:
Current status of the report in the moderation workflow.

Valid values: pending (submitted but not yet reviewed), under_review (moderator is actively reviewing), resolved (moderator took action on the reported content), dismissed (moderator reviewed and determined no violation occurred). Status transitions typically follow: pending → under_review → resolved/dismissed. The status determines report visibility in moderation queues and dashboards.

resolution_notes.description:
Notes from the moderator explaining the decision or action taken on this report.

Provides transparency and accountability for moderation decisions. When a report is resolved, these notes typically describe what enforcement action was taken (content deleted, user warned, etc.). When a report is dismissed, these notes explain why no violation was found. Resolution notes are visible to other moderators for consistency and training purposes.

reporter.description:
Summary information about the member who submitted this report.

Provides context about the reporter including their username, display name, and account status. This helps moderators assess report credibility and identify patterns of abuse or misuse of the reporting system. The summary reference avoids circular dependencies while providing essential reporter context.

reportedArticle.description:
Summary information about the reported article, if the report targets an article.

Provides essential context about the flagged content including title, author, and publication date. This is null when the report targets a comment instead of an article. The summary reference enables moderators to quickly understand what content was reported without requiring separate API calls.

reportedComment.description:
Summary information about the reported comment, if the report targets a comment.

Provides essential context about the flagged comment including content preview, author, and parent article. This is null when the report targets an article instead of a comment. The summary reference enables moderators to quickly understand what content was reported without requiring separate API calls.

reviewingModerator.description:
Summary information about the moderator reviewing or who resolved this report.

Provides context about which moderator is handling the report, including their username and display name. This is null for pending reports that have not been claimed. The summary reference helps track moderation workload distribution and accountability for report handling decisions.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the report was submitted by the reporter.

Automatically recorded when a member flags content as potentially violating guidelines. This timestamp is immutable and used for calculating report age, prioritizing older reports, and tracking moderation response time metrics. Older unresolved reports may be highlighted in moderation dashboards to ensure timely review.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the report was last updated.

Automatically updated whenever the report status changes, a moderator is assigned, or resolution notes are added. This tracks the most recent activity on the report and helps moderators identify recently active reports versus stale ones. Used in moderation dashboards to sort and filter reports by activity.

deleted_at.description:
Soft delete timestamp for audit trail preservation.

When set, the report is hidden from active moderation queues but preserved in the system for historical records and audit purposes. This enables tracking of moderation patterns over time and supports compliance requirements for maintaining records of community safety actions. Null for all active reports.

IDiscussionBoardReport.description:
Complete content report entity with full details and relationships.

Represents a community member's report flagging an article or comment that potentially violates community guidelines. Reports are the primary mechanism for community-driven moderation, enabling members to alert moderators about problematic content for review. This type includes the complete report information including reporter identity, reported content reference (either article or comment), report reason and details, current review status, assigned moderator, and resolution outcome.

Reports support the progressive discipline and moderation workflow defined in the system requirements. Each report captures what content was flagged, why it was flagged, who flagged it, who reviewed it, and what decision was made. The polymorphic structure allows reports to target either articles or comments through mutually exclusive foreign keys.

The report status field tracks the report lifecycle: pending (newly submitted), under_review (moderator is examining), resolved (action was taken), or dismissed (no violation found). Resolution notes document moderator decisions for transparency and consistency. The relationship to moderation_actions links reports to specific enforcement actions taken, completing the audit trail for community safety operations.

reported_article_id.description:
Unique identifier of the article being reported if this report targets an article.

Must reference a valid article ID from the discussion_board_articles table. This field is mutually exclusive with reported_comment_id - exactly one must be provided to specify the target content. When reporting an article, this field must be populated with the article's UUID and reported_comment_id must be null or omitted.

reported_comment_id.description:
Unique identifier of the comment being reported if this report targets a comment.

Must reference a valid comment ID from the discussion_board_comments table. This field is mutually exclusive with reported_article_id - exactly one must be provided to specify the target content. When reporting a comment, this field must be populated with the comment's UUID and reported_article_id must be null or omitted.

report_reason.description:
Category of the community guideline violation being reported.

Must be one of the predefined violation categories: spam (spam or advertising content), harassment (harassment or bullying behavior), hate_speech (hate speech or discrimination), misinformation (misinformation or false information), off_topic (off-topic or irrelevant content), inappropriate_language (inappropriate language or profanity), personal_info (personal information disclosure), or other (requires explanation in report_details). This categorization helps moderators prioritize and route reports appropriately and supports violation pattern tracking.

report_details.description:
Optional detailed explanation of why the content violates community guidelines.

Provides additional context beyond the report_reason category to help moderators understand the specific violation. Maximum 500 characters as per business requirements. This field becomes required when report_reason is set to other to provide necessary explanation for custom violation types. When provided, helps moderators make more informed decisions about appropriate enforcement actions.

IDiscussionBoardReport.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new content report flagging potential community guideline violations.

This DTO enables authenticated members to submit reports identifying articles or comments that may violate community standards. The reporter must specify exactly one target (either an article or a comment through the mutually exclusive reported_article_id and reported_comment_id fields), select an appropriate violation category, and optionally provide detailed explanation to support the report. The authenticated member's identity is automatically captured from the JWT token and becomes the discussion_board_member_id, ensuring accountability in the reporting process.

The report creation DTO excludes all system-managed fields that are automatically populated: id (generated by system), discussion_board_member_id (from authentication context), reviewing_moderator_id (assigned later when moderator claims report), status (initialized to pending), resolution_notes (added by moderator during review), and all timestamps (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at managed by system). This design prevents clients from manipulating report metadata and ensures data integrity.

Validation rules enforce that exactly one of reported_article_id or reported_comment_id must be non-null, report_reason must be a valid violation category from the predefined list, and report_details is required when report_reason is other. The system verifies the reporter is authenticated, the target content exists and is accessible, and the member has not already reported this specific content before accepting the report submission.

reviewing_moderator_id.description:
Unique identifier of the moderator who is reviewing or has resolved this report.

When a moderator begins reviewing a report, they assign themselves by providing their moderator ID. This field can be updated as reports are reassigned between moderators. Setting this to null would unassign the report, returning it to the pending queue. This field is optional in the update payload, allowing moderators to update other aspects of the report without changing assignment.

oneOf.description:
Updated status reflecting the current state of the report in the moderation workflow.

Valid values: pending (not yet reviewed), under_review (moderator is actively examining the report), resolved (moderator took action on reported content), dismissed (moderator determined no violation occurred). Status transitions are typically sequential: pending → under_review → resolved/dismissed. Updating status to resolved or dismissed should include resolution_notes explaining the decision.

Valid values: pending (not yet reviewed), under_review (moderator is actively examining the report), resolved (moderator took action on reported content), dismissed (moderator determined no violation occurred). Status transitions are typically sequential: pending → under_review → resolved/dismissed. Updating status to resolved or dismissed should include resolution_notes explaining the decision.
