IDiscussionBoardUserSuspension.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering user account suspensions.

This DTO provides comprehensive query capabilities for moderators to find suspension records based on multiple criteria. The flexible filtering system supports various moderation workflows including reviewing a specific user's suspension history, auditing a moderator's enforcement actions, identifying currently active suspensions requiring oversight, finding suspensions by violation type, analyzing enforcement patterns over time ranges, and tracking upcoming suspension expirations.

All filter parameters are optional, allowing moderators to construct queries ranging from very broad (all suspensions) to highly specific (active suspensions issued by a specific moderator for harassment violations in the last 30 days). The search parameter enables text-based discovery across suspension reasons and details, while structured filters provide precise categorical filtering.

The pagination controls (page and limit) ensure efficient handling of large result sets, preventing performance issues when suspension history grows to thousands of records. The sorting options (order_by and order_direction) allow moderators to organize results based on their current task, whether reviewing recent enforcement actions, tracking expiring suspensions, or analyzing historical patterns.

This query interface is essential for moderation dashboard functionality, enabling moderators to efficiently navigate and manage the potentially large corpus of suspension records while maintaining system performance and usability.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this user suspension record.

This system-generated UUID serves as the primary key for the suspension entity, enabling precise referencing in moderation workflows, audit trails, and suspension management operations.

discussion_board_member_id.description:
Identifier of the member whose account has been suspended.

This foreign key references the discussion_board_members table, establishing which user is subject to this enforcement action. The suspension prevents this member from logging in and participating in the discussion board.

suspending_moderator_id.description:
Identifier of the moderator who issued this suspension.

This foreign key references the discussion_board_moderators table, providing accountability and traceability for the enforcement decision. This information is critical for audit trails and progressive discipline tracking.

lifted_by_moderator_id.description:
Identifier of the moderator who lifted this suspension early, if applicable.

This foreign key references the discussion_board_moderators table when a suspension is terminated before its scheduled expiration. Null for suspensions that expired naturally or are still active. This enables tracking of early termination decisions and accountability for administrative discretion.

related_moderation_action_id.description:
Identifier of the moderation action that resulted in this suspension, if applicable.

This foreign key references the discussion_board_moderation_actions table, linking the suspension to the broader moderation audit trail. When populated, it establishes a connection between the suspension enforcement and the formal moderation action record that documented the decision-making process, content review, and policy violation assessment.

This linkage is crucial for maintaining complete audit trails in the moderation system. It enables moderators to trace suspensions back to specific content violations or user behavior that triggered the enforcement, review the context and evidence that led to the suspension decision, and understand the progression from content report through moderation review to final suspension enforcement.

The field is nullable because suspensions can be issued through two pathways: in response to a formal moderation action (typically following content report review), where this field references that action record, or as independent enforcement decisions made during proactive moderation without a triggering report or formal action record, where this field remains null.

When conducting suspension reviews, appeals, or progressive discipline analysis, this field helps moderators access the full context of why the suspension was issued by providing a direct link to the documented moderation action with its detailed reasoning and evidence.

suspension_reason.description:
High-level category or classification of the violation that resulted in this suspension.

This field captures the type of policy violation (e.g., repeated harassment, severe spam, hate speech) that triggered the enforcement action. It provides a consistent categorization for reporting and progressive discipline tracking.

suspension_details.description:
Detailed explanation of why the suspension was issued and what specific violations occurred.

This comprehensive narrative describes the enforcement decision, including specific examples of violating behavior, references to community guidelines, and context that justifies the suspension duration. This information is shared with the suspended member and serves as documentation for appeals.

suspended_at.description:
Timestamp when the suspension began and the account was locked.

This marks the precise moment when the member's account access was revoked and they were prevented from logging in. All active sessions are terminated at this timestamp.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp when the suspension is scheduled to automatically end and account access will be restored.

For temporary suspensions, this defines the end of the enforcement period after which the system automatically reactivates the account. Null for permanent bans that have no scheduled expiration.

lifted_at.description:
Timestamp when the suspension was manually lifted early by a moderator.

This field is populated when a moderator uses the lift suspension operation to terminate the enforcement before the scheduled expires_at time. Null for suspensions that expired naturally or are still active.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this suspension record was created in the system.

Automatically set when the suspension is first issued, this provides a permanent record of when the enforcement action was entered into the database.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this suspension record was last modified.

Automatically updated whenever the suspension is modified (e.g., when lifted early), this enables tracking of changes to enforcement records.

suspendedUser.description:
Summary information about the member whose account is suspended.

Provides essential member details including username, display name, and profile information to identify who is subject to this enforcement action without requiring separate API calls.

suspendingModerator.description:
Summary information about the moderator who issued this suspension.

Provides moderator identification and profile details for accountability and audit trail purposes, showing who made the enforcement decision.

liftingModerator.description:
Summary information about the moderator who lifted this suspension early, if applicable.

Provides moderator identification when the suspension was terminated before expiration, enabling tracking of early termination decisions. Null for suspensions that expired naturally or are still active.

IDiscussionBoardUserSuspension.description:
Complete user suspension record including temporal information, responsible moderators, and associated member details.

This type represents a full account suspension entity as stored in the discussion_board_user_suspensions table, providing comprehensive information about enforcement actions that prevent members from accessing their accounts. Suspensions are a critical component of the progressive discipline system, representing more severe enforcement than warnings but potentially reversible unlike permanent bans.

The suspension record captures the complete enforcement lifecycle from initial issuance through potential early termination or natural expiration. It tracks both the moderator who issued the suspension and any moderator who lifted it early, maintaining full accountability for all enforcement decisions. The temporal fields (suspended_at, expires_at, lifted_at) define the suspension period and enable automated account reactivation when suspensions expire.

Suspension records serve multiple business purposes. They enforce access restrictions by preventing suspended members from logging in during the suspension period. They maintain audit trails by preserving complete enforcement history including who was suspended, why, by whom, and for how long. They support progressive discipline by tracking repeat offenses and escalating enforcement appropriately. They enable appeals and administrative discretion by allowing early termination when circumstances warrant.

The suspension workflow integrates with the authentication system to deny login attempts during active suspensions, displaying the suspension reason and expiration date to locked-out users. It connects to the moderation action logging system to record all suspension-related events for transparency and accountability. It coordinates with the member account status to ensure suspended members cannot access restricted features even if they somehow obtain valid session tokens.

This type includes summary references to related entities (suspended member and moderators) to provide complete context without requiring additional API calls, supporting efficient moderation dashboard displays and suspension management interfaces.

discussion_board_member_id.description:
Identifier of the member whose account will be suspended.

This field targets the specific user account that will be subject to the enforcement action. The member must exist in the discussion_board_members table and must not already have an active suspension.

related_moderation_action_id.description:
Optional identifier of the moderation action that resulted in this suspension.

When the suspension is created as part of a broader moderation workflow (such as report review), this links the suspension to the parent moderation action record for complete audit trail. Can be null for suspensions issued independently outside the standard report resolution process.

suspension_reason.description:
Category or type of violation that justifies this suspension.

This high-level classification should align with community guideline violation categories such as spam or advertising, harassment or bullying, hate speech or discrimination, misinformation or false information, off-topic or irrelevant content, inappropriate language or profanity, personal information disclosure, or repeated minor violations. Used for enforcement consistency and violation pattern analysis.

suspension_details.description:
Comprehensive explanation of why the suspension is being issued.

This field must contain detailed justification including the specific content or behavior that violated guidelines, references to relevant community standards or policies, consideration of the member's prior violation history and any previous warnings or suspensions, explanation of why the chosen suspension duration is appropriate, and any mitigating or aggravating factors considered in the decision. Essential for transparency, accountability, and processing potential appeals.

suspended_at.description:
Optional timestamp specifying when the suspension should begin.

When provided, this allows moderators to backdate suspensions or schedule suspension start times for specific moments. This flexibility is useful when a suspension decision is made after the violation occurred and moderators want to accurately reflect when the enforcement actually began, or when coordinating suspension timing with other administrative actions.

When null or omitted, the system automatically sets the suspension start time to the current timestamp at the moment the suspension record is created. This default behavior is appropriate for most suspension scenarios where enforcement begins immediately upon moderator decision.

If a future timestamp is provided, the suspension is scheduled to begin at that time, though account restrictions typically apply immediately to prevent further violations during the waiting period. If a past timestamp is provided (backdating), it accurately reflects historical enforcement timing for audit trail purposes while account restrictions apply immediately.

The suspended_at timestamp is critical for calculating suspension duration and determining when automatic account restoration should occur based on the expires_at value. It establishes the official start of the enforcement period for progressive discipline tracking and appeal timeline calculations.

expires_at.description:
Scheduled timestamp when the suspension will automatically end and account access will be restored.

For temporary suspensions, this defines the enforcement duration based on violation severity and progressive discipline guidelines. The system automatically reactivates the account when this timestamp is reached. Set to null for permanent bans where no automatic restoration is intended. Must be a future timestamp when provided.

IDiscussionBoardUserSuspension.ICreate.description:
Request data for creating a new user account suspension as part of community guideline enforcement.

This structure contains all information necessary for a moderator to suspend a member's account, implementing the progressive discipline framework defined in the moderation requirements. The suspension creation request must identify the target member, provide clear categorization and detailed justification for the enforcement action, and specify the suspension duration.

The suspension reason should align with predefined violation categories to maintain enforcement consistency across the platform. The suspension details field requires comprehensive documentation including what guidelines were violated, relevant context and history, and rationale for the chosen duration, supporting both transparency and potential appeal processes.

The expiration timestamp enables temporary suspensions that automatically restore access after a specified period, while null values create permanent bans. This flexibility supports the progressive discipline approach where enforcement severity escalates based on violation patterns and severity.

The optional suspended_at timestamp allows moderators to specify exactly when the suspension should begin, supporting backdating for accurate historical records or scheduling suspension start times. When omitted, the suspension begins immediately at the current system time.

Fields excluded from this request type include the suspending moderator ID which is automatically captured from the authenticated moderator's JWT token ensuring accountability, the lifted_by_moderator_id which is only populated if the suspension is later lifted early, the lifted_at timestamp which is set only when early termination occurs, and system timestamps created_at and updated_at which are automatically managed. These exclusions follow security best practices where actor identity comes from verified authentication rather than client input.

lifting_reason.description:
Optional explanation for why this suspension is being lifted early.

Moderators can provide context such as "Appeal granted due to evidence of error in original enforcement," "User demonstrated understanding and reform," "Suspension determined to be disproportionate to violation," or "Administrative decision to reduce enforcement duration." While optional, providing a lifting reason improves transparency and helps maintain consistent moderation standards across the team.

IDiscussionBoardUserSuspension.ILift.description:
Request body for lifting an active user suspension early to restore account access.

This type represents the data required when a moderator decides to terminate a suspension before its scheduled expiration date. The operation enables administrative flexibility in the enforcement system, allowing moderators to respond to appeals, correct errors, or adjust enforcement based on changed circumstances.

The lifting operation is a key component of the moderation system's progressive discipline framework. While suspensions are issued with defined durations (expires_at timestamps), moderators retain discretion to end suspensions early when appropriate. Common scenarios include successful appeals where the suspended member provides compelling evidence that the original enforcement was inappropriate, recognition that the suspension duration was too harsh relative to the actual violation, demonstrations of genuine understanding and reform by the suspended member, or administrative decisions by the moderation team to reduce enforcement for policy consistency.

When a suspension is lifted, the system immediately restores the member's account access, allowing them to log in and resume participation. The original suspension record is preserved with the lifted_at timestamp and lifting moderator information, maintaining a complete audit trail of the enforcement lifecycle. This supports transparency and enables analysis of moderation patterns over time.

The lifting_reason field, while optional, is strongly encouraged to maintain moderation quality and team coordination. Documented reasons help other moderators understand the decision-making process, support consistent enforcement standards, and provide context for future similar cases. Reasons also protect moderators by documenting their rationale if enforcement decisions are later questioned.

Security and authorization requirements mandate that only authenticated moderators can submit suspension lift requests. The system validates that the target suspension exists, is currently active (not already expired or lifted), and that the requesting moderator has appropriate permissions. The authenticated moderator's identity is automatically captured from the JWT token and recorded as the lifting_moderator_id, ensuring accountability without requiring clients to specify who they are.

pending_reports.description:
List of pending content reports awaiting moderator review.

This array contains all reports with status 'pending' that have not yet been assigned to a moderator or begun review. Reports are ordered by priority, with multiply-reported content and urgent reports appearing first to help moderators address the most critical issues immediately.

under_review_reports.description:
List of reports currently being reviewed by moderators.

This array contains reports with status 'under_review', showing which content is actively being evaluated by moderators. Each report indicates which moderator is handling it, enabling team coordination and preventing duplicate review efforts.

recent_moderation_actions.description:
Recent moderation actions taken by all moderators in the past 24 hours.

This array provides a chronological activity log of recent enforcement decisions, content edits, deletions, warnings, and suspensions. It enables moderators to see what actions their teammates have taken, promoting consistency and coordination in enforcement standards.

active_suspensions.description:
Currently active user account suspensions.

This array contains all suspensions where suspended_at is in the past, expires_at is in the future (or null for permanent bans), and lifted_at is null. It shows which members are currently prevented from accessing their accounts, helping moderators track enforcement actions and upcoming expirations.

statistics.description:
Aggregated moderation system statistics and metrics.

Provides quantitative overview of moderation workload, trends, and system health including counts of pending reports, resolved reports, active suspensions, recent warnings, and other key performance indicators for the moderation system.

IDiscussionBoardModerationDashboardOverv.description:
Comprehensive moderation dashboard overview consolidating all critical moderation information.

This type provides moderators with a complete situational awareness snapshot, aggregating data from multiple tables to enable efficient moderation workflows. The dashboard overview serves as the primary entry point for moderators, presenting pending work, ongoing reviews, recent team activity, and system health metrics in a single unified response.

The overview is designed to answer the moderator's key questions at a glance: What needs my immediate attention (pending reports)? What are my teammates working on (under review reports)? What enforcement actions have been taken recently (recent moderation actions)? Which members are currently suspended (active suspensions)? How is the moderation system performing overall (statistics)?

By consolidating this information from discussion_board_reports, discussion_board_moderation_actions, and discussion_board_user_suspensions tables, the dashboard enables single-call atomic information retrieval. Moderators can load the dashboard and immediately understand the current moderation state without making multiple sequential API calls for reports, actions, and suspensions separately. This atomic operation design reduces latency, simplifies client logic, and improves moderator productivity.

The dashboard overview supports critical moderation workflows including daily moderation queue review where moderators check pending reports and prioritize review work, team coordination where moderators see what colleagues are handling to avoid duplicate effort, enforcement oversight where moderators monitor suspension expirations and enforcement patterns, and workload assessment where moderation team leads evaluate whether current moderator capacity is adequate.

Each array in the overview is intentionally limited to recent or urgent items to maintain fast response times. Pending reports show the most urgent issues requiring immediate review, not the complete historical report archive. Recent moderation actions cover the past 24 hours, not all historical actions. Active suspensions show only current enforcement, not expired historical suspensions. This scoping ensures the dashboard loads quickly even as the moderation data grows over time.

The statistics object provides quantitative metrics that complement the qualitative report and action lists, giving moderators both detailed work items and high-level system health indicators in a single comprehensive response.

pending_reports_count.description:
Total number of reports with status 'pending' awaiting moderator review.

This count helps moderators understand current workload and prioritize their time. High pending counts may indicate need for additional moderator resources or review of automation opportunities.

under_review_reports_count.description:
Total number of reports currently being reviewed by moderators.

Indicates reports with status 'under_review', showing active moderation work in progress across the team. Helps identify whether reports are being processed or if review capacity is saturated.

resolved_reports_count_24h.description:
Number of reports resolved in the past 24 hours.

Counts reports with status 'resolved' or 'dismissed' that were updated in the last day. Measures moderator productivity and report processing velocity.

active_suspensions_count.description:
Number of user suspensions currently in effect.

Counts suspensions where suspended_at is in the past, expires_at is in the future or null, and lifted_at is null. Indicates current enforcement load and community health.

warnings_issued_count_7d.description:
Number of user warnings issued in the past 7 days.

Counts warning records from discussion_board_user_warnings created within the last week. Provides insight into early-stage enforcement activity and potential escalation patterns.

total_moderation_actions_count_24h.description:
Total number of moderation actions taken in the past 24 hours.

Counts all entries in discussion_board_moderation_actions created in the last day, regardless of action type. Provides overall moderation activity metric.

urgent_reports_count.description:
Number of reports flagged as urgent based on multiple user reports.

Counts pending reports where the same content has been reported by 5 or more members, indicating high-priority issues requiring immediate moderator attention.

average_report_resolution_time_hours.description:
Average time in hours between report submission and resolution for reports resolved in the past 7 days.

Calculates mean duration from created_at to updated_at for reports that changed to 'resolved' or 'dismissed' status in the past week. Null if no reports were resolved in the measurement period. This metric measures moderator responsiveness and helps identify processing bottlenecks.

IDiscussionBoardModerationDashboardStati.description:
Aggregated quantitative metrics for moderation system health and workload assessment.

This type provides statistical insights into the moderation system's current state and recent performance, enabling moderators and administrators to assess workload, identify trends, and make data-driven decisions about moderation resource allocation. The statistics complement the qualitative information in the dashboard overview's report and action lists, giving moderators both detailed work items and high-level system health indicators.

The statistics serve multiple analytical purposes. Workload assessment helps moderators understand current queue depth and whether pending work is manageable or requires additional moderator shifts. Trend identification reveals patterns such as increasing report volumes, seasonal variations in violations, or effectiveness of recent policy changes. Resource planning supports decisions about moderator hiring or scheduling based on sustained high report volumes. Performance tracking measures how quickly the team resolves reports and whether response times meet the target of 12 hours average resolution.

Time-based metrics use specific windows to balance recency with statistical validity. The 24-hour window for resolved reports and total actions captures very recent activity while smoothing short-term fluctuations. The 7-day window for warnings and resolution time average provides broader trend visibility while remaining actionable. Urgent report counts are real-time to enable immediate response to critical situations.

The statistics integrate data from multiple tables to provide comprehensive moderation metrics. Report counts query the discussion_board_reports table with status and timestamp filters. Suspension counts query discussion_board_user_suspensions with temporal logic to identify currently active enforcement. Warning counts query discussion_board_user_warnings with date range filters. Moderation action counts query the discussion_board_moderation_actions audit log.

These metrics support the moderation effectiveness measurement requirements defined in the system specifications, where report resolution time should average less than 12 hours and pending queues should be cleared at least once daily. By exposing these metrics in the dashboard, moderators and administrators can monitor whether the moderation system is meeting its service level objectives.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.description:
Comprehensive statistical analysis of moderation activity and system health metrics for the discussion board.

This schema provides moderators with detailed analytics that aggregate data from multiple moderation-related tables to deliver actionable insights about moderation patterns, enforcement effectiveness, and community health. The statistics enable data-driven decision-making about policy enforcement and resource allocation by revealing trends, workload distribution, and violation patterns over time.

The statistics include multiple analytical dimensions that help moderators understand the complete picture of moderation activity. Time-series data reveals how report volumes and moderation actions have evolved, enabling early detection of emerging issues or seasonal patterns. Violation type breakdowns categorize enforcement activity by guideline violation types, helping identify which policy areas require the most attention and may benefit from clearer guidelines or increased enforcement focus.

overview.description:
High-level summary metrics providing at-a-glance system health indicators.

Includes total counts of pending reports, reports resolved in the past 24 hours, active user suspensions, and warnings issued in the past week. These metrics give moderators immediate visibility into current workload and recent enforcement activity.

reportMetrics.description:
Detailed analytics about content reports submitted by the community.

Provides insights into report volume trends, average resolution times, report accuracy rates, and breakdown by violation categories. Helps moderators understand how effectively the community is identifying policy violations and how efficiently the moderation team is responding to reports.

moderationActionMetrics.description:
Analytics about moderation actions taken by the moderation team.

Includes distribution of action types such as content edits, deletions, warnings, and suspensions over various time periods. Shows trends in enforcement activity and helps identify whether moderation is becoming more or less active over time.

moderatorWorkload.description:
Workload distribution across the moderation team.

Shows how moderation work is distributed among moderators including reports reviewed per moderator, average review time, and actions taken. Helps identify workload balance issues and recognize particularly active team members.

userBehaviorMetrics.description:
Analytics about user behavior patterns and enforcement effectiveness.

Tracks repeat violation rates, time between violations for users with multiple infractions, and effectiveness of progressive discipline in reducing problematic behavior. Measures whether warnings and suspensions successfully deter future violations.

contentHealthMetrics.description:
Overall community and content quality indicators.

Includes ratio of reported content to total content, percentage of content requiring moderation intervention, and trends in content quality over time. Helps assess overall community health and whether quality is improving or degrading.

temporalTrends.description:
Time-series data showing how moderation metrics have changed over different time periods.

Provides hourly, daily, weekly, and monthly trend data for key metrics including report volumes, resolution rates, and action types. Enables identification of patterns, peak periods, and emerging issues requiring attention.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IOv.description:
High-level summary metrics providing at-a-glance moderation system health indicators.

This overview section delivers the most critical metrics that moderators need to understand current system state immediately. The metrics are derived from real-time queries against discussion_board_reports, discussion_board_moderation_actions, discussion_board_user_warnings, and discussion_board_user_suspensions tables to provide up-to-date counts and recent activity summaries.

pendingReportsCount.description:
Total number of reports currently awaiting moderator review.

Calculated by counting records in discussion_board_reports where status equals pending. This metric indicates current workload and urgency for moderation team action.

underReviewReportsCount.description:
Number of reports currently under active review by moderators.

Counted from discussion_board_reports where status equals under_review. Helps track how many reports are being actively worked on versus sitting in the queue.

resolvedReportsLast24Hours.description:
Number of reports resolved in the past 24 hours.

Calculated by counting discussion_board_reports where status equals resolved or dismissed and updated_at is within the last 24 hours. Measures recent moderation team productivity and responsiveness.

activeSuspensionsCount.description:
Number of user accounts currently under active suspension.

Counted from discussion_board_user_suspensions where expires_at is in the future or null for permanent bans and lifted_at is null. Indicates current enforcement level and number of restricted accounts.

warningsIssuedLastWeek.description:
Total number of warnings issued to users in the past 7 days.

Calculated by counting discussion_board_user_warnings where created_at is within the last 7 days. Shows recent enforcement activity at the warning level of progressive discipline.

averageReportResolutionTimeHours.description:
Average time in hours from report submission to resolution.

Calculated by averaging the difference between created_at and updated_at timestamps for resolved/dismissed reports in the past 30 days. Key performance indicator for moderation team responsiveness.

reportAccuracyPercentage.description:
Percentage of submitted reports that resulted in moderation action rather than dismissal.

Calculated by dividing reports with resolution leading to action by total resolved reports in the past 30 days, multiplied by 100. Indicates how well the community understands and applies reporting guidelines.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IRe.description:
Detailed analytics about content reports submitted by community members.

This section provides comprehensive metrics about the reporting system's usage and effectiveness. Data is derived from the discussion_board_reports table with calculations including temporal aggregations, violation category distributions, and outcome analysis. These metrics help moderators understand reporting patterns, identify high-priority violation types, and measure how effectively the community uses the reporting mechanism.

totalReportsAllTime.description:
Total cumulative number of reports submitted since system inception.

Counted from all records in discussion_board_reports regardless of status. Provides historical context for moderation activity volume.

reportsLast24Hours.description:
Number of new reports submitted in the past 24 hours.

Counted from discussion_board_reports where created_at is within the last 24 hours. Indicates current report volume and immediate workload.

reportsLastWeek.description:
Number of new reports submitted in the past 7 days.

Counted from discussion_board_reports where created_at is within the last 7 days. Shows weekly reporting activity trends.

reportsLastMonth.description:
Number of new reports submitted in the past 30 days.

Counted from discussion_board_reports where created_at is within the last 30 days. Provides monthly reporting volume for trend analysis.

averageResolutionTimeHours.description:
Average time in hours from report submission to moderator resolution.

Calculated by averaging the difference between created_at and updated_at for reports with status resolved or dismissed in the past 30 days. Key performance indicator for moderation responsiveness.

reportsByViolationType.description:
Breakdown of reports by violation category showing which types of guideline violations are most commonly reported.

Each entry aggregates discussion_board_reports by report_reason field, providing counts and percentages for categories like spam, harassment, misinformation, hate speech, and off-topic content. Helps identify which policy areas see the most enforcement activity.

reportsByStatus.description:
Distribution of reports across different status values showing pipeline state.

Aggregates discussion_board_reports by status field to show how many reports are pending, under_review, resolved, or dismissed. Helps moderators understand report queue health and processing velocity.

reportAccuracyRate.description:
Percentage of reports that resulted in moderation action versus those dismissed as invalid.

Calculated by dividing reports with status resolved that led to moderation actions by total resolved/dismissed reports, multiplied by 100. Indicates community's understanding of guidelines and reporting appropriateness.

multipleReportedContentCount.description:
Number of distinct articles or comments that have been reported multiple times by different users.

Calculated by counting distinct combinations of reported_article_id or reported_comment_id in discussion_board_reports where the same content has more than one report. High-priority items requiring immediate attention.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IVi.description:
Count and percentage breakdown for a specific violation category in the reporting system.

Represents aggregated data from discussion_board_reports grouped by report_reason field. Each instance shows how many reports fall into a particular violation category and what percentage of total reports that represents, enabling moderators to identify the most common policy violation types.

violationType.description:
Category of guideline violation reported.

Derived from the report_reason field in discussion_board_reports. Common values include spam-or-advertising, harassment-or-bullying, hate-speech-or-discrimination, misinformation-or-false-information, off-topic-or-irrelevant, inappropriate-language, personal-information-disclosure, and other.

count.description:
Total number of reports submitted for this violation type.

Counted from discussion_board_reports where report_reason matches this violation type. Shows absolute volume of reports in this category.

percentage.description:
Percentage of total reports that fall into this violation category.

Calculated by dividing count by total reports and multiplying by 100. Helps identify which violation types dominate moderation workload.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IRe.description:
Distribution of reports across different status states in the moderation pipeline.

Aggregates discussion_board_reports by status field to show the current state of the report queue. Provides visibility into how many reports are awaiting review, actively being reviewed, or already resolved, helping moderators understand processing velocity and queue health.

pending.description:
Number of reports with status pending awaiting initial moderator review.

Counted from discussion_board_reports where status equals pending. Represents current backlog requiring attention.

underReview.description:
Number of reports with status under_review currently being examined by moderators.

Counted from discussion_board_reports where status equals under_review. Shows active work in progress.

resolved.description:
Number of reports with status resolved where moderation action was taken.

Counted from discussion_board_reports where status equals resolved. Indicates reports that led to content edits, deletions, or user enforcement.

dismissed.description:
Number of reports with status dismissed where no violation was found.

Counted from discussion_board_reports where status equals dismissed. Shows reports that were reviewed but did not result in enforcement action.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IMo.description:
Analytics about moderation actions taken by the moderation team.

Aggregates data from discussion_board_moderation_actions table to show the distribution and frequency of different enforcement actions. Provides insight into what types of interventions moderators are performing and how enforcement patterns change over time.

totalActionsAllTime.description:
Total cumulative number of moderation actions taken since system inception.

Counted from all records in discussion_board_moderation_actions. Provides historical context for enforcement activity volume.

actionsLast24Hours.description:
Number of moderation actions taken in the past 24 hours.

Counted from discussion_board_moderation_actions where created_at is within the last 24 hours. Shows current enforcement activity level.

actionsLastWeek.description:
Number of moderation actions taken in the past 7 days.

Counted from discussion_board_moderation_actions where created_at is within the last 7 days. Indicates weekly enforcement volume.

actionsLastMonth.description:
Number of moderation actions taken in the past 30 days.

Counted from discussion_board_moderation_actions where created_at is within the last 30 days. Provides monthly enforcement trend data.

actionsByType.description:
Breakdown of moderation actions by action type showing which interventions are most common.

Each entry aggregates discussion_board_moderation_actions by action_type field, providing counts and percentages for categories like edit_content, delete_content, warn_user, suspend_user, and dismiss_report.

actionsByTargetType.description:
Distribution of moderation actions by target entity type.

Aggregates discussion_board_moderation_actions by target_type field to show whether actions primarily target articles, comments, users, or reports. Reveals which content types require the most moderation.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IAc.description:
Count and percentage breakdown for a specific moderation action type.

Represents aggregated data from discussion_board_moderation_actions grouped by action_type field. Shows how frequently each type of moderation intervention is performed.

actionType.description:
Type of moderation action performed.

Derived from action_type field in discussion_board_moderation_actions. Values include edit_content for content modifications, delete_content for content removal, restore_content for reversing deletions, warn_user for issuing warnings, suspend_user for account suspensions, ban_user for permanent bans, lift_suspension for early suspension termination, and dismiss_report for closing reports without action.

count.description:
Total number of times this action type was performed.

Counted from discussion_board_moderation_actions where action_type matches this type. Shows absolute volume for this intervention type.

percentage.description:
Percentage of total moderation actions that are of this type.

Calculated by dividing count by total actions and multiplying by 100. Reveals which enforcement actions dominate moderation work.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.ITa.description:
Count and percentage breakdown for moderation actions by targeted entity type.

Aggregates discussion_board_moderation_actions by target_type field to show whether enforcement actions primarily target articles, comments, users, or reports. Helps identify which content types require the most moderation attention.

targetType.description:
Type of entity that was the target of moderation action.

Derived from target_type field in discussion_board_moderation_actions. Values include article for actions on discussion_board_articles, comment for actions on discussion_board_comments, user for actions on discussion_board_members, and report for actions on discussion_board_reports themselves.

count.description:
Total number of moderation actions targeting this entity type.

Counted from discussion_board_moderation_actions where target_type matches this type. Shows absolute intervention volume per entity type.

percentage.description:
Percentage of total moderation actions that target this entity type.

Calculated by dividing count by total actions and multiplying by 100. Reveals which content types consume the most moderation resources.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IMo.description:
Workload distribution across the moderation team showing individual moderator activity and efficiency.

Aggregates data from discussion_board_reports and discussion_board_moderation_actions joined with discussion_board_moderators to analyze how moderation work is distributed. Helps identify workload imbalances, recognize high performers, and ensure fair distribution of moderation responsibilities.

totalActiveModerators.description:
Number of moderators who have taken at least one moderation action in the past 30 days.

Calculated by counting distinct discussion_board_moderator_id values in discussion_board_moderation_actions where created_at is within the last 30 days. Shows active moderation team size.

averageReportsPerModerator.description:
Average number of reports reviewed per active moderator in the past 30 days.

Calculated by dividing total resolved/dismissed reports in the past 30 days by totalActiveModerators. Indicates typical individual workload.

averageActionsPerModerator.description:
Average number of moderation actions taken per active moderator in the past 30 days.

Calculated by dividing total moderation actions in the past 30 days by totalActiveModerators. Measures average enforcement activity per team member.

moderatorActivity.description:
Individual activity metrics for each active moderator.

Array of per-moderator statistics showing reports reviewed, actions taken, and average review time for each team member. Enables workload comparison and identification of particularly active or effective moderators.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IMo.description:
Activity metrics for an individual moderator showing their contribution to moderation work.

Derived by joining discussion_board_moderation_actions and discussion_board_reports with discussion_board_moderators and aggregating per moderator. Shows individual performance and workload for team management and recognition purposes.

moderator.description:
Summary information about the moderator whose activity is being reported.

Provides moderator identification and basic profile data for context.

reportsReviewed.description:
Number of reports this moderator has reviewed and resolved in the past 30 days.

Counted from discussion_board_reports where reviewing_moderator_id matches this moderator and status is resolved or dismissed and updated_at is within the past 30 days.

actionsTaken.description:
Total number of moderation actions performed by this moderator in the past 30 days.

Counted from discussion_board_moderation_actions where discussion_board_moderator_id matches this moderator and created_at is within the past 30 days.

averageReviewTimeHours.description:
Average time in hours this moderator takes to review and resolve reports.

Calculated by averaging the difference between created_at and updated_at for reports resolved by this moderator in the past 30 days. Indicates moderator efficiency.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IUs.description:
Analytics about user behavior patterns and the effectiveness of enforcement measures.

Aggregates data from discussion_board_user_warnings and discussion_board_user_suspensions to measure whether progressive discipline successfully deters repeat violations. Tracks patterns in user violations to assess policy enforcement effectiveness and identify users who may require additional intervention.

totalUsersWarned.description:
Number of distinct users who have received at least one warning.

Calculated by counting distinct discussion_board_member_id values in discussion_board_user_warnings where deleted_at is null.

totalUsersSuspended.description:
Number of distinct users who have been suspended at least once.

Calculated by counting distinct discussion_board_member_id values in discussion_board_user_suspensions.

repeatOffendersCount.description:
Number of users who have received multiple warnings or suspensions.

Calculated by counting users with more than one record in discussion_board_user_warnings or discussion_board_user_suspensions. Indicates users with persistent problematic behavior.

repeatOffenderRate.description:
Percentage of warned or suspended users who commit subsequent violations.

Calculated by dividing repeatOffendersCount by total distinct users with any warnings or suspensions, multiplied by 100. Measures effectiveness of progressive discipline.

averageDaysBetweenViolations.description:
Average number of days between violations for users with multiple infractions.

Calculated by analyzing created_at timestamps in discussion_board_user_warnings and discussion_board_user_suspensions for users with multiple records. Indicates how quickly problematic users repeat violations.

warningToBanConversionRate.description:
Percentage of warned users who eventually receive permanent bans.

Calculated by counting users who appear in discussion_board_user_warnings and later in discussion_board_user_suspensions with expires_at null indicating permanent ban, divided by total warned users, multiplied by 100. Measures escalation frequency in progressive discipline.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.ICo.description:
Overall community and content quality indicators derived from moderation data.

Calculates ratios and percentages that measure the health of the discussion board community. Low moderation intervention rates indicate healthy community norms, while high rates may suggest policy clarity issues or community culture problems. These metrics help assess whether community quality is improving or degrading over time.

totalArticlesCount.description:
Total number of published articles in the system.

Counted from discussion_board_articles where deleted_at is null and status equals published. Provides denominator for ratio calculations.

totalCommentsCount.description:
Total number of non-deleted comments in the system.

Counted from discussion_board_comments where deleted_at is null. Provides denominator for comment-related metrics.

reportedArticlesPercentage.description:
Percentage of published articles that have been reported at least once.

Calculated by counting distinct reported_article_id values in discussion_board_reports, dividing by totalArticlesCount, and multiplying by 100. High percentages may indicate quality issues or unclear guidelines.

reportedCommentsPercentage.description:
Percentage of comments that have been reported at least once.

Calculated by counting distinct reported_comment_id values in discussion_board_reports, dividing by totalCommentsCount, and multiplying by 100. Measures comment quality and appropriateness.

moderationInterventionRate.description:
Percentage of total content (articles plus comments) that has required moderator intervention.

Calculated by counting content items targeted by discussion_board_moderation_actions with action_type edit_content or delete_content, dividing by sum of totalArticlesCount and totalCommentsCount, and multiplying by 100. Lower rates indicate healthier community norms.

deletedContentPercentage.description:
Percentage of all content that has been deleted by moderators.

Calculated by counting articles and comments where deleted_at is not null, dividing by total content items ever created, and multiplying by 100. High percentages may indicate systemic quality issues.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.ITe.description:
Time-series data showing how key moderation metrics have changed over different time periods.

Provides trend analysis by aggregating moderation data across hourly, daily, weekly, and monthly time buckets. Enables moderators to identify patterns such as peak reporting times, increasing or decreasing violation rates, and seasonal trends in community behavior. Temporal trends help predict future workload and identify emerging issues early.

hourlyReportsLast24Hours.description:
Hour-by-hour report submission counts for the past 24 hours.

Array contains 24 entries, one per hour, showing how many reports were submitted in each hour. Derived by grouping discussion_board_reports by hour of created_at timestamp for the past 24 hours. Helps identify peak reporting times and intraday patterns.

dailyReportsLastWeek.description:
Day-by-day report submission counts for the past 7 days.

Array contains 7 entries, one per day, showing report volume per day. Derived by grouping discussion_board_reports by date of created_at for the past 7 days. Reveals daily patterns and day-of-week effects.

weeklyReportsLastMonth.description:
Week-by-week report submission counts for the past 30 days.

Array contains approximately 4 entries, one per week, showing report volume per week. Derived by grouping discussion_board_reports by week for the past month. Shows weekly trends and patterns.

dailyActionsLastWeek.description:
Day-by-day moderation action counts for the past 7 days.

Array contains 7 entries showing how many moderation actions were taken each day. Derived by grouping discussion_board_moderation_actions by date of created_at. Tracks enforcement activity over time.

monthlyActionsLastYear.description:
Month-by-month moderation action counts for the past 12 months.

Array contains 12 entries showing monthly enforcement activity. Derived by grouping discussion_board_moderation_actions by month of created_at for the past year. Reveals long-term trends and seasonal patterns.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IHo.description:
Data point representing metrics for a single hour in time-series analysis.

Used in hourly trend data to show how moderation metrics vary throughout the day. Helps identify peak activity hours and intraday patterns that can inform moderator scheduling and resource allocation.

hour.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp representing the start of this hour.

Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00:00Z. Identifies the specific hour this data point represents in UTC timezone.

count.description:
Count of events (reports or actions) that occurred during this hour.

Derived by counting records in the source table where created_at falls within this hour.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IDa.description:
Data point representing metrics for a single day in time-series analysis.

Used in daily trend data to show how moderation metrics vary day-to-day. Reveals daily patterns, day-of-week effects, and short-term trends in reporting and enforcement activity.

date.description:
ISO 8601 date representing this data point.

Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Identifies the specific day this data represents.

count.description:
Count of events (reports or actions) that occurred on this date.

Derived by counting records in the source table where created_at date matches this date.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IWe.description:
Data point representing metrics for a single week in time-series analysis.

Used in weekly trend data to show how moderation metrics vary week-to-week. Helps identify weekly patterns and medium-term trends in community behavior and moderation workload.

weekStartDate.description:
ISO 8601 date representing the start of this week (typically Monday).

Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Identifies the beginning of the week this data represents.

count.description:
Count of events (reports or actions) that occurred during this week.

Derived by counting records in the source table where created_at falls within this week period.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics.IMo.description:
Data point representing metrics for a single month in time-series analysis.

Used in monthly trend data to show how moderation metrics vary month-to-month. Reveals long-term trends, seasonal patterns, and overall growth or improvement in community health over extended periods.

month.description:
ISO 8601 date representing the first day of this month.

Format: YYYY-MM-01. Identifies the month this data represents.

count.description:
Count of events (reports or actions) that occurred during this month.

Derived by counting records in the source table where created_at falls within this month.
